knowledge_statements.statement_title: LMI Variable-Elimination Lemma
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Eliminates an independent auxiliary matrix variable that enters a strict affine matrix inequality linearly, using two nullspace projections.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A:\mathbb R^q\to\mathbb S^n\) be affine, \(C\in\mathbb R^{n\times p}\), and \(B\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\). Let the rows of \(C_\perp\) form a basis of \(\mathcal N(C^\top)\), and let the columns of \(B_\perp\) form a basis of \(\mathcal N(B)\). Then \[\exists x\in\mathbb R^q,\ Y\in\mathbb R^{p\times m}:\ A(x)+CYB+B^\top Y^\top C^\top\succ0\] if and only if \[\exists x\in\mathbb R^q:\ C_\perp A(x)C_\perp^\top\succ0\quad\text{and}\quad B_\perp^\top A(x)B_\perp\succ0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strict LMI containing an independent auxiliary matrix variable is feasible exactly when the same choice of x makes both relevant nullspace projections of A(x) positive definite.
assumptions_latex: C\in\mathbb R^{n\times p},\quad B\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists x,Y:\ A(x)+CYB+B^\top Y^\top C^\top\succ0\iff\exists x:\ C_\perp A(x)C_\perp^\top\succ0\ \land\ B_\perp^\top A(x)B_\perp\succ0.

children.title: Spectrahedral Projection
children.top_down_role: Projected descriptions of spectrahedra in retained coordinates.

assumptions_latex: \(L(x,y)\in\mathbb S^m\) is an affine symmetric pencil.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\pi_x\{(x,y):L(x,y)\succeq0\}=\{x:\exists y,L(x,y)\succeq0\}\) is a spectrahedral shadow.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition of a finite-dimensional spectrahedral shadow by coordinate projection.

source_refs.locator: 6 Semidefinite Representability p. 251
source_refs.source_title: Semidefinite Optimization and Convex Algebraic Geometry

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
S=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^p:L(x,y)\succeq0\}
\]
be a spectrahedron defined by an affine symmetric pencil. Its projection onto the retained coordinates is
\[
\pi_x(S)=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:\exists y\in\mathbb R^p, L(x,y)\succeq0\}.
\]
Any set admitting such a representation is called a spectrahedral shadow, or equivalently a semidefinite-representable set. When \(p=0\), the representation is direct and the set is a spectrahedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A spectrahedral projection is the set of retained coordinates admitting auxiliary values that satisfy a lifted affine LMI.
knowledge_statements.title: Spectrahedral Projection

children.title: Matrix-Elimination Principles
children.top_down_role: Matrix-structured elimination mechanisms used in LMI equivalence.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\begin{pmatrix}A&B\\B^{\mathsf T}&C\end{pmatrix}\succeq0\iff A-BC^{-1}B^{\mathsf T}\succeq0\).

notation.meaning: Symmetric block matrix to be reduced.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-definite-pivot Schur-complement form of block matrix elimination.

source_refs.locator: 2.3.7 Convex matrix functions p. 26

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
M=\begin{pmatrix}A&B\\B^{\mathsf T}&C\end{pmatrix},
\]
where \(A\in\mathbb S^p\), \(C\in\mathbb S^q\), \(B\in\mathbb R^{p\times q}\), and \(C\succ0\). Then
\[
M\succeq0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
A-BC^{-1}B^{\mathsf T}\succeq0.
\]
Thus the block associated with \(C\) can be eliminated exactly, yielding the Schur-complement inequality. The strict assumption \(C\succ0\) ensures that \(C^{-1}\) exists; singular pivots require a generalized-inverse condition together with a range constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With a positive definite pivot block, a block PSD constraint is exactly equivalent to positivity of its Schur complement.
knowledge_statements.title: Matrix-Elimination Principles

source_witnesses.locator: 2.3.7 Convex matrix functions p. 26

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Norm-Bounded Robust LMI Equivalence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Eliminates universally quantified operator-norm-bounded matrix uncertainty through an equivalent scalar-multiplier block LMI.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A(x)\in\mathbb S^n\) depend affinely on \(x\), with \(B\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) and \(C\in\mathbb R^{n\times p}\). Then \[A(x)+CYB+B^\top Y^\top C^\top\succeq0\quad\text{for every }Y\in\mathbb R^{p\times m}\text{ satisfying }\|Y\|_2\le1\] if and only if there exists \(\lambda\in\mathbb R\) such that \[\begin{bmatrix}A(x)-\lambda CC^\top&B^\top\\B&\lambda I_m\end{bmatrix}\succeq0.\] Equivalently, the robust inequality holds if and only if there exists \(\lambda\in\mathbb R\) such that \[\begin{bmatrix}A(x)-\lambda B^\top B&C\\C^\top&\lambda I_p\end{bmatrix}\succeq0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An affine matrix inequality holds for every operator-norm-bounded matrix perturbation exactly when either equivalent scalar-multiplier block LMI is feasible.
assumptions_latex: B\in\mathbb R^{m\times n},\quad C\in\mathbb R^{n\times p}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall Y\,\bigl(\|Y\|_2\le1\Rightarrow A(x)+CYB+B^\top Y^\top C^\top\succeq0\bigr)\iff\exists\lambda\in\mathbb R:\begin{bmatrix}A(x)-\lambda CC^\top&B^\top\\B&\lambda I_m\end{bmatrix}\succeq0,\text{ equivalently }\exists\lambda\in\mathbb R:\begin{bmatrix}A(x)-\lambda B^\top B&C\\C^\top&\lambda I_p\end{bmatrix}\succeq0.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
S=\left\{(x,y)\in\mathbb R^2:
\begin{pmatrix}x&1\\1&y\end{pmatrix}\succeq0\right\},
\]
and let \(\pi_x\) denote projection onto the first coordinate. Then \(S\) is a closed spectrahedron and
\[
\pi_x(S)=(0,\infty).
\]
Thus a spectrahedral projection need not be closed and need not admit a direct spectrahedral representation, even though it remains semidefinite representable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: This closed two-dimensional spectrahedron projects onto the open ray (0, infinity), so spectrahedral projections need not be closed or directly spectrahedral.
knowledge_statements.title: Projection Exactness Boundaries

children.title: Direct Spectrahedral Representations
children.top_down_role: Representations without projection variables.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C\) is directly spectrahedral exactly when \(C=\{x:A_0+\sum_{i=1}^n x_iA_i\succeq0\}\) for finite symmetric matrices \(A_i\).

source_refs.locator: 5.5 Spectrahedra and Semidefinite Programming p. 231

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A set \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) has a direct spectrahedral representation if there exist an integer \(m\ge1\) and matrices \(A_0,A_1,\ldots,A_n\in\mathbb S^m\) such that
\[
C=\left\{x\in\mathbb R^n:A_0+\sum_{i=1}^n x_iA_i\succeq0\right\}.
\]
No auxiliary variable is quantified or projected out. Such a set is a spectrahedron; it is convex and closed because it is the inverse image of \(\mathbb S_+^m\) under an affine continuous map.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A direct spectrahedral representation describes a set by one finite affine LMI in its original variables, without auxiliary projection variables.
knowledge_statements.title: Direct Spectrahedral Representations

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A set \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a spectrahedral shadow if there exist integers \(r,m\geq 0\), matrices \(A_0,A_1,\ldots,A_n,B_1,\ldots,B_m\in\mathbb S^r\), and the coordinate projection \(\pi(x,y)=x\) such that
\[
C=\pi\!\left(\left\{(x,y)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m:A_0+\sum_{i=1}^n x_iA_i+\sum_{j=1}^m y_jB_j\succeq0\right\}\right).
\]
Equivalently, \(C\) is a linear image of a spectrahedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A spectrahedral shadow is the projection of the feasible set of an affine linear matrix inequality in visible and auxiliary variables.
knowledge_statements.title: Spectrahedral Shadows

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A PSD extended formulation of \(C\) consists of an integer \(r\), a linear map \(\mathcal A:\mathbb S^r\to\mathbb R^q\), a vector \(b\in\mathbb R^q\), and a linear map \(\pi:\mathbb S^r\to\mathbb R^n\) satisfying
\[
C=\left\{\pi(X):\mathcal A(X)=b,\ X\succeq0\right\}.
\]
An affine projection may be used equivalently by adjoining a fixed scalar coordinate. The formulation is exact only when both inclusions between \(C\) and the projected lifted feasible set hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A PSD extended formulation describes a set as the exact projection of a positive-semidefinite matrix satisfying affine equations.

children.title: Projection-Induced Nonclosedness
children.top_down_role: Closure failures arising from linear images of semidefinite feasible sets.

knowledge_statements.title: Projection-Induced Nonclosedness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A two-by-two PSD projection exhibiting loss of closedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\pi:\mathbb S^2\to\mathbb R^2\) be defined by \(\pi(X)=(X_{11},X_{12})\). Then
\[
\pi(\mathbb S_+^2)=\left\{(a,b)\in\mathbb R^2:a>0\right\}\cup\{(0,0)\}.
\]
For every integer \(k\geq1\), the point \((1/k,1)\) belongs to this image, whereas its limit \((0,1)\) does not. Consequently, \(\pi(\mathbb S_+^2)\) is not closed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projecting the two-by-two PSD cone onto one diagonal and one off-diagonal entry gives a nonclosed convex set: it contains every point with positive first coordinate and also the origin, but no other point with zero first coordinate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\pi(\mathbb S_+^2)\) is a nonclosed linear image of the closed PSD cone \(\mathbb S_+^2\).

notation.meaning: Projection retaining the upper-left and off-diagonal entries.

children.title: PSD Block Size
children.top_down_role: Largest semidefinite block as a representation-size parameter.

assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) admits at least one finite-dimensional PSD extended formulation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{bs}_{\mathrm{psd}}(C)\) is the minimum PSD matrix order required by an exact single-block lift of \(C\).

notation.meaning: Minimum order of a single PSD block representing C.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Single-block PSD size; multiple-block conventions require separate accounting.

source_refs.locator: 6 Semidefinite Representability p. 251
source_refs.source_title: Semidefinite Optimization and Convex Algebraic Geometry

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a semidefinite-representable set \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), define its single-block PSD size by
\[
\operatorname{bs}_{\mathrm{psd}}(C)=\min\left\{r:\ C=\left\{\pi(X):\mathcal A(X)=b,\ X\in\mathbb S_+^r\right\}\right\},
\]
where the minimum ranges over all finite-dimensional linear maps \(\mathcal A\), right-hand sides \(b\), and affine or linear projections \(\pi\). If no such formulation exists, set \(\operatorname{bs}_{\mathrm{psd}}(C)=+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: PSD block size is the smallest matrix order of a single positive-semidefinite block in an exact lift of the represented set.
knowledge_statements.title: PSD Block Size

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a semidefinite-representable set \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), its PSD lift dimension in auxiliary-coordinate convention is
\[
\operatorname{ldim}_{\mathrm{psd}}(C)=\min\left\{m:\ C=\left\{x\in\mathbb R^n:\exists y\in\mathbb R^m,\ A_0+\sum_{i=1}^n x_iA_i+\sum_{j=1}^m y_jB_j\succeq0\right\}\right\}.
\]
The matrix order is unrestricted in this measure. If no such representation exists, define \(\operatorname{ldim}_{\mathrm{psd}}(C)=+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lift dimension counts the minimum auxiliary scalar variables needed to express a set as the projection of an affine LMI.
knowledge_statements.title: Lift Dimension

children.title: PSD Extension Complexity Lower Bounds
children.top_down_role: Structural limits on the size of positive-semidefinite extended formulations.

assumptions_latex: \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a polytope with facet inequalities and vertices defining a slack matrix \(S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{xc}_{\mathrm{psd}}(P)=\operatorname{rank}_{\mathrm{psd}}(S)\), so PSD-rank lower bounds are PSD extension-complexity lower bounds.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polytope PSD extension complexity through slack-matrix PSD rank.

source_refs.locator: 6 Semidefinite Representability p. 251
source_refs.source_title: Semidefinite Optimization and Convex Algebraic Geometry

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S\in\mathbb R_+^{f\times v}\) be a slack matrix of a polytope \(P\). The least order of a PSD cone admitting an exact lift of \(P\) equals the least integer \(r\) for which there exist matrices \(A_1,\ldots,A_f,B_1,\ldots,B_v\in\mathbb S_+^r\) satisfying
\[
S_{ij}=\langle A_i,B_j\rangle\quad\text{for all }i,j.
\]
Consequently, proving that no such factorization exists at order below \(r\) certifies \(\operatorname{xc}_{\mathrm{psd}}(P)\geq r\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a polytope, PSD extension complexity equals the PSD rank of its slack matrix, converting factorization obstructions into lift-size lower bounds.
knowledge_statements.title: PSD Extension Complexity Lower Bounds

children.title: Semidefinite-Representability Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Nonrepresentability and closure-sensitive projection phenomena.

assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is considered in finite-dimensional real space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Nonconvexity or failure of semialgebraicity precludes semidefinite representability, whereas nonclosedness alone does not.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary representability conditions and the closure-sensitive projection boundary.

source_refs.locator: 6 Semidefinite Representability p. 251
source_refs.source_title: Semidefinite Optimization and Convex Algebraic Geometry

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Every spectrahedron is convex and semialgebraic, and these properties are preserved under linear projection. Hence every semidefinite-representable set \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is convex and semialgebraic. Therefore, if \(C\) is nonconvex or is not semialgebraic, then \(C\) has no finite PSD lift. Closedness is not a necessary condition: a projection of a closed spectrahedron can be nonclosed. Thus failure of closedness cannot by itself certify nonrepresentability, and closure-sensitive arguments must distinguish \(C\), \(\overline C\), and the actual projected image.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Semidefinite-representable sets must be convex and semialgebraic, but they need not be closed because projection can destroy closedness.
knowledge_statements.title: Semidefinite-Representability Boundaries

knowledge_statements.title: Matrix-Variable Conic Form
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal matrix-variable form with affine equality and inequality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(C\in\mathbb S^r\), linear maps \(\mathcal A:\mathbb S^r\to\mathbb R^m\) and \(\mathcal G:\mathbb S^r\to\mathbb R^p\), and vectors \(b\in\mathbb R^m\) and \(h\in\mathbb R^p\), a matrix-variable semidefinite program has the form
\[
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{minimize}_{X\in\mathbb S^r}\quad &\langle C,X\rangle\\
\operatorname{subject\ to}\quad &\mathcal A(X)=b,\\
&\mathcal G(X)\leq h,\\
&X\succeq0,
\end{aligned}
\]
where \(\langle C,X\rangle=\operatorname{tr}(CX)\) and the inequality is componentwise. When \(p=0\), the feasible region is an affine slice of \(\mathbb S_+^r\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A matrix-variable SDP minimizes a trace-linear objective over a positive-semidefinite matrix subject to affine equalities and optional componentwise affine inequalities.
assumptions_latex: \(C\in\mathbb S^r\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(h\in\mathbb R^p\) are fixed data.
\(\mathcal A:\mathbb S^r\to\mathbb R^m\) and \(\mathcal G:\mathbb S^r\to\mathbb R^p\) are linear maps.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The program optimizes a linear functional over \(\mathbb S_+^r\) intersected with affine equality and componentwise affine inequality constraints.

notation.meaning: Trace inner product on symmetric matrices.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An affine-pencil semidefinite program is
\[
\operatorname{minimize}_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\ c^\top x
\quad\operatorname{subject\ to}\quad
A(x):=A_0+\sum_{i=1}^n x_iA_i\succeq0.
\]
Its feasible set \(\{x:A(x)\succeq0\}\) is a spectrahedron. Affine scalar equalities may be imposed separately or encoded by paired scalar inequalities; multiple linear matrix inequalities may be combined into one block-diagonal pencil without changing the visible feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An affine-pencil SDP optimizes over vector variables whose affine symmetric matrix pencil must be positive semidefinite.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Affine-pencil SDP and block-diagonal aggregation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Covers the vector-variable affine-pencil form, its diagonal LP boundary, and aggregation of multiple LMIs and scalar inequalities. The separately extracted matrix-variable standard form remains owned by the corresponding matrix-variable node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $F_1,\ldots,F_n,G\in\mathbb S^k$. A vector-variable affine-pencil SDP has the form
\[
\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}c^Tx\quad\text{subject to}\quad F(x):=\sum_{j=1}^n x_jF_j+G\preccurlyeq0,\qquad Ax=b.
\]
Its inequality form omits the affine equalities. If $F_1,\ldots,F_n,G$ are diagonal, then $F(x)\preccurlyeq0$ is equivalent to componentwise scalar linear inequalities, and the problem reduces to an LP. More generally, for affine symmetric-matrix mappings $F^{(i)}(x)$ and scalar inequalities $Hx\leq h$,
\[
\left(F^{(i)}(x)\preccurlyeq0\ \forall i=1,\ldots,K\ \text{and}\ Hx\leq h\right)
\iff
\operatorname{diag}\!\left(\operatorname{Diag}(Hx-h),F^{(1)}(x),\ldots,F^{(K)}(x)\right)\preccurlyeq0.
\]
Any affine equalities $Ax=b$ are retained separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A vector-variable SDP constrains an affine symmetric-matrix pencil to be negative semidefinite, possibly together with affine equalities. When every matrix in the pencil is diagonal, the matrix inequality is exactly a collection of scalar linear inequalities, so the model is an LP. Multiple LMIs and scalar linear inequalities can be represented by one block-diagonal LMI, while affine equalities remain separate.
assumptions_latex: F^{(i)}(x)\text{ is affine and symmetric-matrix-valued for }i=1,\ldots,K.
\operatorname{Diag}(Hx-h)\text{ denotes the diagonal matrix with diagonal }Hx-h.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \left[F^{(i)}(x)\preccurlyeq0\ \forall i\ \text{and}\ Hx\leq h\right]\iff\operatorname{diag}\!\left(\operatorname{Diag}(Hx-h),F^{(1)}(x),\ldots,F^{(K)}(x)\right)\preccurlyeq0;\qquad F_j,G\text{ diagonal}\Rightarrow F(x)\preccurlyeq0\text{ is a finite system of linear inequalities}.

children.title: Linear-Cone Component
children.top_down_role: Polyhedral constraint blocks within mixed conic formulations.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Membership in \(K_{\mathrm{lin}}\) exactly imposes componentwise nonnegativity, equality-to-zero, and unrestricted linear coordinates.

notation.meaning: Product cone for linear inequality, equality, and free components.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear portion of a mixed product-cone model.

source_refs.locator: 11.1 From linear to conic models p. 381

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For affine maps \(g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^p\), \(h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^q\), and \(u:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^f\), the linear-cone component is
\[
(g(x),h(x),u(x))\in K_{\mathrm{lin}}:=\mathbb R_+^p\times\{0\}^q\times\mathbb R^f.
\]
This condition is equivalent to \(g(x)\geq0\) componentwise and \(h(x)=0\), while \(u(x)\) is unrestricted. Sign conventions may replace \(\mathbb R_+^p\) by \(\mathbb R_-^p\) after negating the corresponding affine map.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The linear component collects nonnegative orthants, zero cones for equalities, and free coordinates into one product cone.
knowledge_statements.title: Linear-Cone Component

children.title: Second-Order-Cone Component
children.top_down_role: Lorentz-cone constraint blocks within mixed conic formulations.

assumptions_latex: \(d\geq2\) and \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^{d-1}\), \(t:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) are affine.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((t(x),F(x))\in\mathcal Q_d\) if and only if \(\|F(x)\|_2\leq t(x)\).

notation.meaning: Lorentz or second-order cone of dimension d.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lorentz-cone component of a mixed conic formulation.

source_refs.locator: 10.1 Second-order cone programs p. 347

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The \(d\)-dimensional second-order cone is
\[
\mathcal Q_d=\left\{(s,z)\in\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^{d-1}:\|z\|_2\leq s\right\}.
\]
Accordingly, a second-order-cone component in a mixed model has the form \((t(x),F(x))\in\mathcal Q_d\), equivalently \(\|F(x)\|_2\leq t(x)\). Several such constraints form a Cartesian product \(\mathcal Q_{d_1}\times\cdots\times\mathcal Q_{d_k}\), with membership checked independently block by block.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A second-order-cone component requires an affine scalar to dominate the Euclidean norm of an affine vector.

children.title: Product-Cone Coupling

knowledge_statements.title: Product-Cone Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional mixed conic form with linear equations coupling scalar, Lorentz, and semidefinite blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\mathbb R_+^p\times\prod_{j=1}^q\mathcal Q_{n_j}\times\prod_{k=1}^r\mathbb S_+^{m_k}\), and partition \(x=(u,z_1,\ldots,z_q,X_1,\ldots,X_r)\). A mixed-cone program has the coupled form \[\inf\left\{\langle c,x\rangle:\mathcal A_0u+\sum_{j=1}^q\mathcal A_jz_j+\sum_{k=1}^r\mathcal B_kX_k=b,\ x\in K\right\}.\] Coupling occurs only through the common linear equation; cone membership is blockwise. Moreover, \[K^*=\mathbb R_+^p\times\prod_{j=1}^q\mathcal Q_{n_j}\times\prod_{k=1}^r\mathbb S_+^{m_k},\] because each displayed factor is self-dual under its standard inner product.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mixed cone blocks retain separate membership constraints but interact through shared linear equations; the dual cone is the product of their dual cones.
assumptions_latex: All spaces are finite-dimensional real inner-product spaces.
Each product factor carries its standard Euclidean or trace inner product.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\in K\) is blockwise, while \(\mathcal A x=b\) couples the blocks, and \(K^*=\prod_i K_i^*\).

children.title: Lagrangian Dual Construction

knowledge_statements.title: Lagrangian Dual Construction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lagrangian derivation for an equality-form finite-dimensional conic minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \((P)\), defined by \(p^*=\inf\{\langle c,x\rangle:\mathcal Ax=b,\ x\in K\}\), use the Lagrangian \[L(x,y)=\langle c,x\rangle+\langle y,b-\mathcal Ax\rangle=\langle b,y\rangle+\langle c-\mathcal A^*y,x\rangle.\] Its dual function is \[g(y)=\inf_{x\in K}L(x,y)=\begin{cases}\langle b,y\rangle,&c-\mathcal A^*y\in K^*,\\-\infty,&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}\] Therefore the Lagrangian dual is \[d^*=\sup\{\langle b,y\rangle:c-\mathcal A^*y\in K^*\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimizing the Lagrangian over the primal cone yields the dual-cone slack condition and the standard conic dual objective.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a nonempty closed convex cone in a finite-dimensional real inner-product space.
\(\mathcal A\) is linear and \(\mathcal A^*\) is its adjoint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d^*=\sup\{\langle b,y\rangle:c-\mathcal A^*y\in K^*\}\).

children.title: Conic Dual Construction

knowledge_statements.title: Conic Dual Construction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual-cone construction of the equality-form conic dual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \((P)\): \(p^*=\inf\{\langle c,x\rangle:\mathcal Ax=b,\ x\in K\}\). A vector \(y\) is dual feasible exactly when the residual \(s=c-\mathcal A^*y\) belongs to \(K^*\). Hence the conic dual is \[(D)\qquad d^*=\sup\{\langle b,y\rangle:\mathcal A^*y+s=c,\ s\in K^*\}.\] For every primal-feasible \(x\) and dual-feasible \((y,s)\), the objective difference is \[\langle c,x\rangle-\langle b,y\rangle=\langle s,x\rangle\ge 0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The dual uses a slack in the dual cone; primal minus dual objective equals the nonnegative cone pairing of primal and slack variables.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a closed convex cone in a finite-dimensional real inner-product space.
The primal uses the minimization and equality-form convention displayed in the statement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((D)=\sup\{\langle b,y\rangle:\mathcal A^*y+s=c,\ s\in K^*\}\).

children.title: Dual-Form Equivalence
children.top_down_role: Correspondence between Lagrangian and conic dual representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Form Equivalence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence between the Lagrangian and explicit dual-slack formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the primal problem \(\inf\{\langle c,x\rangle:\mathcal Ax=b,\ x\in K\}\), the Lagrangian-dual feasible set \[Y_D=\{y:c-\mathcal A^*y\in K^*\}\] is in one-to-one correspondence with the explicit conic-dual feasible set \[F_D=\{(y,s):\mathcal A^*y+s=c,\ s\in K^*\}\] through \(s=c-\mathcal A^*y\). This correspondence preserves the objective \(\langle b,y\rangle\); consequently both constructions have the same feasible objective values, supremum, and attainment status.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Introducing the uniquely determined dual slack converts the Lagrangian dual into the explicit conic dual without changing values or attainment.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a convex cone in a finite-dimensional real inner-product space.
Both dual constructions use the same primal sign convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Y_D\ni y\longleftrightarrow (y,c-\mathcal A^*y)\in F_D\), with identical objective values.

children.title: Weak-Duality Value Ordering
children.top_down_role: Ordering relationships between primal and dual objective values.

knowledge_statements.title: Weak-Duality Value Ordering
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak duality for the canonical equality-form conic primal–dual pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\in K\) satisfy \(\mathcal Ax=b\), and let \((y,s)\) satisfy \(\mathcal A^*y+s=c\) with \(s\in K^*\). Then \[\langle b,y\rangle=\langle \mathcal Ax,y\rangle=\langle x,\mathcal A^*y\rangle=\langle c,x\rangle-\langle s,x\rangle\le \langle c,x\rangle.\] Thus every dual-feasible value is no greater than every primal-feasible value. With extended-value conventions, the optimal values obey \(d^*\le p^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every dual-feasible objective is a lower bound on every primal-feasible objective, so the dual optimum cannot exceed the primal optimum.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a convex cone and \(K^*\) is its dual cone.
The displayed primal and dual points are feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\langle b,y\rangle\le\langle c,x\rangle\), and hence \(d^*\le p^*\).

children.title: Primal Bound Certificates

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Bound Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasible primal points certify upper bounds for a conic minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \((P)\), let \(p^*=\inf\{\langle c,x\rangle:\mathcal Ax=b,\ x\in K\}\). A proposed point \(\widehat x\) is a primal bound certificate for \(U\in\mathbb R\) when \[\mathcal A\widehat x=b,\qquad \widehat x\in K,\qquad \langle c,\widehat x\rangle\le U.\] These conditions are directly checkable from the problem data and imply \[p^*\le\langle c,\widehat x\rangle\le U.\] In particular, any primal-feasible point certifies its own objective value as an upper bound on the primal optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A verifiably feasible primal point certifies that its objective value, or any larger number, is an upper bound on the minimum.
assumptions_latex: The primal problem is a minimization problem.
Cone membership and the linear equality can be checked for the proposed point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p^*\le\langle c,\widehat x\rangle\le U\).

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Bound Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasible dual points certify lower bounds for a conic minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the dual \((D)\), a pair \((\widehat y,\widehat s)\) is a dual bound certificate for \(L\in\mathbb R\) when \[\mathcal A^*\widehat y+\widehat s=c,\qquad \widehat s\in K^*,\qquad \langle b,\widehat y\rangle\ge L.\] For every primal-feasible \(x\), weak duality gives \[\langle c,x\rangle-\langle b,\widehat y\rangle=\langle x,\widehat s\rangle\ge0.\] Consequently \(L\le\langle b,\widehat y\rangle\le p^*\), so the certificate supplies a verifiable global lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible dual point and dual-cone slack certify that the dual objective, or any smaller number, globally lower-bounds the primal minimum.
assumptions_latex: The primal–dual pair uses the equality-form minimization convention.
Dual-cone membership and the affine dual equation are checkable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L\le\langle b,\widehat y\rangle\le p^*\).

children.title: Zero Duality Gap
children.top_down_role: Semidefinite optimization regimes with coincident primal and dual values.

knowledge_statements.title: Zero Duality Gap
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional Slater strong duality for the canonical conic pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\) be a closed convex cone and consider \[(P)\quad p^*=\inf\{\langle c,x\rangle:\mathcal Ax=b,\ x\in K\},\qquad (D)\quad d^*=\sup\{\langle b,y\rangle:\mathcal A^*y+s=c,\ s\in K^*\}.\] Suppose both problems are feasible. If either there exists \(x_0\in\operatorname{int}K\) with \(\mathcal Ax_0=b\), or there exists \((y_0,s_0)\) with \(\mathcal A^*y_0+s_0=c\) and \(s_0\in\operatorname{int}K^*\), then \[p^*=d^*\in\mathbb R.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Feasibility of both sides plus strict feasibility of either the primal cone constraint or dual slack yields equality of finite optimal values.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a nonempty closed convex cone.
Both primal and dual are feasible, and one satisfies the displayed Slater condition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p^*=d^*\in\mathbb R\).

children.title: Primal Attainment Regimes

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Attainment Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal attainment under strict feasibility of the dual slack.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the finite-dimensional conic pair \[(P)\quad \inf\{\langle c,x\rangle:\mathcal Ax=b,\ x\in K\},\qquad (D)\quad \sup\{\langle b,y\rangle:\mathcal A^*y+s=c,\ s\in K^*\}.\] If the primal is feasible and there exists a strictly dual-feasible pair \((y_0,s_0)\) satisfying \(\mathcal A^*y_0+s_0=c\) and \(s_0\in\operatorname{int}K^*\), then the primal infimum is finite and attained: there exists \(x^*\in K\) with \(\mathcal Ax^*=b\) and \[\langle c,x^*\rangle=p^*=d^*.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal feasibility together with an interior dual slack guarantees a finite zero gap and attainment of the primal minimum.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a nonempty closed convex cone.
The primal is feasible and the dual slack is strictly feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists x^*\in K:\mathcal Ax^*=b\) and \(\langle c,x^*\rangle=p^*=d^*\).

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Attainment Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual attainment under strict feasibility of the primal cone constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the finite-dimensional conic pair \[(P)\quad \inf\{\langle c,x\rangle:\mathcal Ax=b,\ x\in K\},\qquad (D)\quad \sup\{\langle b,y\rangle:\mathcal A^*y+s=c,\ s\in K^*\}.\] If the dual is feasible and there exists a strictly primal-feasible point \(x_0\in\operatorname{int}K\) satisfying \(\mathcal Ax_0=b\), then the dual supremum is finite and attained: there exists \((y^*,s^*)\) with \(s^*\in K^*\), \(\mathcal A^*y^*+s^*=c\), and \[\langle b,y^*\rangle=d^*=p^*.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dual feasibility together with an interior primal point guarantees a finite zero gap and attainment of the dual maximum.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a nonempty closed convex cone.
The dual is feasible and the primal is strictly feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists(y^*,s^*):\mathcal A^*y^*+s^*=c\), \(s^*\in K^*\), and \(\langle b,y^*\rangle=d^*=p^*\).

children.title: Gap-Attainment Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Distinctions among positive gaps, unattained values, and asymmetric attainment.

knowledge_statements.title: Gap-Attainment Failure Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A two-by-two SDP showing that zero gap and opposite-side Slater do not ensure primal attainment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \[p^*=\inf_{x,y\in\mathbb R}\left\{x:\begin{pmatrix}x&1\\1&y\end{pmatrix}\succeq0\right\}.\] Positive semidefiniteness forces \(x>0\), while \((x,y)=(1/t,t)\) is feasible for every \(t>0\). Hence \(p^*=0\) but no primal optimizer exists. The dual is \[d^*=\sup_{Z\succeq0}\{-2Z_{12}:Z_{11}=1,\ Z_{22}=0\}=0,\] attained at \(Z=\operatorname{diag}(1,0)\). Thus the gap is zero and the primal is strictly feasible, yet primal attainment fails because the dual has no strictly feasible slack.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A two-by-two SDP has zero gap and attained dual value but no primal minimizer, showing that the wrong-sided Slater condition does not ensure attainment.
assumptions_latex: Matrix inequalities use the trace inner product.
Variables \(x\) and \(y\) are unrestricted real scalars.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p^*=d^*=0\), the dual attains, and the primal does not attain.

notation.meaning: entry of Z in row i and column j

children.title: Optimal-Value Function Geometry

knowledge_statements.title: Optimal-Value Function Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex geometry of the right-hand-side perturbation value function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the extended-real perturbation value function \[v(u)=\inf\{\langle c,x\rangle:\mathcal Ax=b+u,\ x\in K\},\] with \(v(u)=+\infty\) when the constraint is infeasible and \(v(u)=-\infty\) when it is unbounded below. If \(K\) is convex, then \(v\) is convex: for \(u_1,u_2\) and \(\theta\in[0,1]\), \[v(\theta u_1+(1-\theta)u_2)\le\theta v(u_1)+(1-\theta)v(u_2).\] Moreover, \((u,t)\in\operatorname{epi}v\) exactly when, for every \(\varepsilon>0\), some \(x\in K\) satisfies \(\mathcal Ax=b+u\) and \(\langle c,x\rangle\le t+\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The right-hand-side perturbation value is convex, and its epigraph consists of limits of achievable feasible objective upper bounds.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a convex cone in a finite-dimensional real vector space.
The extended-real arithmetic in the convexity inequality is well-defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v\) is convex and \(\operatorname{epi}v\) has the stated approximate-feasibility representation.

children.title: Perturbation-Space Closure
children.top_down_role: Closure properties of feasible value sets under data perturbations.

knowledge_statements.title: Perturbation-Space Closure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses right-hand-side perturbations and the attainable upper image at the unperturbed value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define
\[
\mathcal E=\{(u,\alpha)\in\mathbb R^m\times\mathbb R:\exists X\succeq0,\ \mathcal A(X)=b+u,\ \langle C,X\rangle\leq\alpha\}.
\]
Then \(\mathcal E\) is closed over the fiber \(u=0\), meaning that
\[
u_k\to0,\quad \alpha_k\to\alpha,\quad (u_k,\alpha_k)\in\mathcal E
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad (0,\alpha)\in\mathcal E,
\]
if and only if \(v\) is lower semicontinuous at \(0\) and the infimum defining \(v(0)\) is attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The attainable perturbation upper image is closed over the original right-hand side exactly when the value function is lower semicontinuous there and the original primal infimum is attained.
assumptions_latex: \(n,m\in\mathbb N\), \(\mathcal A:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is linear, \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(C\in\mathbb S^n\).
\(v(u)=\inf\{\langle C,X\rangle:\mathcal A(X)=b+u,\ X\succeq0\}\), with \(\inf\varnothing=+\infty\), and \(v(0)\in\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal E\) is closed over \(u=0\) if and only if \(v\) is lower semicontinuous at \(0\) and \(v(0)\) is attained.

children.title: Supporting-Hyperplane Certificates
children.top_down_role: Support geometry connecting perturbation sets with dual certificates.

knowledge_statements.title: Supporting-Hyperplane Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A dual optimum gives an affine lower support to the convex perturbation value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If \(y\in\mathbb R^m\) satisfies \(C-\mathcal A^*y\succeq0\) and \(b^Ty=v(0)\), then
\[
v(u)\geq v(0)+y^Tu\qquad\text{for every }u\in\mathbb R^m.
\]
Thus \(u\mapsto v(0)+y^Tu\) is a supporting affine function for \(v\) at \(u=0\), and \(y\) with its dual slack is a supporting-hyperplane certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dual-feasible multiplier whose objective equals the unperturbed primal value gives a global affine lower bound that touches the perturbation value function at the origin.
assumptions_latex: \(n,m\in\mathbb N\), \(\mathcal A:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is linear, \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(C\in\mathbb S^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The affine function \(u\mapsto v(0)+y^Tu\) supports \(v\) at \(u=0\).

children.title: Primal Slater Regime

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Slater Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional SDP strong duality under primal strict feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the primal-dual pair
\[
p^*=\inf\{\langle C,X\rangle:\mathcal A(X)=b,\ X\succeq0\},\qquad
d^*=\sup\{b^Ty:C-\mathcal A^*y\succeq0\},
\]
if there exists \(X_0\succ0\) with \(\mathcal A(X_0)=b\) and \(p^*\in\mathbb R\), then there exists a dual-feasible \(y^*\in\mathbb R^m\) such that
\[
b^Ty^*=d^*=p^*.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal strict feasibility and a finite primal value imply zero duality gap and attainment of the dual optimum.
assumptions_latex: \(n,m\in\mathbb N\), \(\mathcal A:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is linear, \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(C\in\mathbb S^n\).
There exists \(X_0\in\mathbb S^n\) with \(X_0\succ0\) and \(\mathcal A(X_0)=b\).
The primal optimal value satisfies \(p^*\in\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The dual optimum is attained and \(d^*=p^*\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Primal Slater Condition and Its SDP Form
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal strict feasibility and its relation to regularity condition (4.1.28).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The primal Slater condition holds when there exists \(\bar x\in C\) such that \(G(\bar x)\in\operatorname{int}K\). For \(K=\mathcal S_-^m\), this condition is \(G(\bar x)\prec0\). Slater's condition implies regularity condition (4.1.28); in the stated convex setting, the converse holds when \(\operatorname{int}K\ne\varnothing\), in particular for convex semidefinite programs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal Slater regularity requires a point in the domain whose cone constraint is strictly feasible. For a negative-semidefinite cone, the constraint matrix must be negative definite. Slater regularity implies the referenced regularity condition, with the stated converse under the source's convexity and nonempty-interior hypotheses.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Slater Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional SDP strong duality under dual strict feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dual strict feasibility and a finite dual value imply zero duality gap and attainment of the primal optimum.
assumptions_latex: \(n,m\in\mathbb N\), \(\mathcal A:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is linear, \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(C\in\mathbb S^n\).
There exists \(y_0\in\mathbb R^m\) such that \(C-\mathcal A^*y_0\succ0\).
The dual optimal value satisfies \(d^*\in\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The primal optimum is attained and \(p^*=d^*\).

children.top_down_role: Joint primal-dual strict feasibility and central-path compatibility.

knowledge_statements.title: Two-Sided Slater Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint strict feasibility supplies symmetric strong duality and an interior domain for primal-dual path methods.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the primal-dual SDP pair, suppose there exist \(X_0\succ0\) and \((y_0,S_0)\) with
\[
\mathcal A(X_0)=b,\qquad \mathcal A^*y_0+S_0=C,\qquad S_0\succ0.
\]
If both optimal values are finite, then the primal and dual optima are attained and
\[
p^*=d^*.
\]
Moreover, the strictly feasible primal-dual domain
\[
\{(X,y,S):\mathcal A(X)=b,\ \mathcal A^*y+S=C,\ X\succ0,\ S\succ0\}
\]
is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Joint primal and dual strict feasibility, together with finite optimal values, yields attainment on both sides, zero duality gap, and a nonempty strictly feasible primal-dual domain.
assumptions_latex: \(n,m\in\mathbb N\), \(\mathcal A:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is linear, \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(C\in\mathbb S^n\).
There exist \(X_0\in\mathbb S^n\), \(y_0\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(S_0\in\mathbb S^n\) satisfying \(X_0\succ0\), \(\mathcal A(X_0)=b\), \(S_0\succ0\), and \(\mathcal A^*y_0+S_0=C\).
The primal and dual optimal values are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Both optima are attained with \(p^*=d^*\), and the strictly feasible primal-dual domain is nonempty.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every nonempty affine slice \(\mathcal F\) of the positive-semidefinite cone, its minimal containing face \(F_{\min}\) contains a feasible point in its relative interior:
\[
\mathcal F\cap\operatorname{ri}(F_{\min})\neq\varnothing.
\]
Thus failure of an ambient Slater point \(X\succ0\) does not preclude strict feasibility relative to \(F_{\min}\). If \(F_{\min}=U\mathbb S_+^rU^T\) for a full-column-rank orthonormal matrix \(U\), relative-interior feasibility means that some feasible matrix has the form \(U ZU^T\) with \(Z\succ0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every nonempty SDP feasible set contains a point in the relative interior of its smallest containing PSD face.

assumptions_latex: \(F_{\min}\) is the smallest face of \(\mathbb S_+^n\) containing the nonempty feasible set \(\mathcal F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Replacing \(X\succeq0\) by \(X=UZU^T\), \(Z\succeq0\), preserves the feasible matrices and objective values.

notation.meaning: orthonormal basis for the face support

source_refs.locator: 3.3.1 Facial structure, nondegeneracy and strict complementarity p. 37

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Every face of \(\mathbb S_+^n\) has a representation
\[
F_{\min}=\{UZU^T:Z\in\mathbb S_+^r\}
\]
for some matrix \(U\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\) satisfying \(U^TU=I_r\). Consequently, restricting the primal SDP to its minimal face gives the equivalent reduced problem
\[
\inf_{Z\succeq0}\{\langle U^TCU,Z\rangle:\mathcal A(UZU^T)=b\}.
\]
The mapping \(Z\mapsto UZU^T\) is a bijection from the reduced feasible set onto the original feasible set and preserves objective values.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The minimal PSD face is a compressed PSD cone, so substituting a smaller matrix variable gives an equivalent SDP.

knowledge_statements.title: Regularity Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Restriction to the minimal feasible face restores primal Slater regularity relative to the reduced PSD cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F_{\min}=U\mathbb S_+^rU^T\) be the minimal face containing the nonempty primal feasible set. The equivalent reduced SDP
\[
\inf\{\langle U^TCU,Z\rangle:\mathcal A(UZU^T)=b,\ Z\succeq0\}
\]
has a feasible point \(\widehat Z\succ0\). If its optimal value is finite, then its conic dual attains the same value, and this value equals the original primal optimal value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compression to the minimal feasible face yields a strictly feasible reduced SDP and therefore recovers strong duality and reduced-dual attainment when the value is finite.
assumptions_latex: \(n,m\in\mathbb N\), \(\mathcal A:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is linear, \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(C\in\mathbb S^n\).
The feasible set \(\mathcal F=\{X\in\mathbb S_+^n:\mathcal A(X)=b\}\) is nonempty and has finite optimal value.
\(F_{\min}=U\mathbb S_+^rU^T\) is the minimal face containing \(\mathcal F\), where \(U\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\) and \(U^TU=I_r\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The reduced SDP satisfies primal Slater regularity and has zero duality gap with dual attainment.

children.title: Complementary Slackness in SDP
children.top_down_role: Primal-dual interaction through optimal PSD faces.

knowledge_statements.title: Complementary Slackness in SDP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: PSD complementary slackness is a zero-gap certificate and an orthogonality relation between optimal faces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every primal-dual feasible triple \((X,y,S)\), the primal-dual gap is
\[
\langle C,X\rangle-b^Ty=\langle X,S\rangle.
\]
The triple is primal-dual optimal with zero gap if and only if
\[
\langle X,S\rangle=0.
\]
For \(X,S\succeq0\), this is equivalent to
\[
XS=SX=0,
\]
and to \(\operatorname{range}(X)\perp\operatorname{range}(S)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible primal-dual SDP triple certifies optimality and zero gap exactly when its primal matrix and dual slack have zero inner product, equivalently zero product and orthogonal ranges.
assumptions_latex: \(n,m\in\mathbb N\), \(\mathcal A:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is linear, \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(C\in\mathbb S^n\).
\(X\in\mathbb S_+^n\), \(y\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(S=C-\mathcal A^*y\in\mathbb S_+^n\) satisfy \(\mathcal A(X)=b\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The feasible triple is optimal with zero gap exactly when \(\langle X,S\rangle=0\), equivalently \(XS=0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Complementary Slackness Suffices for SDP Optimality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A sufficient primal-dual optimality certificate; the converse is not asserted without additional assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) and \(y\) be feasible for the stated primal-dual SDP pair, and define the dual slack \(Z=C-\sum_{i=1}^mA_i y_i\). If \[ZX=\left(C-\sum_{i=1}^mA_i y_i\right)X=0,\] then \(\langle C,X\rangle=b^Ty\), and \(X\) and \(y\) are primal and dual optimal, respectively. The converse may require additional assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal and dual feasibility together with matrix complementary slackness certifies equal objective values and optimality on both sides. The converse may require additional assumptions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: X\text{ and }y\text{ are primal and dual optimal, and }\langle C,X\rangle=b^Ty

children.top_down_role: Maximal complementary-rank regimes and their failure boundaries.

knowledge_statements.title: Strict Complementarity in SDP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional strict complementarity for an optimal PSD primal-slack pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An optimal complementary pair \((X^*,S^*)\in\mathbb S_+^n\times\mathbb S_+^n\) is strictly complementary when
\[
X^*+S^*\succ0.
\]
Under \(X^*S^*=0\), this condition is equivalent to
\[
\ker(X^*)\cap\ker(S^*)=\{0\}
\]
and to
\[
\operatorname{rank}(X^*)+\operatorname{rank}(S^*)=n.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A complementary optimal PSD pair is strictly complementary exactly when its sum is positive definite, equivalently when its ranks add to the matrix dimension.
assumptions_latex: \((X^*,y^*,S^*)\) is a primal-dual optimal triple with \(X^*,S^*\in\mathbb S_+^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Strict complementarity holds exactly when \(X^*+S^*\succ0\), equivalently \(\operatorname{rank}(X^*)+\operatorname{rank}(S^*)=n\).

children.title: Primal Nondegeneracy
children.top_down_role: Primal-side transversality and its implications for dual solution structure.

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is primal feasible with rank \(r\), and \(Q^TXQ=\begin{bmatrix}\Lambda&0\\0&0\end{bmatrix}\) for \(\Lambda\succ0\).

notation.meaning: tangent space to the constant-rank PSD manifold at the primal point
orthogonal eigenbasis partitioned after rank r

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tangent-space definition at a fixed-rank primal feasible matrix.

source_refs.locator: 3.3.1 Facial structure, nondegeneracy and strict complementarity p. 37

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Q=[Q_1\ Q_2]\) be orthogonal and define
\[
\mathcal T_X=\left\{Q\begin{bmatrix}H&K\\K^T&0\end{bmatrix}Q^T:H\in\mathbb S^r,\ K\in\mathbb R^{r\times(n-r)}\right\}.
\]
The feasible matrix \(X\) is primal nondegenerate when
\[
\mathcal T_X+\ker\mathcal A=\mathbb S^n.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
\mathcal T_X^\perp\cap\operatorname{range}(\mathcal A^*)=\{0\}.
\]
This condition says that no nonzero equality-constraint normal lies entirely in the normal space to the constant-rank PSD manifold at \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A primal feasible matrix is nondegenerate when its rank-manifold tangent directions together with equality-feasible directions span the full symmetric-matrix space.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal Nondegeneracy

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal M_r=\{X\in\mathcal S^n:\operatorname{rank}(X)=r\}\). For \(X\in\mathcal M_r\), let \(Q\) be an orthogonal eigenvector matrix conformally ordered with the rank-\(r\) and null-space blocks of \(X\), and define \(\mathcal T_X=\left\{Q\begin{bmatrix}U&V\\V^T&0\end{bmatrix}Q^T:U\in\mathcal S^r,\ V\in\mathbb R^{r\times(n-r)}\right\}\) and \(\mathcal N=\{Z\in\mathcal S^n:A_i\bullet Z=0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\). A solution \(X\) of \((P)\) is primal nondegenerate when \(\mathcal T_X+\mathcal N=\mathcal S^n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rank-r SDP solution is primal nondegenerate when the tangent space of the rank-r symmetric-matrix manifold at that solution, together with the nullspace of the constraint map, spans the full symmetric-matrix space.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a maximum-rank primal-dual optimal pair \((\bar X,\bar y,\bar S)\) attaining a common optimal value, define \(\mathcal B=\operatorname{range}(\bar X)\), \(\mathcal N=\operatorname{range}(\bar S)\), and \(\mathcal T=(\mathcal B+\mathcal N)^\perp\). Complementarity gives \(\bar X\bar S=0\), hence \(\mathcal B\perp\mathcal N\), and therefore \(\mathbb R^n=\mathcal B\oplus\mathcal T\oplus\mathcal N\). Relative to this decomposition, \(\bar X\) is positive definite on \(\mathcal B\) and zero on \(\mathcal T\oplus\mathcal N\), while \(\bar S\) is positive definite on \(\mathcal N\) and zero on \(\mathcal B\oplus\mathcal T\). Strict complementarity holds exactly when \(\mathcal T=\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For primal and dual optima attaining a common value, maximum-rank primal and slack matrices define orthogonal primal, transition, and dual subspaces. The transition subspace vanishes exactly under strict complementarity.

children.title: Linear-Data Perturbation Family
children.top_down_role: Value and optimal-face behavior under linear data changes.

children.title: Objective-Coefficient Perturbations
children.top_down_role: Value and optimal-face changes caused by objective-data variation.

assumptions_latex: \(C,D_1,\ldots,D_p\in\mathbb S^n\), while \(\mathcal A\) and \(b\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v(u)=\inf\{\langle C+\sum_{j=1}^p u_jD_j,X\rangle:\mathcal A(X)=b,\ X\succeq0\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Only the primal objective matrix varies; constraints and cone remain fixed.

source_refs.locator: 4.2 Parametric Linear Semidefinite Programming p. 92

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given symmetric directions \(D_1,\ldots,D_p\), an objective-coefficient perturbation replaces \(C\) by \(C(u)=C+\sum_{j=1}^p u_jD_j\) while retaining \(\mathcal A(X)=b\) and \(X\succeq0\). The perturbed primal value is \(v(u)=\inf\{\langle C(u),X\rangle:\mathcal A(X)=b,\ X\succeq0\}\), and its dual is \(\sup\{b^\top y:S=C(u)-\mathcal A^*y\succeq0\}\). Thus the feasible primal set is independent of \(u\), whereas the dual affine slack and the exposed optimal face may vary with \(u\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An objective perturbation changes the cost matrix linearly while leaving the primal feasible set fixed; the dual slack affine space changes accordingly.
knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Coefficient Perturbations

source_witnesses.locator: 4.2 Parametric Linear Semidefinite Programming p. 92

children.title: Right-Hand-Side Perturbations
children.top_down_role: Feasible-set and value changes caused by affine-constraint variation.

assumptions_latex: \(E:\mathbb R^q\to\mathbb R^m\) is linear, while \(C\) and \(\mathcal A\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v(w)=\inf\{\langle C,X\rangle:\mathcal A(X)=b+Ew,\ X\succeq0\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Only the equality right-hand side varies; objective, equality map, and cone remain fixed.

source_refs.locator: 4.2 Parametric Linear Semidefinite Programming p. 92

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a linear map \(E:\mathbb R^q\to\mathbb R^m\), a right-hand-side perturbation replaces \(b\) by \(b(w)=b+Ew\) while retaining \(C\), \(\mathcal A\), and the cone \(\mathbb S_+^n\). The perturbed primal value is \(v(w)=\inf\{\langle C,X\rangle:\mathcal A(X)=b(w),\ X\succeq0\}\), and its dual is \(\sup\{b(w)^\top y:C-\mathcal A^*y\succeq0\}\). Hence the dual feasible set is fixed, while the primal affine slice and the dual objective vary with \(w\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A right-hand-side perturbation moves the primal affine slice linearly while keeping the dual feasible set fixed and changing its objective.
knowledge_statements.title: Right-Hand-Side Perturbations

source_witnesses.locator: 4.2 Parametric Linear Semidefinite Programming p. 92

children.title: Coupled Linear-Data Perturbations
children.top_down_role: Simultaneous variation of objective coefficients and affine constraint data.

assumptions_latex: The objective and right-hand-side perturbations depend linearly on a common parameter \(t\in\mathbb R^r\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v(t)=\inf\{\langle C+Dt,X\rangle:\mathcal A(X)=b+Et,\ X\succeq0\}\).

notation.meaning: Linear objective perturbation, interpreted componentwise in a symmetric-matrix basis.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A common parameter simultaneously changes objective and equality right-hand side.

source_refs.locator: 4.2 Parametric Linear Semidefinite Programming p. 92

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D:\mathbb R^r\to\mathbb S^n\) and \(E:\mathbb R^r\to\mathbb R^m\) be linear. The coupled linear-data family is \(v(t)=\inf\{\langle C+Dt,X\rangle:\mathcal A(X)=b+Et,\ X\succeq0\}\). Its dual is \(\sup\{(b+Et)^\top y:S=C+Dt-\mathcal A^*y\succeq0\}\). The same parameter therefore moves both the primal affine objective and equality slice. Objective-only and right-hand-side-only families are recovered by setting \(E=0\) and \(D=0\), respectively.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A coupled linear-data family uses one parameter to vary both the objective matrix and equality right-hand side; the one-sided families are special cases.
knowledge_statements.title: Coupled Linear-Data Perturbations

source_witnesses.locator: 4.2 Parametric Linear Semidefinite Programming p. 92

children.title: Matrix-Coefficient Perturbations
children.top_down_role: Stability under changes to affine matrix-pencil data.

assumptions_latex: Each perturbed coefficient \(A_i(t)\) is symmetric and depends affinely on \(t\in\mathbb R^r\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v(t)=\inf\{\langle C,X\rangle:\langle A_i(t),X\rangle=b_i\ (i=1,\ldots,m),\ X\succeq0\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Perturbations act on matrices defining the affine pencil or equality map.

source_refs.locator: 4.2 Parametric Linear Semidefinite Programming p. 92

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For symmetric matrices \(A_i^j\), define \(A_i(t)=A_i^0+\sum_{j=1}^r t_jA_i^j\) and \(\mathcal A_t(X)_i=\langle A_i(t),X\rangle\). A matrix-coefficient perturbation family is \(v(t)=\inf\{\langle C,X\rangle:\mathcal A_t(X)=b,\ X\succeq0\}\), with dual \(\sup\{b^\top y:S=C-\mathcal A_t^*y\succeq0\}\). Unlike objective or right-hand-side perturbations, changing \(t\) moves both the primal constraint operator and the dual slack operator, so neither feasible set is generally fixed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Matrix-coefficient perturbations change the symmetric matrices defining the equality map, thereby moving both primal constraints and the dual slack operator.
knowledge_statements.title: Matrix-Coefficient Perturbations

children.title: Rank-Partition Transition Geometry
children.top_down_role: Changes in invariant subspaces and solution ranks across parameter regimes.

children.title: Rank-Transition Regimes
children.top_down_role: Parameter regions distinguished by changes in optimal matrix rank.

assumptions_latex: For every parameter \(t\) in the set considered, both optimal sets are nonempty.
Maximum optimal ranks \(r_P(t)\) and \(r_D(t)\) are well defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_{r,s}=\{t:r_P(t)=r,\ r_D(t)=s\}\), and rank transitions occur on its relative boundary.

notation.meaning: Maximum primal-optimal rank at parameter t.
Maximum dual-optimal slack rank at parameter t.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regimes classify parameters by maximum primal and dual-slack optimal ranks.

source_refs.locator: 4.2.3 Optimal Partition p. 100

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a parametric SDP with nonempty optimal sets, define \(r_P(t)=\max\{\operatorname{rank}X:X\in\mathcal X^*(t)\}\) and \(r_D(t)=\max\{\operatorname{rank}S:S\in\mathcal S^*(t)\}\). A rank-transition regime is a maximal connected subset of \(R_{r,s}=\{t:r_P(t)=r,\ r_D(t)=s\}\) for fixed integers \(r,s\). A parameter \(t_0\) is a rank-transition point when every relative neighborhood of \(t_0\) contains a parameter at which either maximum rank differs. Such a transition requires a positive eigenvalue of a maximally complementary primal matrix or slack to approach zero along some convergent optimal sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rank regime is a maximal connected parameter region with constant maximum primal and dual-slack ranks; transitions occur where one of those ranks changes.
knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Transition Regimes

source_witnesses.locator: 4.2.3 Optimal Partition p. 100

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The constant-rank sets are intelligible definitions, but the additional assertion that every transition forces a positive eigenvalue to approach zero along a convergent optimal sequence requires selection, boundedness, or continuity hypotheses not supplied here. The cited optimal-partition section does not specifically establish that parametric spectral claim, so an exact source is required.

children.title: Optimal-Partition Transitions
children.top_down_role: Changes in optimal facial partitions across parameter values.

assumptions_latex: A maximally complementary optimal pair exists at every parameter under consideration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((\dim\mathcal B(t),\dim\mathcal T(t),\dim\mathcal N(t))\) changes at an optimal-partition transition.

notation.meaning: Parameter-dependent primal, transition, and dual optimal-partition subspaces.
Maximum-rank primal and dual optimal matrices.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between parameter regions having different optimal-partition dimensions.

source_refs.locator: 4.2.3 Optimal Partition p. 100

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each parameter \(t\), let \(\mathcal B(t)=\operatorname{range}\bar X(t)\), \(\mathcal N(t)=\operatorname{range}\bar S(t)\), and \(\mathcal T(t)=(\mathcal B(t)+\mathcal N(t))^\perp\), using any maximally complementary pair. An optimal-partition transition occurs at \(t_0\) if the dimension triple \((\dim\mathcal B(t),\dim\mathcal T(t),\dim\mathcal N(t))\) is not locally constant at \(t_0\). Equivalently, every neighborhood contains a parameter with different maximum primal rank or maximum slack rank. Strict complementarity may consequently be gained or lost when \(\dim\mathcal T(t)\) changes between zero and a positive value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An optimal-partition transition occurs where the dimensions of the primal, transition, or dual invariant subspaces cease to be locally constant.
knowledge_statements.title: Optimal-Partition Transitions

source_witnesses.locator: 4.2.3 Optimal Partition p. 100

children.title: Invariant-Subspace Bifurcations
children.top_down_role: Qualitative changes in kernel and range subspaces along parametric families.

assumptions_latex: A continuous selection of maximally complementary optimal matrices exists along the parameter sequence considered.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Loss of a spectral gap at zero is necessary for a discontinuous change in the associated range projector.

notation.meaning: Orthogonal projector onto the range of a positive-semidefinite matrix Z.
Smallest positive eigenvalue of Z, when Z is nonzero.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bifurcation means loss of continuous stability of an optimal invariant subspace.

source_refs.locator: 4.2.3 Optimal Partition p. 100

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Z(t)\) denote either a continuous maximally complementary primal matrix or dual slack, and let \(P_{Z(t)}\) project onto \(\operatorname{range}Z(t)\). If, near \(t_0\), the rank is constant and \(\lambda_{\min}^+(Z(t))\geq\gamma>0\), then \(P_{Z(t)}\) varies continuously with \(t\). Consequently, an invariant-subspace bifurcation at which the range dimension changes or the projector has no continuous extension requires loss of the spectral gap: along some sequence \(t_k\to t_0\), \(\lambda_{\min}^+(Z(t_k))\to0\). The colliding eigenspace can then transfer between the primal, transition, and dual partition subspaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A primal or dual optimal invariant subspace can bifurcate only when its positive spectrum loses separation from zero along a convergent parameter sequence.
knowledge_statements.title: Invariant-Subspace Bifurcations

source_witnesses.locator: 4.2.3 Optimal Partition p. 100

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The spectral-gap statement is plausible under a genuinely continuous matrix selection, but it is a spectral-projector perturbation result rather than a consequence documented by the cited optimal-partition locator. The exact meaning of continuity along the parameter domain and the claimed necessity for every stated bifurcation require an authoritative perturbation-theory source.

children.title: SDP Condition Measures
children.top_down_role: Quantitative sensitivity measures for semidefinite feasibility and optimization.

assumptions_latex: The SDP data space carries a fixed norm \(\|\cdot\|_{\mathcal D}\).
The ill-posed set \(\Sigma\) is nonempty and closed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\kappa(d)=\|d\|_{\mathcal D}/\operatorname{dist}_{\mathcal D}(d,\Sigma)\), with \(\kappa(d)=+\infty\) on \(\Sigma\).

notation.meaning: Ill-posed data separating stable status regimes.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normwise distance-to-ill-posedness condition measure for a specified SDP data representation.

source_refs.locator: 4.2 Parametric Linear Semidefinite Programming p. 92

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a norm \(\|\cdot\|_{\mathcal D}\) on SDP data \(d=(\mathcal A,b,C)\), and let \(\Sigma\) be the closed set of ill-posed instances forming the boundary between the chosen well-posed status regimes, such as strict feasibility and infeasibility. Define \(\operatorname{dist}_{\mathcal D}(d,\Sigma)=\inf_{\hat d\in\Sigma}\|d-\hat d\|_{\mathcal D}\). The associated relative condition measure is \(\kappa(d)=\|d\|_{\mathcal D}/\operatorname{dist}_{\mathcal D}(d,\Sigma)\) when the denominator is positive, and \(\kappa(d)=+\infty\) when \(d\in\Sigma\). Its reciprocal is the smallest relative data perturbation capable of reaching ill-posedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An SDP condition measure compares the data norm with the distance to a specified ill-posed set; its reciprocal is the smallest relative destabilizing perturbation.
knowledge_statements.title: SDP Condition Measures

source_witnesses.locator: 4.2 Parametric Linear Semidefinite Programming p. 92

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A distance-to-ill-posedness ratio is a standard condition-number pattern, but the relevant SDP data representation, status problem, and ill-posed set must be specified to make this a definite SDP condition measure. The reciprocal interpretation also requires nonzero data norm. The cited parametric-SDP section is not an exact conditioning source, so the mathematical version cannot be accepted without a dedicated reference.

children.title: Error-Bound Regimes
children.top_down_role: Residual-to-solution-distance behavior under differing regularity conditions.

knowledge_statements.title: Error-Bound Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local metric error bounds for affine semidefinite feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal A(x)=A_0+\sum_{i=1}^m x_iA_i\) and \(F=\{x\in\mathbb R^m:\mathcal A(x)\succeq0\}\). The system is in a local error-bound regime at \(\bar x\in F\) if there exist a neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar x\) and \(\kappa<\infty\) such that
\[\operatorname{dist}(x,F)\leq \kappa\,\operatorname{dist}(\mathcal A(x),\mathbb S_+^n)\qquad(x\in U).\]
For Frobenius distance, the residual on the right equals \(\|\Pi_{\mathbb S_-^n}(\mathcal A(x))\|_F\). The local error-bound modulus is the infimum of all admissible constants \(\kappa\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local error bound controls distance to the feasible parameter set by a constant times the negative-semidefinite residual of the affine matrix pencil; its modulus is the infimum of the admissible constants.
assumptions_latex: Matrix-space distance is Frobenius distance when the projection formula is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}(x,F)\leq\kappa\operatorname{dist}(\mathcal A(x),\mathbb S_+^n)\) locally.

notation.meaning: cone of positive-semidefinite real symmetric matrices
Frobenius projection onto the negative-semidefinite cone

children.title: Distance to Ill-Posedness
children.top_down_role: Data-space proximity to transitions between stable feasibility statuses.

knowledge_statements.title: Distance to Ill-Posedness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normwise distance of SDP feasibility data to the status boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D=(A_0,A_1,\ldots,A_m)\) denote the data of the feasibility system \(A_0+\sum_i x_iA_i\succeq0\), equipped with a fixed product norm. Let \(\mathrm{SF}\) be the set of strictly feasible data, \(\mathrm{SI}\) the set of strongly infeasible data, and
\[\Sigma=\overline{\mathrm{SF}}\cap\overline{\mathrm{SI}}\]
the ill-posed status boundary. The distance to ill-posedness is
\[\rho(D)=\operatorname{dist}(D,\Sigma)=\inf_{D'\in\Sigma}\|D-D'\|.\]
Thus \(\rho(D)>0\) is a perturbation margin within a well-posed status regime, whereas \(\rho(D)=0\) identifies ill-posed data.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Distance to ill-posedness is the smallest normwise perturbation taking SDP feasibility data to the common boundary of strict feasibility and strong infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: The finite-dimensional data space carries a fixed product norm.
\(\mathrm{SF}\) and \(\mathrm{SI}\) use the same perturbation model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho(D)=\inf_{D'\in\Sigma}\|D-D'\|\).

notation.meaning: distance from the data to ill-posedness

children.title: Strictly Feasible Regimes
children.top_down_role: Systems whose feasible region reaches the positive-definite interior.

knowledge_statements.title: Strictly Feasible Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Slater interior access for an affine semidefinite system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For symmetric matrices \(A_0,\ldots,A_m\in\mathbb S^n\), define \(\mathcal A(x)=A_0+\sum_{i=1}^m x_iA_i\). The feasibility system \(\mathcal A(x)\succeq0\) is strictly feasible if
\[\exists\,\bar x\in\mathbb R^m\quad \mathcal A(\bar x)\succ0.\]
Equivalently, \(\mathcal A(\mathbb R^m)\cap\operatorname{int}\mathbb S_+^n\neq\varnothing\), where \(\operatorname{int}\mathbb S_+^n=\mathbb S_{++}^n\). A witness \(\bar x\) is a Slater point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An SDP feasibility system is strictly feasible exactly when its affine matrix space contains a positive-definite matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal A(\mathbb R^m)\cap\mathbb S_{++}^n\neq\varnothing\).

children.title: Boundary-Feasible Regimes
children.top_down_role: Feasible systems confined to a proper face of the PSD cone.

knowledge_statements.title: Boundary-Feasible Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility confined to the boundary of the semidefinite cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal A(x)=A_0+\sum_{i=1}^m x_iA_i\). The system \(\mathcal A(x)\succeq0\) is boundary-feasible if
\[\{x:\mathcal A(x)\succeq0\}\neq\varnothing
\quad\text{and}\quad
\{x:\mathcal A(x)\succ0\}=\varnothing.\]
Equivalently, the affine space \(\mathcal A(\mathbb R^m)\) meets \(\mathbb S_+^n\) but not its interior. Consequently every feasible matrix is singular and belongs to a proper face of \(\mathbb S_+^n\), although different feasible matrices need not have identical kernels.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A boundary-feasible SDP has positive-semidefinite solutions but no positive-definite solution; every feasible matrix is therefore singular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal A(\mathbb R^m)\cap\mathbb S_+^n\neq\varnothing\) and \(\mathcal A(\mathbb R^m)\cap\mathbb S_{++}^n=\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: affine matrix space generated by the pencil

children.title: Interior-Access Transition
children.top_down_role: Geometric boundary separating interior-accessible instances from face-confined instances.

knowledge_statements.title: Interior-Access Transition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-sided identity perturbation converts boundary feasibility into strict feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal A(x)=A_0+\sum_{i=1}^m x_iA_i\) with \(A_0,ldots,A_m\in\mathbb S^n\), suppose \(\mathcal A(\bar x)\succeq0\), and define \(\mathcal A_\varepsilon(x)=\mathcal A(x)+\varepsilon I_n\). For every \(\varepsilon>0\),
\[\mathcal A_\varepsilon(\bar x)\succ0.\]
Thus, when the original system is boundary-feasible, the family has boundary-only access at \(\varepsilon=0\) and strict interior access for every \(\varepsilon>0\). Under the Frobenius product norm on the data, the constant-term perturbation has magnitude \(\varepsilon\sqrt n\), which tends to zero as \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding any positive multiple of the identity to a feasible affine pencil produces a positive-definite witness; the Frobenius magnitude of this constant-term perturbation tends to zero with the multiplier.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal A_\varepsilon(\bar x)\succ0\).

children.title: Strong Infeasibility
children.top_down_role: Separated affine and cone systems admitting ordinary separation certificates.

knowledge_statements.title: Strong Infeasibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-distance infeasibility of an affine matrix space and the PSD cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(L=A_0+\operatorname{span}\{A_1,\ldots,A_m\}\subseteq\mathbb S^n\). The semidefinite system determined by \(L\) is strongly infeasible when
\[L\cap\mathbb S_+^n=\varnothing
\quad\text{and}\quad
\operatorname{dist}(L,\mathbb S_+^n)>0.\]
In finite dimensions, this is equivalent to the existence of \(Y\succeq0\) satisfying \(\langle Y,A_i\rangle=0\) for every \(i=1,\ldots,m\) and \(\langle Y,A_0\rangle<0\). Such a matrix \(Y\) is a strict separation certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong infeasibility means the affine matrix space is disjoint from and a positive distance from the PSD cone, equivalently admitting a strict PSD separation certificate.
assumptions_latex: Distance is induced by a fixed finite-dimensional norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L\cap\mathbb S_+^n=\varnothing\) and \(\operatorname{dist}(L,\mathbb S_+^n)>0\).

children.title: Weak Infeasibility
children.top_down_role: Disjoint but nonseparated systems and their asymptotic geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Weak Infeasibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Infeasibility without positive separation from the semidefinite cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(L=A_0+\operatorname{span}\{A_1,\ldots,A_m\}\subseteq\mathbb S^n\). The semidefinite system is weakly infeasible if
\[L\cap\mathbb S_+^n=\varnothing
\quad\text{and}\quad
\operatorname{dist}(L,\mathbb S_+^n)=0.\]
Equivalently, no feasible matrix exists, but there are sequences \(W_k\in L\) and \(X_k\succeq0\) such that \(\|W_k-X_k\|\to0\). Hence no strict-separation certificate of the ordinary form \(Y\succeq0\), \(\langle Y,A_i\rangle=0\), and \(\langle Y,A_0\rangle<0\) can exist.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A weakly infeasible SDP has no feasible point, yet its affine matrix space has zero distance from the PSD cone.
assumptions_latex: Distance is induced by any fixed finite-dimensional norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L\cap\mathbb S_+^n=\varnothing\) and \(\operatorname{dist}(L,\mathbb S_+^n)=0\).

notation.meaning: asymptotically coincident affine and PSD sequences

children.top_down_role: Instances lying close to feasibility despite lacking a stable feasible status.

knowledge_statements.title: Near-Feasible Instances
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tolerance-dependent proximity of an affine SDP system to feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D=(A_0,A_1,\ldots,A_m)\), let \(L(D)=A_0+\operatorname{span}\{A_1,\ldots,A_m\}\subseteq\mathbb S^n\), and equip \(\mathbb S^n\) with the Frobenius norm. For \(\varepsilon\geq0\), the instance \(D\) is \(\varepsilon\)-near-feasible when
\[r(D):=\inf_{W\in L(D)}\operatorname{dist}_F(W,\mathbb S_+^n)\leq\varepsilon.\]
Equivalently, for every \(\eta>0\), there exists \(x\in\mathbb R^m\) such that
\[\left\|\Pi_{\mathbb S_-^n}\!\left(A_0+\sum_{i=1}^m x_iA_i\right)\right\|_F\leq\varepsilon+\eta.\]
Exact feasibility implies \(r(D)=0\), while \(r(D)=0\) also permits weak infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An instance is near-feasible at tolerance epsilon when its affine matrix space comes within epsilon, in Frobenius distance, of the PSD cone.
assumptions_latex: Matrix-space distance is induced by the Frobenius norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r(D)\leq\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: Frobenius distance residual of the affine matrix space from the PSD cone

children.title: Ill-Posed Feasibility Instances
children.top_down_role: Instances whose feasibility status is unstable under small perturbations.

knowledge_statements.title: Ill-Posed Feasibility Instances
knowledge_statements.scope_note: SDP data lying on the boundary between robust feasibility statuses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
In a normed space of affine SDP data, let \(\mathrm{SF}\) denote strictly feasible instances and \(\mathrm{SI}\) strongly infeasible instances. An instance \(D\) is feasibility-ill-posed when
\[D\in\Sigma:=\overline{\mathrm{SF}}\cap\overline{\mathrm{SI}}.\]
Equivalently, for every \(\varepsilon>0\), there exist data \(D_{\mathrm{sf}}\in\mathrm{SF}\) and \(D_{\mathrm{si}}\in\mathrm{SI}\) with \(\|D-D_{\mathrm{sf}}\|<\varepsilon\) and \(\|D-D_{\mathrm{si}}\|<\varepsilon\). Thus arbitrarily small admissible perturbations can place the data on either robust side of the feasibility-status boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Ill-posed feasibility data can be perturbed arbitrarily slightly to both a strictly feasible instance and a strongly infeasible instance.
assumptions_latex: The data space and admissible perturbation norm are fixed.
Strict and strong statuses are defined for the same formulation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D\in\overline{\mathrm{SF}}\cap\overline{\mathrm{SI}}\).

children.title: Status-Boundary Perturbations
children.top_down_role: Perturbation directions that move systems across the feasible–infeasible boundary.

knowledge_statements.title: Status-Boundary Perturbations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Perturbation stability away from the ill-posed SDP feasibility boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Sigma=\overline{\mathrm{SF}}\cap\overline{\mathrm{SI}}\) be the ill-posed boundary in a fixed normed data space, and let \(\rho(D)=\operatorname{dist}(D,\Sigma)>0\). If \(D\in\mathrm{SF}\cup\mathrm{SI}\), then every continuous perturbation path \(\gamma:[0,1]\to B(D,\rho(D))\) beginning at \(D\) remains in the same status region as \(D\). In particular, a status change from strict feasibility to strong infeasibility, or conversely, requires a perturbation path to meet \(\Sigma\); consequently its maximum displacement from \(D\) is at least \(\rho(D)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A continuous perturbation cannot switch between strict feasibility and strong infeasibility without reaching the ill-posed boundary; distance to that boundary is the stability margin.
assumptions_latex: The perturbation path is continuous in the chosen data norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\gamma([0,1])\subseteq B(D,\rho(D))\) cannot change the robust feasibility status.

source_refs.locator: 3 The Geometry of Semidefinite Programming p. 29

source_witnesses.locator: 3 The Geometry of Semidefinite Programming p. 29

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Avoiding the set defined only as closure(SF) intersect closure(SI) does not by itself establish that every point of the ball belongs to the same robust status region. The claim requires an inspectable source proving the relevant decomposition and boundary topology for this SDP data model.
