knowledge_statements.title: Fill-Induced Clique Growth
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relates chordal fill choices to the largest PSD block in sparse conversion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H=(V,E\cup F)\) be a chordal extension of \(G=(V,E)\), with maximal cliques \(C_1,\ldots,C_q\). children.title: Minimum Completion Rank

notation.meaning: Set of PSD completions of the partial matrix

auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines minimum rank within one nonempty PSD-completion fiber.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the nonempty completion fiber \(\mathcal C(a)=\{X\in\mathbb S^n_+:P_E(X)=a\}\), the minimum completion rank is
\[
r_{\min}(a):=\min_{X\in\mathcal C(a)}\operatorname{rank}X.
\]
The minimum is attained because the rank takes values in the finite set \(\{0,1,\ldots,n\}\). Equivalently, \(r_{\min}(a)\) is the least integer \(r\) for which vectors \(u_1,\ldots,u_n\in\mathbb R^r\) exist with \(u_i^{\mathsf T}u_j=a_{ij}\) for every \((i,j)\in E\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The minimum completion rank is the smallest rank attained by any positive-semidefinite matrix matching all specified entries.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The partial matrix \(a\) has a unique positive-semidefinite completion if its completion fiber is a singleton:
\[
\mathcal C(a)=\{X\in\mathbb S^n_+:P_E(X)=a\}=\{X_\star\}
\]
for some \(X_\star\in\mathbb S^n_+\). Equivalently, whenever \(Y\in\mathbb S^n_+\) satisfies \(P_E(Y)=a\), one has \(Y=X_\star\). This definition concerns the completed matrix itself; Gram factors of \(X_\star\) may still differ by orthogonal transformations.

assumptions_latex: \(E\) is a symmetric index set containing every diagonal index.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Represents rank-bounded completion fibers through finite-dimensional Gram vectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define
\[
\mathcal C_r(a):=\{X\in\mathbb S^n_+:P_E(X)=a,\ \operatorname{rank}X\leq r\}.
\]
Then
\[
\mathcal C_r(a)=\{U^{\mathsf T}U:U=[u_1\ \cdots\ u_n]\in\mathbb R^{r\times n},\ u_i^{\mathsf T}u_j=a_{ij}\text{ for all }(i,j)\in E\}.
\]
Consequently, \(\mathcal C_r(a)\neq\varnothing\) if and only if \(a\) has a Gram realization by vectors in \(\mathbb R^r\), and the least such \(r\) equals its minimum completion rank.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X_\star\) is unique if and only if \(\ker P_E\cap(\mathbb S^n_+-X_\star)=\{0\}\).

notation.meaning: Feasible displacement set from the completion

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives an exact feasible-displacement criterion linking boundary rank and uniqueness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The completion \(X_\star\) is the unique member of \(\{X\in\mathbb S^n_+:P_E(X)=a\}\) if and only if
\[
\ker P_E\cap(\mathbb S^n_+-X_\star)=\{0\}.
\]
Indeed, a second completion has the form \(X_\star+D\) with nonzero \(D\in\ker P_E\) and \(X_\star+D\succeq0\). The rank of \(X_\star\) determines the face of \(\mathbb S^n_+\) containing it and therefore restricts which such displacements are possible, but low rank alone neither implies nor excludes uniqueness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A completion is unique exactly when no nonzero unspecified-entry perturbation can preserve positive semidefiniteness; rank controls the relevant PSD face.
knowledge_statements.title: Rank–Uniqueness Interaction

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The feasible-displacement criterion is correct and fits the rank–uniqueness leaf, but it lacks a citation and includes an explicit proof sentence.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The completion problem is degenerate when \(\mathcal C(a)\neq\varnothing\) but \(\mathcal C(a)\cap\mathbb S^n_{++}=\varnothing\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A feasible PSD-completion problem is completion-degenerate when
\[
\mathcal C(a)=\{X\in\mathbb S^n_+:P_E(X)=a\}\neq\varnothing
\quad\text{and}\quad
\mathcal C(a)\cap\mathbb S^n_{++}=\varnothing.
\]
Equivalently, the affine completion constraints satisfy feasibility but fail Slater's condition in the ambient cone \(\mathbb S^n_+\). In that case every completion lies in a proper face of \(\mathbb S^n_+\), although the completion fiber may contain either one matrix or many matrices.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F_0=\mathbb S^n_+\). The completion singularity degree \(\operatorname{sd}(a)\) is the least integer \(k\geq0\) for which there are valid facial-reduction exposing matrices \(Z_1,\ldots,Z_k\) producing faces
\[
F_i=F_{i-1}\cap\{X:\langle Z_i,X\rangle=0\},\qquad i=1,\ldots,k,
\]
such that \(F_k=F_{\min}\), the minimal face of \(\mathbb S^n_+\) containing \(\mathcal C(a)\). Thus \(\operatorname{sd}(a)=0\) under ambient strict feasibility, while a degenerate feasible system has \(\operatorname{sd}(a)\geq1\).

children.title: Graph-Induced Degeneracy
children.top_down_role: Degenerate completion behavior attributable to sparsity-graph structure.

assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq V\) is a clique of the specification graph.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every PSD completion is singular and satisfies \(X\widehat u=0\) for each \(u\in\ker a[C]\).

notation.meaning: Fully specified principal submatrix indexed by the clique

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: a singular specified clique block forces its null vectors into the nullspace of every PSD completion
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A singular fully specified clique supplies a graph-local degeneracy certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(0\neq u\in\ker a[C]\), and extend \(u\) by zero outside \(C\) to obtain \(\widehat u\in\mathbb R^V\). For every PSD completion \(X\),
\[
\widehat u^{\mathsf T}X\widehat u=u^{\mathsf T}a[C]u=0.
\]
Because \(X\succeq0\), this equality implies \(X\widehat u=0\). Hence every completion is singular, strict feasibility fails, and the specified clique forces linear relations between the rows or Gram vectors indexed by \(C\) and the remaining vertices. The pair \((C,u)\) is therefore a verifiable graph-induced degeneracy certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A singular specified clique forces its null vectors into every completion's nullspace, making all PSD completions singular.
knowledge_statements.title: Graph-Induced Degeneracy

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The singular-clique certificate is mathematically sound and correctly classified as a certificate, but it has no citation and the statement includes its proof.

knowledge_statements.title: Sparse–Completable Cone Duality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional duality under the trace pairing on the specified-entry space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P_E:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb S^n(E)\) be orthogonal projection. Define \(K_E=\mathbb S_+^n\cap\mathbb S^n(E)\) and \(C_E=P_E(\mathbb S_+^n)\). With duals taken inside \(\mathbb S^n(E)\), \[K_E^*=C_E\qquad\text{and}\qquad C_E^*=K_E.\] Thus zero-filled sparse PSD matrices and PSD-completable partial matrices occupy the same coordinate space but are mutually dual cones rather than generally identical cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the trace pairing, the dual of the sparse PSD cone is the PSD-completable cone, and conversely.

\(\mathbb S^n(E)\) carries the trace inner product inherited from \(\mathbb S^n\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A chordal extension of \(G=(V,E)\) is a graph \(H=(V,E\cup F)\), where \(F\subseteq\binom V2\setminus E\), such that every cycle of \(H\) having length at least four possesses a chord. Equivalently, \(H\) admits a perfect elimination ordering: for each vertex, its neighbors occurring later in the ordering form a clique. The pairs in \(F\) are called fill edges; an extension is minimal when no proper subset of \(F\) remains a chordal extension.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A chordal extension adds fill edges until every long cycle has a chord, equivalently until the graph has a perfect elimination ordering.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: There exists a tree \(T\) with node set \(\mathcal C\) such that, for every vertex \(v\in V\), the set \(\{C\in\mathcal C:v\in C\}\) induces a connected subtree. Equivalently, along the unique path in \(T\) between cliques \(C\) and \(D\), every intermediate clique contains \(C\cap D\). Consequently each edge \(CD\) of \(T\) has separator \(S_{CD}=C\cap D\), and these separators organize all overlaps needed by clique-based matrix formulations.

children.title: Elimination Trees
children.top_down_role: Tree structures encoding sparse elimination dependencies.

assumptions_latex: \(H\) is chordal with perfect elimination ordering \(1,\ldots,n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p\) defines the elimination forest of the ordering.

notation.meaning: Parent map of the elimination forest.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Vertex elimination forest associated with a fixed perfect elimination ordering.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each vertex \(i\), let \(N_i^+=\{j>i:\{i,j\}\in E(H)\}\). If \(N_i^+\ne\varnothing\), define \(p(i)=\min N_i^+\) and add the directed edge from \(i\) to \(p(i)\); otherwise \(i\) is a root. Since every parent has a larger index, these edges form a forest, called the elimination forest, and a tree when there is one root. Chordality ensures that \(N_i^+\) is a clique, which supports nested propagation of elimination updates toward the roots.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each vertex points to its earliest later neighbor in a perfect elimination ordering; the resulting acyclic parent relation is the elimination forest.
knowledge_statements.title: Elimination Trees

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated parent convention is plausible, but elimination-tree definitions vary with ordering and graph/factorization conventions. No citation is supplied to establish the intended convention and the final propagation claim.

children.title: Fill-versus-Block-Size Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Computational consequences of extension choices for clique size and fill.

assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a chordal extension with maximal cliques \(\mathcal C(H)\) and clique-tree separators \(\mathcal S(H)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Phi(H)=\sum_{C\in\mathcal C(H)}|C|^3\) is a dense-factorization proxy, while \(\Psi(H)=\sum_{S\in\mathcal S(H)}|S|^2\) measures overlap coupling.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural cost proxies, not a universal solver complexity theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For clique-based semidefinite computations using dense linear algebra within each clique, a standard arithmetic proxy is \[\Phi(H)=\sum_{C\in\mathcal C(H)}|C|^3.\] Storage and equality-coupling burdens are reflected by quantities such as \[\Psi(H)=\sum_{S\in\mathcal S(H)}|S|^2.\] Choosing additional fill can change both the number of maximal cliques and their sizes: fewer coupling interfaces may be obtained at the price of larger dense blocks. Hence minimizing fill-edge count alone need not minimize either proxy or actual solver time.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A chordal extension trades the number of clique interfaces against dense block sizes; minimizing added edges alone need not minimize computational cost.
knowledge_statements.title: Fill-versus-Block-Size Tradeoffs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The qualitative tradeoff is plausible, but the cubic clique and quadratic separator proxies depend on the computational formulation and solver model. A direct source is required for these particular proxies and their scope.

children.title: Clique-Separator Coupling
children.top_down_role: Consistency interfaces induced by overlaps between neighboring cliques.

knowledge_statements.title: Clique-Separator Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separator equalities for matrix-valued clique variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every edge \(CD\in E(T)\), set \(S=C\cap D\) and impose \[X_C[S,S]=X_D[S,S].\] By the running-intersection property, equality on tree-edge separators implies equality of the corresponding principal submatrices for every pair of cliques containing the same entries. These local equalities are sufficient for the clique matrices to define one consistent partial symmetric matrix on the union of clique entry sets; constraints for all pairs of overlapping cliques are redundant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equality of neighboring clique matrices on clique-tree separators is sufficient to make all copies of shared matrix entries globally consistent.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is a clique tree of a chordal graph with clique variables \(X_C\in\mathbb S^{|C|}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X_C[S,S]=X_D[S,S]\) for every \(CD\in E(T)\), where \(S=C\cap D\), couples the clique variables globally.

notation.meaning: Separator associated with clique-tree edge CD.

knowledge_statements.title: Overlap Consistency Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact assembly criterion for independently introduced clique matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: There exists a partial symmetric matrix \(a\) on the chordal pattern satisfying \(a[C,C]=Y_C\) for every clique \(C\) if and only if, for every edge \(CD\in E(T)\), \[Y_C[S_{CD},S_{CD}]=Y_D[S_{CD},S_{CD}],\qquad S_{CD}=C\cap D.\] If each \(Y_C\succeq0\), the assembled partial matrix additionally belongs to the PSD-completable cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent clique matrices assemble into one partial matrix exactly when adjacent clique copies agree on their separator submatrices.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is a clique tree with clique matrices \(Y_C\in\mathbb S^{|C|}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{Y_C\}_{C\in V(T)}\) comes from one partial matrix iff adjacent cliques agree on every separator.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal–Dual Representation Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Adjoint correspondence between clique summation and clique principal-submatrix extraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Equip the product clique space and \(\mathbb S^{|V|}(E_H)\) with their trace inner products. For every \(Y\in\mathbb S^{|V|}(E_H)\), the adjoint of the clique-sum map is \[\mathcal A^*(Y)=(E_CYE_C^{\mathsf T})_{C\in\mathcal C}.\] Accordingly, \(\mathcal A(\prod_{C\in\mathcal C}\mathbb S_+^{|C|})\) is the sparse PSD decomposition cone, while its dual consists of sparse matrices whose extracted clique matrices \(E_CYE_C^{\mathsf T}\) are positive semidefinite, giving the chordal PSD-completion representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Clique summation and clique extraction are adjoint maps, so sparse PSD decomposition and clique-wise PSD completion form the corresponding primal-dual representation pair.
assumptions_latex: \(H=(V,E_H)\) is chordal with maximal cliques \(\mathcal C\).
\(\mathcal A((X_C)_C)=\sum_{C\in\mathcal C}E_C^{\mathsf T}X_CE_C\) maps clique matrices into \(\mathbb S^{|V|}(E_H)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal A^*(Y)=(E_CYE_C^{\mathsf T})_{C\in\mathcal C}\), yielding the decomposition-completion dual pair.

children.title: Low-Rank Constraint Data

notation.meaning: Full-column-rank basis for the range of the coefficient matrix.

source_refs.locator: 1.4.3 A dual view: Rank relaxation p. 16

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Every symmetric coefficient matrix \(A_i\) of rank \(r_i\) admits an exact compact factorization \[A_i=U_iH_iU_i^{\mathsf T},\] where \(U_i\in\mathbb R^{n\times r_i}\) has full column rank and \(H_i\in\mathbb S^{r_i}\) is nonsingular. For every \(X\in\mathbb S^n\), cyclicity of the trace gives \[\langle A_i,X\rangle=\langle H_i,U_i^{\mathsf T}XU_i\rangle.\] Thus an affine semidefinite constraint or objective can store and evaluate \(A_i\) through its range basis and small core without forming a dense \(n\)-by-\(n\) matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A symmetric rank-r coefficient matrix can be stored as a tall range basis and a small symmetric core, reducing its inner product to an r-dimensional compression.

children.title: Permutation-Symmetry Reduction
children.top_down_role: Reduction based on invariance under coordinate or index permutations.

knowledge_statements.title: Permutation-Symmetry Reduction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite permutation-invariant semidefinite programs reduced by Reynolds averaging.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G\) be a finite group of permutation matrices and let \(G\) act by \(X\mapsto P_gXP_g^{\mathsf T}\). Suppose an SDP has a convex feasible set \(\mathcal F\subseteq\mathbb S^n\) invariant under this action and an invariant linear objective \(\langle C,P_gXP_g^{\mathsf T}\rangle=\langle C,X\rangle\). For every \(X\in\mathcal F\), the Reynolds average \(\bar X=|G|^{-1}\sum_{g\in G}P_gXP_g^{\mathsf T}\) lies in \(\mathcal F\), has the same objective value, and satisfies \(P_g\bar XP_g^{\mathsf T}=\bar X\) for every \(g\in G\). Hence optimization may be restricted to permutation-invariant matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A permutation-invariant convex SDP always has an equally good feasible solution fixed by every permutation in the symmetry group.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is finite and represented by permutation matrices.
\(\mathcal F\) is convex and invariant under conjugation by \(G\).
The linear objective is invariant under the same action.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\inf_{X\in\mathcal F}\langle C,X\rangle=\inf_{X\in\mathcal F,\;P_gXP_g^{\mathsf T}=X\;\forall g}\langle C,X\rangle.\]

notation.meaning: Permutation matrix representing group element g.
Convex feasible set of the SDP.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: finite-group Reynolds averaging preserves invariant convex feasible sets and objectives

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite permutation-group averaging principle is mathematically precise and fits the leaf, but no inspectable citation is supplied.

children.title: Group-Symmetry Reduction
children.top_down_role: Reduction based on representations of finite or compact symmetry groups.

knowledge_statements.title: Group-Symmetry Reduction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite orthogonal-group reduction of invariant semidefinite programs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G\) be finite and let \(\rho:G\to O(n)\) be an orthogonal representation acting on \(\mathbb S^n\) by \(X\mapsto\rho(g)X\rho(g)^{\mathsf T}\). If a convex feasible set \(\mathcal F\) and a linear objective are invariant under this action, then averaging any feasible \(X\) gives \(\mathcal R_G(X)=|G|^{-1}\sum_{g\in G}\rho(g)X\rho(g)^{\mathsf T}\). This matrix is feasible, has the same objective value, and belongs to the fixed-point space \(\operatorname{Fix}(G)=\{Y:\rho(g)Y\rho(g)^{\mathsf T}=Y\ \forall g\in G\}\). Therefore the original SDP and its restriction to \(\mathcal F\cap\operatorname{Fix}(G)\) have equal optimal values.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite group-invariant convex SDP can be solved over the matrices fixed by the group action without changing its optimal value.
assumptions_latex: The feasible set is convex and group invariant.
The objective is linear and group invariant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\inf_{X\in\mathcal F}\langle C,X\rangle=\inf_{X\in\mathcal F\cap\operatorname{Fix}(G)}\langle C,X\rangle.\]

notation.meaning: Orthogonal representation of the finite group.
Fixed-point subspace for conjugation by the group.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Reynolds averaging is the standard finite-group convex symmetry reduction

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem is a correct finite-group symmetry reduction, but the record has no source with a specific locator.

children.title: Orbit Aggregation
children.top_down_role: Compression of variables or constraints according to symmetry orbits.

knowledge_statements.title: Orbit Aggregation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate representation of permutation-invariant matrices by pair orbits.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a finite permutation group \(G\) act on \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\), and let \(\mathcal O_1,\ldots,\mathcal O_r\) be its orbits on ordered index pairs. Define \((E_k)_{ij}=1\) when \((i,j)\in\mathcal O_k\) and \((E_k)_{ij}=0\) otherwise. A matrix \(X\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) satisfies \(P_gXP_g^{\mathsf T}=X\) for every \(g\in G\) if and only if it is constant on every pair orbit, equivalently \(X=\sum_{k=1}^r x_kE_k\). For symmetric matrices, coefficients belonging to transposed orbits must agree. Substitution of this expansion aggregates orbit-equivalent matrix entries into one scalar variable per relevant orbit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A permutation-invariant matrix is constant on each orbit of index pairs, so one coefficient can replace all entries in that orbit.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is a finite permutation group on \(n\) indices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[P_gXP_g^{\mathsf T}=X\ \forall g\in G\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad X\in\operatorname{span}\{E_1,\ldots,E_r\}.\]

notation.meaning: Indicator matrix of the kth pair orbit.
Aggregated coordinate associated with an orbit.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: fixed matrices of a permutation action are constant on pair orbits

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The orbit-indicator representation is mathematically sound and appropriately classified, but it lacks an inspectable source.

children.title: Invariant-Subspace Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Block structure obtained from invariant matrix subspaces.

knowledge_statements.title: Invariant-Subspace Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block decomposition induced by isotypic components of an orthogonal group representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\rho:G\to O(n)\) be a finite-dimensional orthogonal representation of a finite group, and decompose \(\mathbb R^n=V_1\oplus\cdots\oplus V_s\) into mutually orthogonal isotypic components. There is an orthogonal matrix \(U\), depending only on \(\rho\), such that every symmetric matrix \(X\) commuting with all \(\rho(g)\) has the form \(U^{\mathsf T}XU=\operatorname{diag}(X_1,\ldots,X_s)\), where \(X_j\) acts on \(V_j\). Consequently, \(X\succeq0\) if and only if \(X_j\succeq0\) for every \(j\). Thus a symmetry-restricted PSD constraint separates across the representation’s invariant components.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Group-fixed symmetric matrices split along orthogonal isotypic components, and positive semidefiniteness can be checked independently on the resulting blocks.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[U^{\mathsf T}XU=\operatorname{diag}(X_1,\ldots,X_s),\qquad X\succeq0\Longleftrightarrow X_j\succeq0\ \text{for all }j.\]

notation.meaning: An isotypic component of the representation.
Orthogonal change of basis adapted to the components.
Restriction of X to the jth component.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: orthogonal representations decompose into isotypic components preserved by the commutant

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The decomposition across isotypic components is correct at the stated granularity, but no representation-theory source and locator are provided.

children.title: Matrix-Algebra Block Diagonalization
children.top_down_role: Reduction through invariant matrix algebras and simultaneous block structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Matrix-Algebra Block Diagonalization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simultaneous reduction of a transpose-closed matrix algebra into common blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal A\subseteq\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be a finite-dimensional matrix algebra closed under transpose. Then \(\mathbb R^n\) admits an orthogonal direct sum of minimal common reducing subspaces \(V_1\oplus\cdots\oplus V_s\). For an orthogonal basis matrix \(U\) adapted to this sum, every \(A\in\mathcal A\) satisfies \(U^{\mathsf T}AU=\operatorname{diag}(A_1,\ldots,A_s)\). In particular, if an SDP’s symmetric data and variable are restricted to \(\mathcal A\), its PSD constraint is equivalent to the block constraints \(X_j\succeq0\) for all \(j\). Linear objectives and affine constraints transform by applying the same basis change to their coefficient matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A transpose-closed matrix algebra has common orthogonal reducing subspaces, turning one structured PSD constraint into independent smaller block constraints.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal A\) is a finite-dimensional real matrix algebra.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[U^{\mathsf T}\mathcal AU\subseteq\{\operatorname{diag}(A_1,\ldots,A_s)\},\qquad X\succeq0\Longleftrightarrow X_j\succeq0\ \forall j.\]
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: finite-dimensional transpose-closed matrix algebras are completely reducible by orthogonal reducing subspaces

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The simultaneous block-reduction claim fits the topic and is plausible for a transpose-closed finite-dimensional matrix algebra, but it requires a precise source.

children.title: Extremal-Eigenvalue Models
children.top_down_role: Optimization families involving largest or smallest eigenvalue behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Extremal-Eigenvalue Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: LMI epigraph and hypograph models for extreme eigenvalues of symmetric affine matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(A(x)=A_0+\sum_{i=1}^m x_iA_i\in\mathbb S^n\), the upper bound \(\lambda_{\max}(A(x))\le t\) is equivalent to \(tI-A(x)\succeq0\), while \(\lambda_{\min}(A(x))\ge s\) is equivalent to \(A(x)-sI\succeq0\). Hence minimizing the largest eigenvalue over a convex set \(C\) is the SDP \(\min\{t:x\in C,\ tI-A(x)\succeq0\}\). Maximizing the smallest eigenvalue is analogously \(\max\{s:x\in C,\ A(x)-sI\succeq0\}\), provided the remaining description of \(C\) is semidefinite representable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bounds on the largest or smallest eigenvalue of a symmetric affine matrix are exactly linear matrix inequalities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\lambda_{\max}(A(x))\le t\Longleftrightarrow A(x)\preceq tI,\qquad \lambda_{\min}(A(x))\ge s\Longleftrightarrow A(x)\succeq sI.\]

children.title: Eigenvalue-Sum Models
children.top_down_role: Models involving ordered partial sums of matrix eigenvalues.

knowledge_statements.title: Eigenvalue-Sum Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semidefinite representation of the sum of the largest eigenvalues.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb S^n\) have eigenvalues \(\lambda_1(A)\ge\cdots\ge\lambda_n(A)\), and fix \(k\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\). The Ky Fan sum of the largest \(k\) eigenvalues has the equivalent representations \(\sum_{i=1}^k\lambda_i(A)=\max\{\langle A,P\rangle:0\preceq P\preceq I,\ \operatorname{tr}P=k\}\) and \(\sum_{i=1}^k\lambda_i(A)=\min\{kt+\operatorname{tr}Z:Z\succeq0,\ Z\succeq A-tI\}\). If \(A=A(x)\) is affine, the second formula supplies an SDP epigraph for minimizing this eigenvalue sum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The sum of the largest k eigenvalues equals both a projector relaxation maximum and an explicit semidefinite minimization formula.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\sum_{i=1}^k\lambda_i(A)=\min_{t\in\mathbb R,\,Z\succeq0}\{kt+\operatorname{tr}Z:Z\succeq A-tI\}.\]

children.title: Spectral-Order Models
children.top_down_role: Matrix comparison families expressed through spectral ordering.

knowledge_statements.title: Spectral-Order Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Löwner-order constraints expressed through extremal eigenvalues and LMIs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For symmetric affine matrix pencils \(A(x),B(x)\in\mathbb S^n\), the spectral-order constraint \(A(x)\preceq B(x)\) is equivalent to requiring every eigenvalue of \(B(x)-A(x)\) to be nonnegative. Equivalently, \(\lambda_{\max}(A(x)-B(x))\le0\), or directly \(B(x)-A(x)\succeq0\). More generally, \(\alpha I\preceq A(x)\preceq\beta I\) is equivalent to the pair of LMIs \(A(x)-\alpha I\succeq0\) and \(\beta I-A(x)\succeq0\), which enforces that the spectrum of \(A(x)\) lies in \([\alpha,\beta]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Löwner ordering of symmetric affine matrices is equivalent to a PSD difference, or to a largest-eigenvalue inequality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[A(x)\preceq B(x)\Longleftrightarrow B(x)-A(x)\succeq0\Longleftrightarrow\lambda_{\max}(A(x)-B(x))\le0.\]

notation.meaning: Löwner partial order on symmetric matrices.

children.title: Eigenvalue-Multiplicity Regimes

knowledge_statements.title: Eigenvalue-Multiplicity Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Subdifferential and differentiability of the maximum eigenvalue at repeated eigenvalues.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb S^n\), let its largest eigenvalue have multiplicity \(r\), and let \(U\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\) have orthonormal columns spanning the corresponding eigenspace. The convex subdifferential of the maximum-eigenvalue function is \(\partial\lambda_{\max}(A)=\{UHU^{\mathsf T}:H\in\mathbb S^r,\ H\succeq0,\ \operatorname{tr}H=1\}\). Thus \(\lambda_{\max}\) is differentiable at \(A\) exactly when \(r=1\); in that case, for a unit top eigenvector \(u\), its gradient is \(uu^{\mathsf T}\). Repeated top eigenvalues therefore create a set-valued first-order model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The largest-eigenvalue function is differentiable exactly at a simple top eigenvalue; multiplicity yields a convex set of eigenspace-supported subgradients.
assumptions_latex: The columns of \(U\) orthonormally span the top eigenspace.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\partial\lambda_{\max}(A)=\{UHU^{\mathsf T}:H\succeq0,\ \operatorname{tr}H=1\},\qquad \lambda_{\max}\text{ is differentiable at }A\Longleftrightarrow r=1.\]

notation.meaning: Orthonormal basis matrix for the top eigenspace.

children.title: Determinant-Maximization Models
children.top_down_role: Positive-definite matrix models using determinant-based volume criteria.

knowledge_statements.title: Determinant-Maximization Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex reformulation of positive-definite determinant maximization through the logarithm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F(x)=F_0+\sum_{i=1}^m x_iF_i\in\mathbb S^n\), and let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) be convex. On the domain \(D=\{x\in C:F(x)\succ0\}\), strict monotonicity of the logarithm gives \(\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in D}\det F(x)=\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in D}\log\det F(x)\). Because \(X\mapsto\log\det X\) is concave on \(\mathbb S_{++}^n\), maximizing \(\log\det F(x)\) over convex constraints is a convex optimization model, equivalently minimizing \(-\log\det F(x)\). The determinant objective itself need not be concave, despite having the same maximizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maximizing a positive-definite determinant has the same solutions as maximizing log determinant, whose negative is a convex objective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in D}\det F(x)=\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in D}\log\det F(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in D}-\log\det F(x).\]

source_refs.locator: 11 Semidefinite models p. 381

children.title: Log-Determinant Models
children.top_down_role: Concave matrix-objective models using logarithmic determinant criteria.

knowledge_statements.title: Log-Determinant Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex modeling and differential structure of the log-determinant objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On the positive-definite cone \(\mathbb S_{++}^n\), define \(f(X)=\log\det X\). This function is strictly concave, with differential \(Df(X)[H]=\operatorname{tr}(X^{-1}H)\) and second differential \(D^2f(X)[H,H]=-\operatorname{tr}(X^{-1}HX^{-1}H)\le0\). Consequently, if \(F(x)\) is symmetric affine and constrained to be positive definite, then \(x\mapsto-\log\det F(x)\) is convex on its domain. Thus minimizing a negative log determinant, or equivalently maximizing a log determinant, is compatible with convex affine and LMI constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Log determinant is strictly concave on positive-definite matrices, so its negative composed with an affine matrix pencil is convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[Df(X)[H]=\operatorname{tr}(X^{-1}H),\qquad D^2f(X)[H,H]=-\operatorname{tr}(X^{-1}HX^{-1}H)\le0.\]

source_refs.locator: 11 Semidefinite models p. 381

children.title: Positive-Definite Domain Boundary
children.top_down_role: Domain behavior as matrix arguments approach singularity.

knowledge_statements.title: Positive-Definite Domain Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Singular-boundary behavior of log determinant and its gradient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X_k\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\) converge to a singular matrix \(\bar X\in\mathbb S_+^n\). Continuity of ordered eigenvalues gives \(\lambda_{\min}(X_k)\to0\), while all eigenvalues remain bounded above because \(X_k\to\bar X\). Hence \(\log\det X_k=\sum_{i=1}^n\log\lambda_i(X_k)\to-\infty\). Moreover, \(\|\nabla(-\log\det X_k)\|_2=\|X_k^{-1}\|_2=1/\lambda_{\min}(X_k)\to+\infty\). Therefore the log-determinant objective is finite and differentiable only in the cone interior and cannot be extended as a finite continuous function to singular PSD matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approaching a singular PSD matrix from the positive-definite cone sends log determinant to negative infinity and the negative-log gradient norm to infinity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\log\det X_k\to-\infty,\qquad \|X_k^{-1}\|_2=\lambda_{\min}(X_k)^{-1}\to+\infty.\]

assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\) when the inverse-shape parametrization is used.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric and Gaussian interpretations of determinant objectives for positive-definite matrices, with the matrix parametrization stated explicitly.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\) and \(E(P,c)=\{c+P^{1/2}u:\lVert u\rVert_2\le1\}\). Then \(\operatorname{vol}(E(P,c))=\operatorname{vol}(B_2^n)\det(P)^{1/2}\). If \(X\sim\mathcal N(c,P)\), then \(h(X)=\tfrac12\log\det P+\tfrac n2\log(2\pi e)\). Thus maximizing \(\log\det P\) maximizes both the volume of this shape-parametrized ellipsoid and the entropy of this Gaussian. In the inverse-shape parametrization \(E_{\mathrm{inv}}(A,c)=\{x:\lVert A(x-c)\rVert_2\le1\}\), where \(A\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\), the volume is \(\operatorname{vol}(B_2^n)/\det A\), so maximizing \(\log\det A\) instead minimizes volume. Likewise, for the precision matrix \(J=P^{-1}\), maximizing \(\log\det J\) minimizes Gaussian entropy up to an additive constant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a shape or covariance matrix, log determinant increases ellipsoid volume and Gaussian entropy. For an inverse-shape or precision matrix, the sign is reversed, so maximizing log determinant minimizes volume or entropy.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F(x)=F_0+\sum_{j=1}^m x_jF_j\in\mathbb S^n\). For fixed \(t\ge1\), the conditions \(F(x)\succ0\) and \(\kappa_2(F(x))\le t\) hold exactly when there exists \(\mu>0\) such that \(\mu I\preceq F(x)\preceq t\mu I\). Hence minimizing \(\kappa_2(F(x))\) over an LMI-representable convex set \(\mathcal X\) is quasiconvex: feasibility at each trial value \(t\) is an SDP feasibility problem in \((x,\mu)\). Given a finite bracket containing the optimal value, bisection approximates that value to any prescribed positive tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A spectral condition-number bound is equivalent to sandwiching the matrix between two scaled identity matrices. Each trial bound is an SDP feasibility problem, and a bracketed bisection approximates the optimum to a chosen tolerance.

knowledge_statements.title: Matrix-Norm Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semidefinite epigraph of the spectral norm for affine rectangular matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(A(x)=A_0+\sum_{j=1}^m x_jA_j\in\mathbb R^{p\times q}\) and \(t\ge0\), the spectral-norm constraint \(\lVert A(x)\rVert_2\le t\) is equivalent to the linear matrix inequality \[\begin{pmatrix}tI_p&A(x)\\A(x)^\mathsf T&tI_q\end{pmatrix}\succeq0.\] Therefore minimizing the induced Euclidean matrix norm of an affine matrix map, possibly subject to additional LMIs in \(x\), is a semidefinite program with epigraph variable \(t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The spectral norm of an affine rectangular matrix has an exact symmetric block-LMI epigraph.
assumptions_latex: \(A(x)\) is affine in the decision vector \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert A(x)\rVert_2\le t\iff\begin{pmatrix}tI_p&A(x)\\A(x)^\mathsf T&tI_q\end{pmatrix}\succeq0\).

children.title: Diagonal Scaling Models

knowledge_statements.title: Diagonal Scaling Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quasiconvex diagonal preconditioning model for a symmetric positive-definite matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\). For fixed \(t\ge1\), there exists a positive diagonal scaling \(D\) satisfying \(\kappa_2(D^{-1/2}AD^{-1/2})\le t\) if and only if there exists a positive diagonal matrix \(W\) such that \(W\preceq A\preceq tW\). Indeed, a feasible spectral lower bound can be absorbed into \(W\). Thus optimal diagonal conditioning is obtained by bisection on \(t\), with each feasibility test consisting of LMIs and positivity constraints on the diagonal entries of \(W\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Diagonal preconditioning admits a quasiconvex LMI model by sandwiching the original matrix between a diagonal matrix and its scalar multiple.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists D\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\text{ diagonal}:\kappa_2(D^{-1/2}AD^{-1/2})\le t\iff\exists W\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\text{ diagonal}:W\preceq A\preceq tW\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Optimal Diagonally Scaled Spectral Norm and Its GEVP Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the smallest spectral norm obtainable by diagonal similarity scaling and represents its value through a diagonal positive-definite matrix inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(M\in\mathbf C^{n\times n}\), define
\[
\nu(M):=\inf\left\{\lVert DMD^{-1}\rVert_2: D\in\mathbf C^{n\times n}\text{ is diagonal and nonsingular}\right\}.
\]
Then
\[
\nu(M)=\inf\left\{\gamma\ge 0:\exists\,P\succ0\text{ real diagonal such that }M^*PM\preceq\gamma^2P\right\}.
\]
Equivalently, the same infimal value is obtained by minimizing \(\gamma>0\) subject to a real diagonal \(P\succ0\) and \(M^*PM\prec\gamma^2P\), which is a GEVP formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a complex square matrix M, the optimal diagonally scaled norm is the infimum of the spectral norms of D M D inverse over nonsingular diagonal D. Its value is also the infimum of nonnegative gamma for which a positive-definite real diagonal P satisfies M-star P M at most gamma squared P. Replacing the non-strict inequality by a strict one gives the corresponding GEVP with the same infimal value.
assumptions_latex: D\in\mathbf C^{n\times n}\text{ is diagonal and nonsingular}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \nu(M)=\inf_D\lVert DMD^{-1}\rVert_2=\inf\{\gamma\ge0:\exists P\succ0\text{ real diagonal},\ M^*PM\preceq\gamma^2P\},\text{ with the same infimal value under }M^*PM\prec\gamma^2P.

knowledge_statements.title: Structured Scaling Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: LMI conditioning model with scaling restricted to a prescribed matrix subspace or cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\), and let \(\mathcal S\subseteq\mathbb S^n\) be a convex cone encoding a scaling structure, such as block-diagonal or repeated-block matrices. For fixed \(t\ge1\), a structured scaling with condition number at most \(t\) exists exactly when one can find \(W\in\mathcal S\cap\mathbb S_{++}^n\) satisfying \(W\preceq A\preceq tW\). If membership in \(\mathcal S\) is given by linear equalities and LMIs, the trial-value problem is an SDP, so the best structured bound is quasiconvex in \(t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restricting the comparison matrix to a convex structural cone yields a quasiconvex SDP model for structured conditioning.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal S\) is a convex cone with an LMI representation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{W\in\mathcal S\cap\mathbb S_{++}^n}\kappa_2(W^{-1/2}AW^{-1/2})=\inf\{t\ge1:\exists W\in\mathcal S\cap\mathbb S_{++}^n,\ W\preceq A\preceq tW\}\).

notation.meaning: Prescribed convex cone of structured symmetric scalings.

children.title: Scaling Feasibility Boundaries

knowledge_statements.title: Scaling Feasibility Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary separating finite structured condition bounds from infeasible or singular scaling instances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal S\subseteq\mathbb S^n\) be a cone closed under positive scaling and define \(\gamma_{\mathcal S}(A)=\inf\{t\ge1:\exists W\in\mathcal S\cap\mathbb S_{++}^n,\ W\preceq A\preceq tW\}\). If \(A\) is singular, then \(\gamma_{\mathcal S}(A)=+\infty\), because \(W\succ0\) and \(W\preceq A\) cannot both hold. If \(A\succ0\) and \(\mathcal S\cap\mathbb S_{++}^n\ne\varnothing\), positive rescaling of any such \(W\) gives a finite sandwich. Thus loss of positive definiteness or absence of an admissible positive-definite scaling is the feasibility boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite structured conditioning requires both a positive-definite target matrix and at least one positive-definite matrix in the scaling cone.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal S\) is closed under multiplication by positive scalars.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\gamma_{\mathcal S}(A)<+\infty\iff A\succ0\text{ and }\mathcal S\cap\mathbb S_{++}^n\ne\varnothing\).

knowledge_statements.title: Inner Ellipsoidal Approximation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact containment model for an ellipsoid inscribed in a polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:a_i^\mathsf Tx\le b_i,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\) and \(E(c,B)=\{c+Bu:\lVert u\rVert_2\le1\}\), where \(B\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\). Then \(E(c,B)\subseteq K\) if and only if \(a_i^\mathsf Tc+\lVert B^\mathsf Ta_i\rVert_2\le b_i\) for every \(i\). These second-order-cone constraints, together with a concave objective such as maximizing \(\log\det B\), form a convex model for an inner ellipsoidal approximation of \(K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An ellipsoid lies inside a polyhedron exactly when every facet supports its center plus the ellipsoid’s directional radius.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is represented by finitely many affine inequalities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(E(c,B)\subseteq K\iff a_i^\mathsf Tc+\lVert B^\mathsf Ta_i\rVert_2\le b_i\text{ for all }i\).

notation.meaning: Polyhedron to be approximated from within.

knowledge_statements.title: Outer Ellipsoidal Approximation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: LMI containment model for an ellipsoid enclosing finitely many points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For points \(x_1,\ldots,x_m\in\mathbb R^n\), let \(E(c,P)=\{x:(x-c)^\mathsf TP^{-1}(x-c)\le1\}\) with \(P\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\). The containment \(\{x_1,\ldots,x_m\}\subseteq E(c,P)\) holds if and only if, for every \(i\), \[\begin{pmatrix}P&x_i-c\\(x_i-c)^\mathsf T&1\end{pmatrix}\succeq0.\] The equivalence follows from the Schur complement. Thus these block LMIs provide a semidefinite description of outer ellipsoidal approximation for a finite point set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A point belongs to a positive-definite ellipsoid exactly when a corresponding bordered matrix is positive semidefinite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_i\in E(c,P)\iff\begin{pmatrix}P&x_i-c\\(x_i-c)^\mathsf T&1\end{pmatrix}\succeq0\).

notation.meaning: Ellipsoid centered at c with shape matrix P.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Löwner–John Approximation for Centrally Symmetric Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The sharp improvement of the Löwner–John containment factor under central symmetry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be convex, bounded, have nonempty interior, and be centrally symmetric about \(x_0\). If \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{lj}}\) is the minimum-volume ellipsoid containing \(C\), then \[x_0+\frac1{\sqrt n}\bigl(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{lj}}-x_0\bigr)\subseteq C\subseteq\mathcal E_{\mathrm{lj}}.\] The factor \(1/\sqrt n\) is sharp: for \(C=[-1,1]^n\), the Löwner–John ellipsoid is the Euclidean ball of radius \(\sqrt n\), so any larger concentric scaling than \(1/\sqrt n\) is not contained in \(C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a bounded full-dimensional convex set that is centrally symmetric, its minimum-volume enclosing ellipsoid need only be shrunk by one over the square root of the dimension to lie inside the set. This factor is sharp, as shown by the cube.
assumptions_latex: C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\text{ is convex and bounded}
\mathcal E_{\mathrm{lj}}\text{ is the minimum-volume ellipsoid containing }C
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_0+\frac1{\sqrt n}(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{lj}}-x_0)\subseteq C\subseteq\mathcal E_{\mathrm{lj}},\qquad \frac1{\sqrt n}\text{ is sharp over this class.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Minimum-Volume Ellipsoid Enclosing a Finite Union of Ellipsoids
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Determinant-maximization formulation for the outer ellipsoid of the convex hull of finitely many affine-image ellipsoids.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let W_i=\{A_i u+c_i:\|u\|_2\le 1\}\subset\mathbb R^n for i=1,\ldots,m, and suppose W=\operatorname{conv}(\bigcup_{i=1}^m W_i) has nonempty interior. For Y\in\mathbb S_{++}^n, z\in\mathbb R^n, and \lambda_i\in\mathbb R, define E(Y,z)=\{x:(x-Y^{-1}z)^TY^2(x-Y^{-1}z)\le1\}. Then W\subseteq E(Y,z) exactly when, for every i,
\[
\begin{pmatrix}
I_n&Yc_i-z&YA_i\\
(Yc_i-z)^T&1-\lambda_i&0\\
A_i^TY&0&\lambda_iI_{k_i}
\end{pmatrix}\succeq0.
\]
Consequently, the minimum-volume ellipsoid containing W is obtained by maximizing \det(Y), equivalently \det(Y)^{1/n}, subject to these containment LMIs. If (Y_*,z_*,\lambda_*) is optimal, its center is Y_*^{-1}z_* and its shape matrix is Y_*^2.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For affine-image ellipsoids whose convex hull is full-dimensional, containment in a candidate outer ellipsoid is characterized by one LMI per input ellipsoid. Maximizing the determinant of the candidate's positive-definite shape factor minimizes its volume.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: E_* =\{x:(x-Y_*^{-1}z_*)^TY_*^2(x-Y_*^{-1}z_*)\le1\}\text{ is the minimum-volume ellipsoid containing }W.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Semidefinite formulation of the minimum-volume enclosing ellipsoid of a polytope
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Applies to a full-dimensional polytope whose vertices are denoted by \(x_1,\ldots,x_m\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S=\operatorname{conv}\{x_1,\ldots,x_m\}\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) have nonempty interior. Consider \[\max_{t,Z,z,s}t\quad\text{s.t.}\quad t\le(\det Z)^{1/n},\quad Z\succeq0,\quad \begin{pmatrix}s&z^\top\\z&Z\end{pmatrix}\succeq0,\quad x_i^\top Zx_i-2x_i^\top z+s\le1\quad(i=1,\ldots,m),\] where \(Z\in\mathbb{S}^n\), \(z\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and \(t,s\in\mathbb{R}\). For an optimal solution \((t_*,Z_*,z_*,s_*)\), set \(D_*=Z_*\) and \(c_*=Z_*^{-1}z_*\). Then \(E_*=\{x:(x-c_*)^\top D_*(x-c_*)\le1\}\) is the minimum-volume ellipsoid containing \(S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a full-dimensional polytope specified by its vertices, a lifted semidefinite program maximizes the determinant of the inverse ellipsoid shape while enforcing containment of every vertex. The optimal quadratic shape and center recover the minimum-volume enclosing ellipsoid.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: D_*=Z_*,\quad c_*=Z_*^{-1}z_*,\quad E_*=\{x:(x-c_*)^\top D_*(x-c_*)\le1\}\text{ is the minimum-volume ellipsoid containing }S.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Logarithmic barrier for the maximum-volume inscribed ellipsoid model
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the model-specific barrier on the strict interior of the convex reformulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
On the strict interior given by
\[
G\succ0,\qquad \tau+\ln\det G>0,\qquad b_i-\langle a_i,v\rangle>\|Ga_i\|\quad(i=1,\ldots,m),
\]
define
\[
F(G,v,\tau)=-\ln\det G-\ln\bigl(\tau+\ln\det G\bigr)-\sum_{i=1}^m\ln\!\left((b_i-\langle a_i,v\rangle)^2-\|Ga_i\|^2\right).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The strict interior of the maximum-volume inscribed-ellipsoid formulation has a logarithmic barrier consisting of a determinant term, a log-determinant epigraph-slack term, and squared norm-slack terms for the containment constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F(G,v,\tau)=-\ln\det G-\ln\bigl(\tau+\ln\det G\bigr)-\sum_{i=1}^m\ln\!\left((b_i-\langle a_i,v\rangle)^2-\|Ga_i\|^2\right)

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition and shape-matrix representation for ellipsoids centered at a fixed interior point of a polytope.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Specializes maximum-volume inner ellipsoidal approximation to a finite intersection of full-dimensional ellipsoids having nonempty interior.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convex reformulation of the maximum-volume inscribed ellipsoid problem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives the ellipsoid representation, exact half-space containment conditions, volume identity, and equivalent convex log-determinant formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
Q=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:\langle a_i,x\rangle\le b_i,\ i=1,\ldots,m\},\qquad \operatorname{int}Q\ne\varnothing.
\]
For $G\in\operatorname{int}\mathbb{S}_+^n$ and $v\in\operatorname{int}Q$, define
\[
W(G,v)=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:\|G^{-1}(x-v)\|\le1\}=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:\langle G^{-2}(x-v),x-v\rangle\le1\}.
\]
Then
\[
\operatorname{vol}_nW(G,v)=\operatorname{vol}_nB_2(0,1)\det G
\]
and
\[
W(G,v)\subseteq Q\iff \|Ga_i\|\le b_i-\langle a_i,v\rangle\quad(i=1,\ldots,m).
\]
Consequently, maximizing the volume of an ellipsoid contained in $Q$ is equivalent to
\[
\min_{G\in\mathbb{S}_+^n,\,v\in\mathbb{R}^n,\,\tau\in\mathbb{R}}
\left\{\tau:-\ln\det G\le\tau,\ \|Ga_i\|\le b_i-\langle a_i,v\rangle,\ i=1,\ldots,m\right\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a full-dimensional polyhedron, an ellipsoid with center v and positive-definite shape matrix G is contained in the polyhedron exactly when every transformed half-space normal satisfies the displayed norm bound. Since the ellipsoid's volume is proportional to det G, maximum volume is equivalent to the stated convex log-determinant epigraph problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: W(G,v)\subseteq Q\iff \|Ga_i\|\le b_i-\langle a_i,v\rangle\ (i=1,\ldots,m),\quad \max\{\operatorname{vol}_nW(G,v):W(G,v)\subseteq Q\}\equiv\min\{\tau:-\ln\det G\le\tau,\ \|Ga_i\|\le b_i-\langle a_i,v\rangle\}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Efficiency of Maximum-Volume Inscribed Ellipsoids
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dimension-dependent outer coverage obtained by expanding a maximum-volume inscribed ellipsoid, with an improved factor for centrally symmetric sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be convex, bounded, and have nonempty interior, and let \(\mathcal E_{\max}\subseteq C\) be a maximum-volume inscribed ellipsoid with center \(x_0\). Then \[\mathcal E_{\max}\subseteq C\subseteq x_0+n\bigl(\mathcal E_{\max}-x_0\bigr).\] If \(C\) is centrally symmetric, then \[\mathcal E_{\max}\subseteq C\subseteq x_0+\sqrt n\bigl(\mathcal E_{\max}-x_0\bigr).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Expanding a maximum-volume inscribed ellipsoid about its center by the dimension covers any bounded full-dimensional convex set. For a centrally symmetric set, expansion by the square root of the dimension suffices.
assumptions_latex: C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\text{ is convex and bounded}
\mathcal E_{\max}\text{ is a maximum-volume ellipsoid contained in }C
x_0\text{ is the center of }\mathcal E_{\max}

knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic Containment Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact scalar-multiplier certificate for containment between two nondegenerate ellipsoids.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(i=1,2\), let \(E_i=\{x:q_i(x)\le0\}\), where \(q_i(x)=(x-c_i)^\mathsf TP_i^{-1}(x-c_i)-1\) and \(P_i\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\). Define \(Q_i\in\mathbb S^{n+1}\) by \(q_i(x)=\begin{pmatrix}x\\1\end{pmatrix}^{\!\mathsf T}Q_i\begin{pmatrix}x\\1\end{pmatrix}\). Then \(E_1\subseteq E_2\) if and only if there exists \(\tau\ge0\) such that \(\tau Q_1-Q_2\succeq0\). The scalar \(\tau\), together with this positive-semidefinite matrix inequality, is a directly verifiable containment certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Containment of one nondegenerate ellipsoid in another is certified exactly by one nonnegative scalar multiplier and a matrix inequality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(E_1\subseteq E_2\iff\exists\tau\ge0:\tau Q_1-Q_2\succeq0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Single-Constraint Lossless Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Real finite-dimensional S-lemma with one strictly feasible quadratic constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q_0,q_1:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be quadratic functions, and suppose there exists \(\bar x\in\mathbb R^n\) with \(q_1(\bar x)<0\). Then the implication \(q_1(x)\le0\Rightarrow q_0(x)\le0\) for every \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) holds if and only if there exists a scalar \(\tau\ge0\) such that \(q_0(x)\le\tau q_1(x)\) for every \(x\in\mathbb R^n\). In homogeneous matrix form, the latter global quadratic inequality is one positive-semidefinite matrix constraint, so the scalar-multiplier S-procedure is lossless in this regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With one strictly feasible quadratic constraint, a quadratic implication is equivalent to an exact nonnegative scalar-multiplier certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(q_0\) and \(q_1\) are real quadratic functions on \(\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bigl[\forall x,\ q_1(x)\le0\Rightarrow q_0(x)\le0\bigr]\iff\bigl[\exists\tau\ge0,\ \forall x,\ q_0(x)-\tau q_1(x)\le0\bigr]\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The real finite-dimensional one-constraint S-lemma is stated with the appropriate strict-feasibility hypothesis and correct multiplier sign, and theorem is the correct content kind. However, no source reference is supplied for this nontrivial exact losslessness theorem; an authoritative theorem, section, or page locator is required before candidate-review acceptance.

knowledge_statements.title: Multiple-Constraint S-Procedure Variants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar-multiplier sufficient condition for several quadratic antecedents.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(m\in\mathbb N\), and for \(i=0,\ldots,m\) let \(q_i:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be given by \(q_i(x)=x^{\mathsf T}A_i x+2b_i^{\mathsf T}x+c_i\), where \(A_i\in\mathbb S^n\), \(b_i\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(c_i\in\mathbb R\). If there exist multipliers \(\lambda_i\geq0\), \(i=1,\ldots,m\), such that
\[
q_0(x)-\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_iq_i(x)\geq0\qquad\text{for every }x\in\mathbb R^n,
\]
then
\[
q_1(x)\geq0,\ldots,q_m(x)\geq0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad q_0(x)\geq0.
\]
Equivalently, this sufficient condition is the linear matrix inequality
\[
\begin{bmatrix}A_0&b_0\\b_0^{\mathsf T}&c_0\end{bmatrix}-\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i\begin{bmatrix}A_i&b_i\\b_i^{\mathsf T}&c_i\end{bmatrix}\succeq0.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonnegative scalar multipliers provide an LMI certificate that several quadratic inequalities imply another quadratic inequality; for multiple constraints, this certificate need not be necessary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q_i(x)\geq0\ (i=1,\ldots,m)\Longrightarrow q_0(x)\geq0\).

notation.meaning: Real quadratic functions defining the implication.

knowledge_statements.title: Matrix S-Procedure Variants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loewner-order extension using scalar multipliers and matrix-valued quadratic maps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(i=0,ots,m\), let \(F_i:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb S^r\) be matrix-valued quadratic maps. A sufficient matrix S-procedure certificate for
\[
F_1(x)\succeq0,ots,F_m(x)\succeq0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad F_0(x)\succeq0
\]
is the existence of scalars \(\lambda_i\geq0\) satisfying
\[
F_0(x)-\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_iF_i(x)\succeq0\qquad\text{for every }x\in\mathbb R^n.
\]
Indeed, at any point satisfying the antecedent, the subtracted sum is positive semidefinite, so the displayed global inequality forces the required Loewner-order conclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A globally positive-semidefinite scalar combination of matrix quadratic maps certifies the corresponding matrix implication.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_i(x)\succeq0\ (i=1,ots,m)\Longrightarrow F_0(x)\succeq0\).

notation.meaning: Real symmetric matrices of order r.

children.title: Lossless Structured Regimes

knowledge_statements.title: Lossless Structured Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical lossless single-constraint regime under strict feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(q_0,q_1:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be quadratic functions, and suppose there exists \(\bar x\in\mathbb R^n\) with \(q_1(\bar x)>0\). Then the implication
\[
q_1(x)\geq0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad q_0(x)\geq0
\]
holds for every \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) if and only if there exists \(\lambda\geq0\) such that
\[
q_0(x)-\lambda q_1(x)\geq0
\]
for every \(x\in\mathbb R^n\). Thus, under the strict-feasibility hypothesis, the scalar S-procedure introduces no conservatism for one quadratic constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With one strictly feasible quadratic constraint, the scalar S-procedure is both sufficient and necessary.
assumptions_latex: \(q_0\) and \(q_1\) are real quadratic functions on \(\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q_1\geq0\Rightarrow q_0\geq0\iff\exists\lambda\geq0:\ q_0-\lambda q_1\geq0\text{ on }\mathbb R^n\).

notation.meaning: Strictly feasible point for the antecedent constraint.

children.title: Conservative Variant Boundaries

knowledge_statements.title: Conservative Variant Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete failure of necessity for a multiple-constraint scalar S-procedure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
On \(\mathbb R^2\), define \(q_1(x)=x_1\), \(q_2(x)=-x_1\), and \(q_0(x)=x_1x_2\). Then
\[
q_1(x)\geq0,\u00ad q_2(x)\geq0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad q_0(x)=0,
\]
but there do not exist \(\lambda_1,\lambda_2\geq0\) such that
\[
q_0(x)-\lambda_1q_1(x)-\lambda_2q_2(x)\geq0
\qquad\text{for every }x\in\mathbb R^2.
\]
Thus the nonnegative scalar-multiplier certificate for multiple antecedent constraints need not be necessary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two opposing affine constraints give a valid quadratic implication for which no nonnegative scalar-multiplier certificate exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q_1\geq0,\ q_2\geq0\Rightarrow q_0\geq0\), but \(\nexists\lambda_1,\lambda_2\geq0\) with \(q_0-\lambda_1q_1-\lambda_2q_2\geq0\) globally.

notation.meaning: Quadratic or affine functions in the counterexample.

knowledge_statements.title: Robust Multiplier Variants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic-separation certificate for a family of admissible uncertainty matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\boldsymbol\Delta\subseteq\mathbb R^{p\times q}\) be an uncertainty family, and let \(\mathcal P\subseteq\mathbb S^{p+q}\) satisfy
\[
\begin{bmatrix}I\\ \Delta\end{bmatrix}^{\!\mathsf T}\Pi
\begin{bmatrix}I\\ \Delta\end{bmatrix}\succeq0
\quad\text{for every }\Delta\in\boldsymbol\Delta\text{ and every }\Pi\in\mathcal P.
\]
Let \(\xi\in\mathbb R^N\), \(M\in\mathbb R^{(p+q)\times N}\), and \(H\in\mathbb S^N\), with uncertainty graph coordinates defined by \(\begin{bmatrix}v\\w\end{bmatrix}=M\xi\) and \(w=\Delta v\). If some \(\Pi\in\mathcal P\) satisfies
\[
H+M^{\mathsf T}\Pi M\prec0,
\]
then \(\xi^{\mathsf T}H\xi<0\) for every nonzero \(\xi\) compatible with every \(\Delta\in\boldsymbol\Delta\). The multiplier and strict LMI constitute a robust quadratic certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multiplier valid on every admissible uncertainty graph converts a strict nominal LMI into a uniform robust quadratic certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H+M^{\mathsf T}\Pi M\prec0\Longrightarrow \xi^{\mathsf T}H\xi<0\) on every admissible uncertainty graph.

notation.meaning: Family of multipliers valid on all admissible uncertainty graphs.
Nominal map to uncertainty graph coordinates.

knowledge_statements.title: Full-Block Multiplier Variants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unrestricted symmetric multipliers acting jointly on an uncertainty block's graph variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For an admissible uncertainty matrix \(\Delta\in\mathbb R^{p\times q}\) with \(w=\Delta v\), a full-block multiplier is a symmetric matrix
\[
\Pi=\begin{bmatrix}\Pi_{11}&\Pi_{12}\\\Pi_{12}^{\mathsf T}&\Pi_{22}\end{bmatrix}\in\mathbb S^{q+p}
\]
whose blocks are not required to be diagonal, scalar, or repeated and which satisfies
\[
\begin{bmatrix}I\\ \Delta\end{bmatrix}^{\!\mathsf T}
\Pi
\begin{bmatrix}I\\ \Delta\end{bmatrix}\succeq0
\qquad\text{for every admissible }\Delta.
\]
The off-diagonal block \(\Pi_{12}\) and dense diagonal blocks permit joint quadratic coupling among all input and output coordinates of the uncertainty block.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A full-block multiplier is a dense symmetric quadratic form that is nonnegative on every graph of the specified uncertainty block.
assumptions_latex: \(\Delta\in\mathbb R^{p\times q}\) belongs to a specified admissible family.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Pi\) is valid for the full block when its unrestricted blocks satisfy the graph inequality for every admissible \(\Delta\).

notation.meaning: Input and output coordinates of the uncertainty block.

knowledge_statements.title: Uncertainty-Structure Matching
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplier structure should preserve independently varying uncertainty blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Delta=\operatorname{diag}(\Delta_1,\ldots,\Delta_s)\), where the conformable blocks vary independently over families \(\boldsymbol\Delta_i\). If each \(\Pi_i\) satisfies
\[
\begin{bmatrix}I\\ \Delta_i\end{bmatrix}^{\!\mathsf T}\Pi_i
\begin{bmatrix}I\\ \Delta_i\end{bmatrix}\succeq0
\qquad\text{for every }\Delta_i\in\boldsymbol\Delta_i,
\]
then, after arranging graph coordinates blockwise, \(\Pi=\operatorname{diag}(\Pi_1,\ldots,\Pi_s)\) is valid for \(\boldsymbol\Delta\). Repeated or coupled blocks may instead share multiplier variables consistent with their coupling. Entries mixing independently varying blocks require separate justification and do not follow from the individual graph inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Block-diagonal uncertainty admits block-matched multipliers, while cross-block multiplier terms require additional coupling information.
assumptions_latex: The conformable blocks \(\Delta_i\) vary independently in \(\boldsymbol\Delta_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Pi_i\text{ valid for }\boldsymbol\Delta_i\ (i=1,\ldots,s)\Longrightarrow\operatorname{diag}(\Pi_1,\ldots,\Pi_s)\text{ valid for }\boldsymbol\Delta\).

notation.meaning: Multiplier matched to the corresponding block.

knowledge_statements.title: Multiplier Conservatism Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Restricted multiplier cones can fail despite existence of an unrestricted separator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm r}\subseteq\mathcal P_{\mathrm a}\subseteq\mathbb S^d\), where every element of \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm a}\) is valid on the uncertainty graph and \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm r}\) imposes additional scalar, diagonal, static, or block-separable structure. For a nominal matrix \(M\) and symmetric performance matrix \(H\), the restricted test is conservative precisely when
\[
\{\Pi\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm a}:H+M^{\mathsf T}\Pi M\prec0\}\neq\varnothing
\]
but
\[
\{\Pi\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm r}:H+M^{\mathsf T}\Pi M\prec0\}=\varnothing.
\]
Thus failure of the restricted LMI does not establish robust failure unless the restricted cone is known to be lossless for the uncertainty structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A structured multiplier test is conservative when an admissible separator exists but none lies in the imposed restricted multiplier cone.
assumptions_latex: Every \(\Pi\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm a}\) is valid on the specified uncertainty graph.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Restricted infeasibility is inconclusive whenever an unrestricted admissible multiplier can satisfy the strict separation LMI.

notation.meaning: Larger cone of admissible graph multipliers.

knowledge_statements.title: Integral Quadratic Constraint LMIs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuous-time hard-IQC dissipation LMI with a quadratic storage function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(\dot x=Ax+Bw\) and \(z=Cx+Dw\). Suppose the uncertainty satisfies the hard IQC
\[
\int_0^T\begin{bmatrix}z(t)\\w(t)\end{bmatrix}^{\!\mathsf T}\Pi
\begin{bmatrix}z(t)\\w(t)\end{bmatrix}dt\geq0
\quad\text{for every }T\geq0.
\]
If there exist \(P\succ0\) and \(\varepsilon>0\) such that
\[
\begin{bmatrix}A^{\mathsf T}P+PA&PB\\B^{\mathsf T}P&0\end{bmatrix}+
\begin{bmatrix}C&D\\0&I\end{bmatrix}^{\!\mathsf T}\Pi
\begin{bmatrix}C&D\\0&I\end{bmatrix}
\preceq-\varepsilon I,
\]
then \(V(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Px\) supplies a finite-horizon dissipation certificate and bounds the closed-loop state and internal signals in \(L_2\), subject to well-posedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A hard IQC combined with a strict storage LMI certifies finite-horizon dissipation and robust signal bounds.
assumptions_latex: The feedback interconnection is well posed.
The displayed IQC holds on every finite horizon.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The strict LMI and hard IQC imply a quadratic dissipation inequality and finite-energy internal signals.

notation.meaning: Storage function for the nominal state.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Integral quadratic constraint for a linear system
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the accumulated-energy constraint underlying dynamic nonexpansive-feedback and IQC-LMI analysis, including its relation to the stronger pointwise NLDI constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider the linear system
\[
\dot x=Ax+B_pp+B_uu+B_ww,
\quad q=C_qx+D_{qp}p+D_{qu}u+D_{qw}w,
\]
\[
z=C_zx+D_{zp}p+D_{zu}u+D_{zw}w.
\]
It is subject to the integral quadratic constraint
\[
\int_0^t p(\tau)^Tp(\tau)\,d\tau
\le
\int_0^t q(\tau)^Tq(\tau)\,d\tau
\qquad\text{for every }t\ge0.
\]
Such a system is described as a linear system with dynamic nonexpansive feedback and, unlike the associated pointwise-constrained NLDI, need not be a differential inclusion. Moreover,
\[
p(t)^Tp(t)\le q(t)^Tq(t)\quad\text{for all }t
\]
implies the displayed integral constraint for every \(t\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A linear system satisfies this integral quadratic constraint when, at every time, the accumulated squared norm of p does not exceed that of q. It is called a linear system with dynamic nonexpansive feedback and need not be a differential inclusion. The corresponding pointwise inequality is stronger and implies the integral constraint.
assumptions_latex: p,q\text{ have the displayed integrals on }[0,t]
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p(\tau)^Tp(\tau)\le q(\tau)^Tq(\tau)\ \forall\tau\in[0,t]\ \Longrightarrow\ \int_0^t p(\tau)^Tp(\tau)\,d\tau\le\int_0^t q(\tau)^Tq(\tau)\,d\tau

knowledge_statements.title: Lur’e Feedback Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional linear dynamics in negative feedback with a memoryless nonlinearity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A continuous-time Lur’e model is the feedback system
\[
\dot x(t)=Ax(t)-Bw(t),\qquad v(t)=Cx(t),\qquad w(t)=\phi(v(t)),
\]
where \(x(t)\in\mathbb R^n\), \(v(t),w(t)\in\mathbb R^p\), the linear subsystem is described by \((A,B,C)\), and \(\phi:\mathbb R^p\to\mathbb R^p\) is memoryless and satisfies specified sector or slope restrictions. With zero initial state, the corresponding transform-domain representation is
\[
v=-Gw,\qquad G(s)=C(sI-A)^{-1}B.
\]
Absolute-stability multiplier methods combine this graph relation with quadratic constraints satisfied by \(w=\phi(v)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Lur’e system is a linear dynamical subsystem in negative feedback with a memoryless sector- or slope-restricted nonlinearity.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), \(B\in\mathbb R^{n\times p}\), and \(C\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\).
The transform-domain representation uses zero initial state.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The state-space feedback equations have the zero-state representation \(v=-Gw\).

notation.meaning: Transfer matrix of the linear subsystem.
Input and output variables of the nonlinearity.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sector-bounded Lur’e systems and integral-quadratic Lyapunov functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the componentwise sector-bounded Lur’e feedback model, its integral-quadratic Lyapunov family, and the unknown-constant-gain specialization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A Lur’e system has \(\dot x=Ax+B_pp+B_ww\), \(q=C_qx\), \(z=C_zx\), and \(p_i(t)=\phi_i(q_i(t))\), where \(0\leq \sigma\phi_i(\sigma)\leq\sigma^2\) for all \(\sigma\in\mathbb R\), equivalently \(\phi_i(\sigma)(\phi_i(\sigma)-\sigma)\leq0\). General sectors \(\alpha_i\sigma^2\leq\sigma\phi_i(\sigma)\leq\beta_i\sigma^2\) can be normalized to this sector by a loop transformation. For \(V(\xi)=\xi^TP\xi+2\sum_{i=1}^{n_p}\lambda_i\int_0^{C_{i,q}\xi}\phi_i(\sigma)\,d\sigma\), \(P\succ0\) and \(\lambda_i\geq0\) imply \(V(\xi)\geq\xi^TP\xi>0\) whenever \(\xi\neq0\). If \(\phi_i(\sigma)=\delta_i\sigma\) with \(\delta_i\in[0,1]\), then \(V(\xi)=\xi^T(P+C_q^T\Delta\Lambda C_q)\xi\), where \(\Delta=\operatorname{diag}(\delta_i)\) and \(\Lambda=\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_i)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Lur’e system interconnects a linear state-space system with componentwise static sector-bounded nonlinearities. The stated integral-quadratic Lyapunov function is positive definite when P is positive definite and its integral weights are nonnegative. Constant uncertain linear gains yield a parameter-dependent quadratic Lyapunov function.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: V(\xi)\geq\xi^TP\xi>0\quad\forall\xi\neq0;\qquad \phi_i(\sigma)=\delta_i\sigma\Rightarrow V(\xi)=\xi^T(P+C_q^T\Delta\Lambda C_q)\xi.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unit-energy reachable-set outer certificate for a Lur’e system
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certifies outer bounds on states reachable from the origin by inputs having energy at most one.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{ue}}\) contain the states \(x(T)\) reachable from \(x(0)=0\), with \(T\geq0\) and \(\int_0^T w^Tw\,dt\leq1\). Define \(\mathcal F=\{\xi:V(\xi)\leq1\}\). If \(P\succ0\), \(\Lambda=\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_i)\succeq0\), and there exists \(T_s=\operatorname{diag}(\tau_i)\succeq0\) such that \[\begin{bmatrix}A^TP+PA&PB_p+A^TC_q^T\Lambda+C_q^TT_s&PB_w\\B_p^TP+\Lambda C_qA+T_sC_q&\Lambda C_qB_p+B_p^TC_q^T\Lambda-2T_s&\Lambda C_qB_w\\B_w^TP&B_w^TC_q^T\Lambda&-I\end{bmatrix}\preceq0,\] then \(\dot V(x)\leq w^Tw\) along all admissible trajectories and \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{ue}}\subseteq\mathcal F\subseteq\mathcal E\), where \(\mathcal E=\{\xi:\xi^TP\xi\leq1\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The multiplier LMI ensures that the Lyapunov function grows no faster than accumulated input energy. Thus every state reachable from the origin with input energy at most one lies in the Lyapunov unit sublevel set, which lies inside the ellipsoid defined by P. Known nonlinearities can make the Lyapunov sublevel set tighter than that ellipsoid.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \dot V(x)\leq w^Tw;\qquad\mathcal R_{\mathrm{ue}}\subseteq\mathcal F\subseteq\mathcal E.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Multiplier-LMI Sufficient Condition for Lur’e-System Stability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: For the unforced augmented Lur’e system, a strict quadratic multiplier dissipation inequality yields convergence of the augmented state to zero and admits an LMI form.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider system (8.19) with \(w\) and \(z\) absent. If \(P\succ0\) satisfies
\[
\frac{d}{dt}(\widetilde x^{T}P\widetilde x)+2\sum_{i=1}^{n_p}p_iq_{m,i}<0,
\]
equivalently
\[
\begin{bmatrix}
\widetilde A^{T}P+P\widetilde A & P\widetilde B_p+\widetilde C_q^{T}\\
\widetilde B_p^{T}P+\widetilde C_q & \widetilde D_{qp}+\widetilde D_{qp}^{T}
\end{bmatrix}\prec0,
\]
then \(\lim_{t\to\infty}\widetilde x(t)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For system (8.19) without the external signals w and z, a positive-definite quadratic storage matrix satisfying the strict multiplier dissipation condition, or its equivalent LMI, guarantees that the augmented state converges to zero.
assumptions_latex: The strict multiplier dissipation inequality holds, equivalently the displayed strict LMI in \(P\), \(C_m\), and \(D_m\) holds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\displaystyle\lim_{t\to\infty}\widetilde x(t)=0\); thus the system is stable in the stated convergence sense.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: S-procedure LMI certificate for strict Lur’e Lyapunov decrease
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Provides a sufficient multiplier LMI for strict Lyapunov decrease in the zero-exogenous-input Lur’e system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Set \(w=0\) and let \(V\) be the Lur’e Lyapunov function with \(P\succ0\) and \(\Lambda=\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_i)\succeq0\). If there exists \(T=\operatorname{diag}(\tau_i)\succeq0\) such that \[\begin{bmatrix}A^TP+PA&PB_p+A^TC_q^T\Lambda+C_q^TT\\B_p^TP+\Lambda C_qA+TC_q&\Lambda C_qB_p+B_p^TC_q^T\Lambda-2T\end{bmatrix}\prec0,\] then \(\dot V(x)<0\) for every nonzero admissible state of the Lur’e system whose feedback variables satisfy \(\pi_i(\pi_i-C_{i,q}\xi)\leq0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the zero-input Lur’e system, feasibility of the strict block LMI in the Lyapunov variables and nonnegative diagonal S-procedure multipliers is sufficient for strict decrease of the Lur’e Lyapunov function at every nonzero admissible state.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \dot V(x)<0\quad\text{for every nonzero admissible state }x.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Zero-input output-energy bound from a Lur’e dissipation inequality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bounds infinite-horizon zero-input output energy by the initial value of an integral-quadratic Lur’e Lyapunov function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the Lur’e system with \(w\equiv0\), \(z=C_zx\), and a nonnegative Lyapunov function \(V\) of the integral-quadratic form. If \(\dot V(x)+z^Tz\leq0\) along every admissible trajectory, then \[\int_0^\infty z^Tz\,dt\leq V(x(0)).\] Under the sector representation, the dissipation condition is equivalent to \[2\left(\xi^TP+\sum_{i=1}^{n_p}\lambda_i\pi_iC_{i,q}\right)(A\xi+B_p\pi)+\xi^TC_z^TC_z\xi\leq0\] for every \((\xi,\pi)\) satisfying \(\pi_i(\pi_i-C_{i,q}\xi)\leq0\), \(i=1,\ldots,n_p\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the zero-exogenous-input Lur’e system, if the Lyapunov function dissipates at least as fast as output energy accumulates, then the total infinite-horizon output energy is no greater than its initial Lyapunov value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \int_0^\infty z^Tz\,dt\leq V(x(0)).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lur’e induced-L2-gain certificate and best bound in the Lyapunov family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives a dissipativity inequality and sufficient S-procedure LMI for the induced L2 gain when direct input-output feedthrough is absent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \(D_{zw}=0\). If a Lur’e Lyapunov function \(V\) and \(\gamma\geq0\) satisfy \(\dot V(x)\leq\gamma^2w^Tw-z^Tz\) for every admissible state and input, then, under the usual zero-initial-state definition, the system’s induced \(\mathbf L_2\) gain does not exceed \(\gamma\). A sufficient condition is the existence of \(P\succ0\), \(\Lambda=\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_i)\succeq0\), and \(T=\operatorname{diag}(\tau_i)\succeq0\) such that \[\begin{bmatrix}A^TP+PA+C_z^TC_z&PB_p+A^TC_q^T\Lambda+C_q^TT&PB_w\\B_p^TP+\Lambda C_qA+TC_q&\Lambda C_qB_p+B_p^TC_q^T\Lambda-2T&\Lambda C_qB_w\\B_w^TP&B_w^TC_q^T\Lambda&-\gamma^2I\end{bmatrix}\preceq0.\] The smallest upper bound provable with this Lyapunov family is obtained by minimizing \(\gamma\) over these constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With no direct input-output feedthrough, the stated dissipation inequality bounds the induced L2 gain by gamma. The block semidefinite inequality is a sufficient sector-multiplier certificate, and minimizing gamma gives the best bound certified by this Lur’e Lyapunov family, not necessarily the exact gain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|\mathcal G\|_{\mathbf L_2}\leq\gamma;\qquad\gamma_{\mathrm{cert}}=\min\{\gamma:\text{the stated certificate constraints hold}\}.

children.title: Popov Multiplier Models
children.top_down_role: Frequency-shaped multiplier templates associated with Popov-type certification.

knowledge_statements.title: Popov Multiplier Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar continuous-time Popov frequency-domain certificate under negative-feedback convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider a scalar Lur’e interconnection \(v=-Gw\), \(w=\phi(v)\), where \(G\) is stable and \(0\leq\phi(v)/v\leq k\) for \(v\neq0\). For \(q\geq0\), define the Popov multiplier
\[
\Pi_q(\omega)=
\begin{bmatrix}
0&\frac{k}{2}(1-\mathrm i q\omega)\\
\frac{k}{2}(1+\mathrm i q\omega)&-1
\end{bmatrix}.
\]
If there exists \(\epsilon>0\) such that
\[
\begin{bmatrix}-G(\mathrm i\omega)\\1\end{bmatrix}^{\!*}
\Pi_q(\omega)
\begin{bmatrix}-G(\mathrm i\omega)\\1\end{bmatrix}
\leq-\epsilon
\]
for every real \(\omega\), together with the usual Popov regularity assumptions on \(\phi\), then the multiplier supplies an absolute-stability certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Popov multiplier augments a sector constraint by a nonnegative frequency slope and yields an absolute-stability frequency test.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is a stable scalar proper transfer function.
\(\phi(0)=0\) is time invariant and satisfies \(0\leq\phi(v)/v\leq k\) for \(v\neq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Uniform strict negativity of the Popov graph form certifies absolute stability under the stated convention.
