children.title: Sector-Multiplier Models
children.top_down_role: Quadratic multiplier templates for sector-bounded nonlinearities.

knowledge_statements.title: Sector-Multiplier Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Static quadratic representation of a scalar sector-bounded nonlinearity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(w=\phi(v)\) be scalar and satisfy \(\phi(0)=0\), \(\alpha<\beta\), and
\[
\alpha\leq\frac{\phi(v)}{v}\leq\beta
\qquad\text{for every }v\neq0.
\]
This sector condition is equivalent to
\[
(w-\alpha v)(\beta v-w)\geq0,
\]
or, in quadratic-multiplier form,
\[
\begin{bmatrix}v\\w\end{bmatrix}^{\!\mathsf T}
\begin{bmatrix}
-\alpha\beta&\frac{\alpha+\beta}{2}\\
\frac{\alpha+\beta}{2}&-1
\end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix}v\\w\end{bmatrix}\geq0.
\]
Any nonnegative scaling of this matrix represents the same sector constraint and may be combined with a linear-system dissipation LMI.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scalar sector bound is exactly a static quadratic inequality in the nonlinearity's input and output.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha\leq\phi(v)/v\leq\beta\) for \(v\neq0\) is equivalent to the displayed quadratic multiplier inequality.

notation.meaning: Input and output of the scalar nonlinearity.

knowledge_statements.title: Absolute-Stability Certificate Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient quadratic certificate for a continuous-time Lur’e interconnection with a memoryless sector-bounded nonlinearity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(\dot x=Ax-B\phi(Cx)\), where \(\phi(y)^{\mathsf T}(Ky-\phi(y))\ge 0\) for every \(y\), and \(\phi(0)=0\). If there exist \(P=P^{\mathsf T}\succ0\) and \(\lambda\ge0\) such that
\[
\begin{bmatrix}
A^{\mathsf T}P+PA & -PB+\frac{\lambda}{2}C^{\mathsf T}K^{\mathsf T}\\
-B^{\mathsf T}P+\frac{\lambda}{2}KC & -\lambda I
\end{bmatrix}\prec0,
\]
then \(V(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Px\) decreases along every nonzero closed-loop trajectory compatible with the sector condition. Consequently, the origin is globally exponentially stable whenever the interconnection is well posed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible quadratic Lyapunov matrix and nonnegative sector multiplier certify exponential stability of every well-posed Lur’e feedback trajectory satisfying the stated sector inequality.
assumptions_latex: \(\phi\) is memoryless and satisfies the stated global sector inequality.
The feedback interconnection admits unique forward trajectories.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x=0\) is globally exponentially stable.
review_flags: Exact absolute-stability LMI locator is absent from the supplied inventory.
Sign and sector conventions require source-level confirmation.

knowledge_statements.title: Nominal Quadratic Lyapunov LMIs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuous-time Lyapunov characterization for one finite-dimensional linear time-invariant system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\). The system \(\dot x=Ax\) is exponentially stable if and only if there exists \(P=P^{\mathsf T}\succ0\) satisfying
\[
A^{\mathsf T}P+PA\prec0.
\]
For any such \(P\), the function \(V(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Px\) is positive definite and obeys \(\dot V(x)=x^{\mathsf T}(A^{\mathsf T}P+PA)x<0\) for every \(x\ne0\). Equivalently, for every prescribed \(Q=Q^{\mathsf T}\succ0\), exponential stability is equivalent to the existence of a unique \(P=P^{\mathsf T}\succ0\) solving \(A^{\mathsf T}P+PA=-Q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A continuous-time linear system is exponentially stable exactly when it admits a positive-definite quadratic Lyapunov function with a negative-definite derivative.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is a real, finite-dimensional constant matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A\) is Hurwitz if and only if \(P\succ0\) and \(A^{\mathsf T}P+PA\prec0\) are feasible.

knowledge_statements.title: Common Quadratic Lyapunov LMIs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One quadratic Lyapunov function certifying a finite family of continuous-time linear systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For matrices \(A_1,\ldots,A_m\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), suppose there exist \(P=P^{\mathsf T}\succ0\) and \(\varepsilon>0\) such that
\[
A_i^{\mathsf T}P+PA_i\preceq-\varepsilon I,
\qquad i=1,\ldots,m.
\]
Then \(V(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Px\) is a common quadratic Lyapunov function. Every individual system \(\dot x=A_i x\) is exponentially stable, and the same inequalities certify all convex combinations \(A=\sum_{i=1}^m\theta_iA_i\) with \(\theta_i\ge0\) and \(\sum_i\theta_i=1\). The feasibility conditions are LMIs in \(P\) and \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One positive-definite matrix satisfying every vertex Lyapunov inequality certifies exponential stability of the entire finite family and its convex hull.
assumptions_latex: \(A_1,\ldots,A_m\) have a common finite state dimension.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(V(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Px\) is a common exponential-stability certificate.

notation.meaning: system matrices in the finite family

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Semi-Infinite SDP Characterization of a Common Quadratic Lyapunov Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact optimal-value characterization and certificate extraction for an uncertain linear system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal U\) be the uncertainty set associated with an uncertain linear system, and let \(v_*\) be the optimal value of
\[\min_{s\in\mathbb R,\,X\in\mathbb S^n} s\quad\text{subject to}\quad sI_n-A^TX-XA\succeq0\ \ \forall A\in\mathcal U,\qquad X\succeq I_n.\]
The system admits a quadratic Lyapunov function if and only if \(v_*<0\). Moreover, every feasible \((s,X)\) with \(s<0\) provides a quadratic Lyapunov stability certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An uncertain linear system admits a common quadratic Lyapunov function exactly when the displayed semi-infinite semidefinite program has negative optimal value. Every feasible solution with negative objective supplies such a stability certificate.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal U\text{ is the uncertainty set associated with the uncertain linear system.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathrm{(ULS)}\text{ admits a quadratic Lyapunov function}\iff v_*<0,\quad\text{and every feasible }(s,X)\text{ with }s<0\text{ supplies a quadratic stability certificate.}

knowledge_statements.title: Polytopic-System Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Vertex-exact common-quadratic test for an affine continuous-time matrix polytope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
\mathcal A=\left\{\sum_{i=1}^m\theta_iA_i:\ \theta_i\ge0,\ \sum_{i=1}^m\theta_i=1\right\}.
\]
A fixed matrix \(P=P^{\mathsf T}\succ0\) satisfies \(A^{\mathsf T}P+PA\prec0\) for every \(A\in\mathcal A\) if and only if it satisfies
\[
A_i^{\mathsf T}P+PA_i\prec0,
\qquad i=1,\ldots,m.
\]
Thus finitely many vertex LMIs exactly test the existence of a common quadratic certificate over the polytope. Feasibility implies uniform exponential stability for every constant matrix in \(\mathcal A\), and also for arbitrary measurable time variation within \(\mathcal A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Because the Lyapunov inequality is affine in the system matrix, a common quadratic certificate over a matrix polytope is determined exactly at its vertices.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal A\) is the convex hull of finitely many real matrices of equal dimension.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The common-quadratic robust condition over \(\mathcal A\) is equivalent to the finite collection of vertex LMIs.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(\dot x(t)=A_{\sigma(t)}x(t)\), where \(\sigma:[0,\infty)\to\{1,\ldots,m\}\) is any piecewise-constant switching signal with locally finitely many switches. If there exist \(P=P^{\mathsf T}\succ0\) and \(\varepsilon>0\) satisfying
\[
A_i^{\mathsf T}P+PA_i\preceq-\varepsilon I,
\qquad i=1,\ldots,m,
\]
then \(V(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Px\) is continuous at switching instants and decreases uniformly during every mode interval. Hence constants \(M\ge1\) and \(\alpha>0\), independent of \(\sigma\), exist such that \(\lVert x(t)\rVert\le M e^{-\alpha t}\lVert x(0)\rVert\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strict common quadratic Lyapunov inequality gives exponential stability uniformly over all locally finite switching sequences, without a dwell-time restriction.

knowledge_statements.title: Common-Certificate Conservatism
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical limitation of common-quadratic stability tests for uncertain and switched linear systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a matrix family \(\mathcal A\), feasibility of
\[
P=P^{\mathsf T}\succ0,
\qquad A^{\mathsf T}P+PA\prec0\quad\text{for every }A\in\mathcal A
\]
is sufficient for uniform exponential stability under arbitrary measurable variation of \(A(t)\in\mathcal A\). The converse does not hold for general families: a uniformly exponentially stable inclusion may admit no common quadratic Lyapunov function. Therefore infeasibility of the common-matrix LMIs is not an instability certificate; it only excludes certificates of the form \(V(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Px\). Parameter-dependent, piecewise-quadratic, or higher-degree Lyapunov functions can succeed when the common-quadratic test fails.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Common quadratic feasibility proves robust stability, but infeasibility proves only that this restricted certificate class is unavailable, not that the system is unstable.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal A\) is a bounded family of real matrices with common dimension.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Failure of the common-quadratic LMIs is inconclusive about stability in general.

notation.meaning: single candidate Lyapunov matrix shared by the family

knowledge_statements.title: Parameter-Dependent Lyapunov LMIs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise Lyapunov certificates for frozen parameter uncertainty, with the time-varying-parameter limitation made explicit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Theta\) be compact and let \(A:\Theta\to\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) and \(P:\Theta\to\mathbb S^n\) be continuous. If some \(\varepsilon>0\) satisfies
\[
P(\theta)\succeq\varepsilon I,
\qquad A(\theta)^{\mathsf T}P(\theta)+P(\theta)A(\theta)\preceq-\varepsilon I
\]
for every \(\theta\in\Theta\), then each frozen system \(\dot x=A(\theta)x\) is exponentially stable with a parameter-dependent quadratic certificate. For a differentiable trajectory \(\theta(t)\), however,
\[
\dot V=x^{\mathsf T}\bigl(A^{\mathsf T}P+PA+\dot P\bigr)x,
\qquad \dot P=\sum_j\frac{\partial P}{\partial\theta_j}\dot\theta_j.
\]
Thus the pointwise LMIs alone do not certify arbitrary parameter variation unless the additional derivative term is controlled.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Parameter-dependent Lyapunov inequalities certify every frozen model, while time-varying parameters require bounds on the derivative of the Lyapunov matrix.
assumptions_latex: \(A(\theta)\) and \(P(\theta)\) are continuous; differentiability is additionally assumed when \(\theta\) varies with time.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed pointwise inequalities certify uniform frozen-parameter stability, but not unrestricted parameter variation by themselves.

notation.meaning: derivative induced by the parameter trajectory

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate content kind and frozen-versus-time-varying distinction fit the topic. The formulas are plausible, but no source fixes the intended parameter regularity and rate regime or supports the derivative-term limitation.

knowledge_statements.title: Invariant-Ellipsoid LMIs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive invariance of a centered ellipsoid for an autonomous continuous-time linear system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\dot x=Ax\), let \(P=P^{\mathsf T}\succ0\) and define
\[
\mathcal E_P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:x^{\mathsf T}Px\le1\}.
\]
If
\[
A^{\mathsf T}P+PA\preceq0,
\]
then \(\mathcal E_P\) is positively invariant: every solution beginning in \(\mathcal E_P\) remains there for all future time. If the inequality is strict, every nonzero trajectory has strictly decreasing \(x^{\mathsf T}Px\), and the origin is exponentially stable. The invariance claim follows from the boundary condition \(\frac{d}{dt}(x^{\mathsf T}Px)\le0\) whenever \(x^{\mathsf T}Px=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-definite quadratic form whose derivative is nonpositive defines a centered ellipsoid that linear trajectories cannot leave.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal E_P\) is positively invariant under \(\dot x=Ax\).

notation.meaning: unit sublevel ellipsoid of the quadratic form

children.title: State-Bound LMIs

knowledge_statements.title: State-Bound LMIs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semidefinite representation of linear state bounds over a centered ellipsoid.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P=P^{\mathsf T}\succ0\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(\rho\ge0\). Over the ellipsoid \(\mathcal E_P=\{x:x^{\mathsf T}Px\le1\}\), the bound
\[
|c^{\mathsf T}x|\le\rho\qquad\text{for every }x\in\mathcal E_P
\]
holds if and only if
\[
c^{\mathsf T}P^{-1}c\le\rho^2,
\]
which, by the Schur complement, is equivalent to the LMI
\[
\begin{bmatrix}
\rho^2 & c^{\mathsf T}\\
c & P
\end{bmatrix}\succeq0.
\]
Applying this condition to coordinate vectors gives componentwise state bounds; applying it to rows of an output matrix gives output bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The maximum magnitude of a linear state functional over an ellipsoid has an exact Schur-complement LMI representation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_{x\in\mathcal E_P}|c^{\mathsf T}x|\le\rho\) is equivalent to the displayed LMI.

notation.meaning: centered ellipsoid defined by the quadratic inequality
state or output direction being bounded

knowledge_statements.title: Reachable-Set Outer Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Invariant ellipsoidal outer bound for states reachable under bounded continuous-time disturbances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(\dot x=Ax+Bw\) with \(\lVert w(t)\rVert_2\le1\) almost everywhere. If \(P=P^{\mathsf T}\succ0\) and \(\alpha>0\) satisfy
\[
\begin{bmatrix}
A^{\mathsf T}P+PA+\alpha P & PB\\
B^{\mathsf T}P & -\alpha I
\end{bmatrix}\preceq0,
\]
then \(V(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Px\) obeys \(\dot V\le-\alpha V+\alpha\lVert w\rVert_2^2\). Consequently, the ellipsoid \(\mathcal E_P=\{x:V(x)\le1\}\) is robustly positively invariant. In particular, when \(x(0)=0\), every state reachable at any finite time belongs to \(\mathcal E_P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A block LMI yields an invariant ellipsoid containing every state reachable from the origin under unit-norm bounded disturbances.
assumptions_latex: The disturbance is measurable and satisfies \(\lVert w(t)\rVert_2\le1\) almost everywhere.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The reachable set from \(x(0)=0\) is contained in \(\mathcal E_P\).
review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports this bounded-disturbance reachable-set LMI.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The block inequality algebraically yields the stated dissipation bound and invariant reachable-set outer ellipsoid, and certificate is the correct content kind. An inspectable source locator is nevertheless absent.

children.title: Disturbance-Dependent Invariance
children.top_down_role: Invariant-set certification under bounded exogenous inputs.

knowledge_statements.title: Disturbance-Dependent Invariance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Robust invariance certificate for ellipsoidal disturbances and a centered state ellipsoid.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(\dot x=Ax+Ew\), with disturbances satisfying \(w^{\mathsf T}Ww\le1\), where \(W=W^{\mathsf T}\succ0\). If \(P=P^{\mathsf T}\succ0\) and \(\tau>0\) satisfy
\[
\begin{bmatrix}
A^{\mathsf T}P+PA+\tau P & PE\\
E^{\mathsf T}P & -\tau W
\end{bmatrix}\preceq0,
\]
then \(V(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Px\) satisfies \(\dot V\le-\tau V+\tau w^{\mathsf T}Ww\). Hence, on the boundary \(V=1\), every admissible disturbance gives \(\dot V\le0\). The ellipsoid \(\{x:x^{\mathsf T}Px\le1\}\) is therefore robustly positively invariant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A disturbance-weighted block LMI ensures that every admissible ellipsoidal disturbance points trajectories inward or tangentially at the state-ellipsoid boundary.
assumptions_latex: The disturbance is measurable and obeys \(w(t)^{\mathsf T}Ww(t)\le1\) almost everywhere.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{x:x^{\mathsf T}Px\le1\}\) is robustly positively invariant.
review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports the disturbance-dependent invariance LMI.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The disturbance-weighted block LMI is internally consistent and gives the stated boundary invariance condition. It fits the certificate leaf, but the nontrivial robust-invariance claim has no cited source or standard-field rationale.

knowledge_statements.title: Continuous-Time Bounded-Real Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strict continuous-time bounded-real lemma for a stable finite-dimensional realization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(\dot x=Ax+Bw\), \(z=Cx+Dw\), and let \(G(s)=C(sI-A)^{-1}B+D\). If \(A\) is Hurwitz and \(\gamma>0\), then \(\lVert G\rVert_{\infty}<\gamma\) if and only if there exists \(P=P^{\mathsf T}\succ0\) such that
\[
\begin{bmatrix}
A^{\mathsf T}P+PA & PB & C^{\mathsf T}\\
B^{\mathsf T}P & -\gamma^2 I & D^{\mathsf T}\\
C & D & -I
\end{bmatrix}\prec0.
\]
Equivalently, the zero-initial-state input-output operator has induced \(L_2\) gain strictly below \(\gamma\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a stable continuous-time realization, an exact strict block LMI characterizes whether its induced energy gain is below a prescribed level.
assumptions_latex: The realization is finite dimensional and \(\gamma>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert G\rVert_{\infty}<\gamma\) holds if and only if the displayed strict LMI is feasible.

notation.meaning: transfer matrix from disturbance input to performance output

review_flags: No bounded-real lemma locator is present in the supplied source inventory.
The precise realization hypotheses should be confirmed from an authoritative source.

knowledge_statements.title: Discrete-Time Bounded-Real Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strict discrete-time bounded-real lemma for a minimal stable realization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let the discrete-time system be \(x_{k+1}=Ax_k+Bw_k\), \(z_k=Cx_k+Dw_k\), with transfer matrix \(G(z)=C(zI-A)^{-1}B+D\). If the realization is minimal and \(A\) is Schur stable, then \(\lVert G\rVert_{H_\infty}<\gamma\) if and only if there exists \(P=P^{\mathsf T}\succ0\) such that
\[
\begin{bmatrix}A^{\mathsf T}PA-P+C^{\mathsf T}C&A^{\mathsf T}PB+C^{\mathsf T}D\\B^{\mathsf T}PA+D^{\mathsf T}C&B^{\mathsf T}PB+D^{\mathsf T}D-\gamma^2I\end{bmatrix}\prec0.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stable minimal discrete-time system has gain below gamma exactly when a positive-definite quadratic storage matrix satisfies the bounded-real LMI.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert G\rVert_{H_\infty}<\gamma\) is equivalent to feasibility of the displayed strict LMI with \(P\succ0\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem, hypotheses, and strict discrete-time bounded-real LMI are mathematically coherent and fit the theorem-family leaf, but no source or inspectable locator is supplied. children.title: Strict Bounded-Real Regimes

knowledge_statements.title: Strict Bounded-Real Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuous-time strict dissipativity form of the bounded-real condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\dot x=Ax+Bw\) and \(z=Cx+Dw\), a strict bounded-real regime at level \(\gamma>0\) holds when there exist \(P=P^{\mathsf T}\succ0\) and \(\varepsilon>0\) such that, for every \((x,w)\),
\[
2x^{\mathsf T}P(Ax+Bw)+z^{\mathsf T}z-\gamma^2w^{\mathsf T}w\le-\varepsilon(\lVert x\rVert_2^2+\lVert w\rVert_2^2).
\]
Equivalently, the associated bounded-real matrix is negative definite. Integration along zero-initial-state trajectories yields \(\lVert z\rVert_{L_2}<\gamma\lVert w\rVert_{L_2}\) for every nonzero \(w\in L_2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive quadratic storage function with a uniform dissipation margin certifies a strict induced-gain bound and robust LMI feasibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The strict dissipation inequality implies \(\lVert z\rVert_{L_2}<\gamma\lVert w\rVert_{L_2}\) for every nonzero zero-state input.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Nonstrict bounded-real feasibility with \(P\succeq0\), without minimality or an internal-stability hypothesis, does not imply a strict gain bound or asymptotic internal stability. For example, the scalar discrete-time system \(x_{k+1}=x_k\), \(z_k=w_k\) has \(A=1\), \(B=C=0\), \(D=1\), and \(\gamma=1\). Its transfer matrix is \(G(z)=1\). With \(P=0\), its nonstrict bounded-real matrix equals zero, while \(A\) has a unit-circle eigenvalue and \(\lVert G\rVert_{H_\infty}=1\). Thus equality in the gain bound and marginal internal modes are both possible at the nonstrict boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonstrict bounded-real feasibility can admit equality in the gain and marginal internal dynamics, so it does not by itself imply a strict gain bound or asymptotic internal stability.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonstrict Boundary Regimes

children.title: Positive-Real Certificate Families
children.top_down_role: State-space certificates for positive-real transfer behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Positive-Real Certificate Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuous-time positive-real lemma for a stable minimal real realization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G(s)=C(sI-A)^{-1}B+D\) be a real-rational, minimal realization with \(A\) Hurwitz. Then \(G\) is positive real, meaning \(G(s)+G(s)^*\succeq0\) for \(\operatorname{Re}s>0\), if and only if there exists \(P=P^{\mathsf T}\succeq0\) satisfying
\[
\begin{bmatrix}A^{\mathsf T}P+PA&PB-C^{\mathsf T}\\B^{\mathsf T}P-C&-(D+D^{\mathsf T})\end{bmatrix}\preceq0.
\]
Under minimality and the stated stability hypothesis, the storage matrix may be chosen positive definite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stable minimal transfer matrix is positive real exactly when a quadratic storage matrix satisfies the positive-real LMI.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Positive realness of \(G\) is equivalent to feasibility of the displayed LMI.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The positive-real LMI and theorem role are plausible under the stated stable minimal square-realization assumptions, but the record has no source. A precise positive-real lemma theorem or section locator is required to confirm the equivalence and the positive-definiteness assertion for the storage matrix.

children.title: Passivity Certificate Families
children.top_down_role: Storage-based certificates for passive input-output behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Passivity Certificate Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic-storage certificate for continuous-time input-output passivity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\dot x=Ax+Bu\), \(y=Cx+Du\), suppose \(P=P^{\mathsf T}\succeq0\) satisfies
\[
\begin{bmatrix}A^{\mathsf T}P+PA&PB-C^{\mathsf T}\\B^{\mathsf T}P-C&-(D+D^{\mathsf T})\end{bmatrix}\preceq0.
\]
Then \(V(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Px\) obeys \(\dot V(x(t))\le2u(t)^{\mathsf T}y(t)\) along every classical trajectory. Consequently,
\[
V(x(T))-V(x(0))\le2\int_0^T u(t)^{\mathsf T}y(t)\,dt
\]
for every \(T\ge0\), so \(P\) is a directly checkable passivity certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible positive-semidefinite storage matrix proves passivity by bounding stored-energy growth with supplied input-output power.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(V(x(T))-V(x(0))\le2\int_0^T u^{\mathsf T}y\,dt\) for every \(T\ge0\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed LMI algebraically gives the stated quadratic-storage passivity inequality, and certificate is the correct content kind. No authoritative source with a specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Supply-Rate Variants
children.top_down_role: Passivity-related families organized by alternative quadratic supply rates.

knowledge_statements.title: Supply-Rate Variants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: QSR-dissipativity representation encompassing passivity and gain supply rates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\dot x=Ax+Bu\), \(y=Cx+Du\), and define the quadratic supply rate
\[
w(y,u)=\begin{bmatrix}y\\u\end{bmatrix}^{\mathsf T}\Pi\begin{bmatrix}y\\u\end{bmatrix},\qquad \Pi=\begin{bmatrix}Q&S\\S^{\mathsf T}&R\end{bmatrix}=\Pi^{\mathsf T}.
\]
With \(E=\begin{bmatrix}C&D\\0&I\end{bmatrix}\), a quadratic storage \(V(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Px\), \(P\succeq0\), certifies \(\dot V\le w(y,u)\) exactly when
\[
\begin{bmatrix}A^{\mathsf T}P+PA&PB\\B^{\mathsf T}P&0\end{bmatrix}-E^{\mathsf T}\Pi E\preceq0.
\]
Choices of \(Q,S,R\) recover passivity, sector, and induced-gain supply rates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every quadratic supply rate yields an affine storage LMI; particular coefficient choices encode passivity, sector, and gain conditions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed LMI is equivalent to \(\dot V(x)\le w(y,u)\) for all \((x,u)\).

notation.meaning: map from state-input pairs to output-input pairs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The QSR representation is internally consistent and representation fits the supply-rate leaf, but the record lacks an inspectable source for the general dissipativity LMI and its claimed family of specializations.

children.title: Strict Passivity Regimes
children.top_down_role: Passivity models incorporating positive dissipation margins.

knowledge_statements.title: Strict Passivity Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combined input- and output-strict passivity with quadratic storage.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The continuous-time system \(\dot x=Ax+Bu\), \(y=Cx+Du\) is quadratically input-output strictly passive if there exist \(P=P^{\mathsf T}\succeq0\), \(\rho>0\), and \(\nu>0\) such that
\[
\dot V(x)\le2u^{\mathsf T}y-\rho u^{\mathsf T}u-\nu y^{\mathsf T}y,
\qquad V(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Px,
\]
for all \((x,u)\). Equivalently, the QSR LMI holds with
\[
\Pi=\begin{bmatrix}-\nu I&I\\I&-\rho I\end{bmatrix}.
\]
Setting only \(\rho>0\) or only \(\nu>0\) gives input-strict or output-strict passivity, respectively.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strict passivity subtracts positive input or output energy from the passive supply rate and is certified by the corresponding strict QSR storage inequality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The QSR inequality with the displayed \(\Pi\) certifies combined input-output strict passivity.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The supply matrix is consistent with the stated convention \(2u^{\mathsf T}y\), and condition fits the strict-regime leaf. A source is required to establish the adopted input/output strictness terminology and scaling convention.

children.title: Positive-Real–Passivity Correspondence
children.top_down_role: State-space and input-output connections between the two certificate viewpoints.

knowledge_statements.title: Positive-Real–Passivity Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuous-time equivalence under the common supply convention \(2u^{\mathsf T}y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G(s)=C(sI-A)^{-1}B+D\) be a square, minimal real-rational realization with \(A\) Hurwitz. The following are equivalent: \(G(s)+G(s)^*\succeq0\) for every \(\operatorname{Re}s>0\); the state-space system is passive with supply \(2u^{\mathsf T}y\); and there exists \(P=P^{\mathsf T}\succeq0\) satisfying
\[
\begin{bmatrix}A^{\mathsf T}P+PA&PB-C^{\mathsf T}\\B^{\mathsf T}P-C&-(D+D^{\mathsf T})\end{bmatrix}\preceq0.
\]
Thus frequency-domain positive realness and time-domain passivity share the same semidefinite storage certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a stable minimal square realization, positive realness, passivity, and feasibility of the positive-real storage LMI are equivalent.
assumptions_latex: The real-rational realization is square and minimal
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Positive realness, passivity, and feasibility of the displayed LMI are equivalent.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The asserted positive-real/passivity/KYP equivalence is plausible but unsupported by any citation. In addition, duality is not the precise mathematical role of this correspondence; theorem or principle would better describe an equivalence result. A sourced formulation is required before revising the kind and statement.

children.title: Frequency-Selective Generalized KYP Family
children.top_down_role: Finite-frequency and generalized quadratic-performance forms.

children.title: Generalized KYP Frameworks
children.top_down_role: Generalized quadratic-performance formulations within the KYP family.

knowledge_statements.title: Generalized KYP Frameworks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuous-time generalized KYP lemma over a quadratic frequency region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Phi,\Psi\in\mathbb H^2\) define
\[
\Lambda=\left\{\lambda:\begin{bmatrix}\lambda\\1\end{bmatrix}^*\Phi\begin{bmatrix}\lambda\\1\end{bmatrix}=0,\ \begin{bmatrix}\lambda\\1\end{bmatrix}^*\Psi\begin{bmatrix}\lambda\\1\end{bmatrix}\ge0\right\}.
\]
For a controllable realization \(G(\lambda)=C(\lambda I-A)^{-1}B+D\) having no pole in \(\Lambda\), the strict frequency inequality \(\begin{bmatrix}G(\lambda)\\I\end{bmatrix}^*\Pi\begin{bmatrix}G(\lambda)\\I\end{bmatrix}\prec0\) on \(\Lambda\) is equivalent, under the generalized-KYP regularity conditions, to the existence of Hermitian \(P\) and \(Q\succeq0\) such that
\[
F^*(\Phi\otimes P+\Psi\otimes Q)F+E^*\Pi E\prec0,
\]
where \(F=\begin{bmatrix}A&B\\I&0\end{bmatrix}\) and \(E=\begin{bmatrix}C&D\\0&I\end{bmatrix}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The generalized KYP lemma replaces a frequency inequality over a quadratic region by a finite-dimensional LMI with two Hermitian multipliers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The strict frequency inequality on \(\Lambda\) is equivalent to feasibility of the displayed multiplier LMI.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The generalized-KYP theorem cannot be accepted with the essential hypotheses represented only as unspecified regularity conditions. A precise authoritative theorem locator is needed to determine the admissible quadratic regions, strictness assumptions, multiplier constraints, and exact LMI convention.

children.title: Finite-Frequency Performance
children.top_down_role: Performance models restricted to finite spectral regions.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The singular-value bound on \(\Omega\) is equivalent to the displayed pointwise quadratic inequality.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Band-limited continuous-time induced-gain frequency inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a stable continuous-time transfer matrix \(G(s)\) and a closed frequency band \(\Omega\subset\mathbb R\) containing no pole, the finite-frequency performance requirement is
\[
\sup_{\omega\in\Omega}\bar\sigma(G(\mathrm j\omega))<\gamma.
\]
It is equivalently represented by the pointwise quadratic inequality
\[
\begin{bmatrix}G(\mathrm j\omega)\\I\end{bmatrix}^*
\begin{bmatrix}I&0\\0&-\gamma^2I\end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix}G(\mathrm j\omega)\\I\end{bmatrix}\prec0,
\qquad \omega\in\Omega.
\]
A generalized KYP description of \(\Omega\) converts this continuum of inequalities into a finite-dimensional semidefinite condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A band-limited gain bound is a quadratic frequency inequality restricted to the chosen band and can be encoded through generalized KYP multipliers.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Frequency Performance

children.title: Frequency-Selective KYP Variants
children.top_down_role: KYP formulations tailored to selected frequency sets.

knowledge_statements.title: Frequency-Selective KYP Variants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic region matrices for low-, middle-, and high-frequency continuous-time bands.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
On the imaginary axis choose \(\Phi=\begin{bmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{bmatrix}\), so \(\begin{bmatrix}\lambda\\1\end{bmatrix}^*\Phi\begin{bmatrix}\lambda\\1\end{bmatrix}=0\) means \(\lambda=\mathrm j\omega\). The low-frequency region \(|\omega|\le\omega_\ell\) uses \(\Psi_{\mathrm L}=\operatorname{diag}(-1,\omega_\ell^2)\); the high-frequency region \(|\omega|\ge\omega_h\) uses \(\Psi_{\mathrm H}=\operatorname{diag}(1,-\omega_h^2)\). For \(\omega_1\le\omega\le\omega_2\), use
\[
\Psi_{\mathrm M}=\begin{bmatrix}-1&\mathrm j(\omega_1+\omega_2)/2\\-\mathrm j(\omega_1+\omega_2)/2&-\omega_1\omega_2\end{bmatrix}.
\]
In each case, the inequality defined by \(\Psi\) selects precisely the stated band.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Different quadratic region matrices select low, middle, or high frequencies while leaving the generalized KYP LMI construction unchanged.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The matrices \(\Psi_{\mathrm L}\), \(\Psi_{\mathrm M}\), and \(\Psi_{\mathrm H}\) encode the stated frequency regions.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Direct substitution on \(\lambda=\mathrm j\omega\) is consistent with the stated low-, middle-, and high-frequency regions, and representation fits the leaf. Nevertheless, no authoritative locator is supplied for these convention-sensitive region matrices.

children.title: H-Infinity Control LMI Model

children.title: Full-State H-Infinity Synthesis
children.top_down_role: State-feedback performance synthesis models.

knowledge_statements.title: Full-State H-Infinity Synthesis
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuous-time convex LMI model for full-state feedback performance synthesis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(\dot x=Ax+B_1w+B_2u\), \(z=C_1x+D_{11}w+D_{12}u\), and full-state feedback \(u=Kx\). A sufficient, and under the standard strict bounded-real hypotheses equivalent, synthesis model is to find \(X=X^{\mathsf T}\succ0\), \(Y\), and \(\gamma>0\) satisfying
\[
\begin{bmatrix}
\operatorname{He}(AX+B_2Y)&B_1&(C_1X+D_{12}Y)^{\mathsf T}\\
B_1^{\mathsf T}&-\gamma I&D_{11}^{\mathsf T}\\
C_1X+D_{12}Y&D_{11}&-\gamma I
\end{bmatrix}\prec0.
\]
The recovered controller is \(K=YX^{-1}\), and minimizing \(\gamma\) gives the SDP performance design.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A change of variables converts full-state H-infinity synthesis into an SDP; the feedback gain is recovered as Y times the inverse of X.
assumptions_latex: The plant is continuous-time and full state is measured
Standard strict bounded-real stabilizability and detectability hypotheses hold
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Feasibility yields \(K=YX^{-1}\) with \(\lVert T_{w\to z}\rVert_{H_\infty}<\gamma\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Static state feedback and the closed-loop LDI
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines constant linear state feedback for an uncertain linear differential inclusion, derives the resulting closed-loop dynamics and output, and identifies the associated synthesis problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the LDI \(\dot x=A(t)x+B_w(t)w+B_u(t)u\), \(z=C_z(t)x+D_{zw}(t)w+D_{zu}(t)u\), with \(\begin{bmatrix}A(t)&B_w(t)&B_u(t)\\ C_z(t)&D_{zw}(t)&D_{zu}(t)\end{bmatrix}\in\Omega\), where \(\Omega\) is a singleton, a polytope, or the image of a unit ball under a matrix linear-fractional mapping. If \(K\in\mathbf R^{n_u\times n}\) is constant and \(u=Kx\), then the control law is linear constant state feedback and \(K\) is its state-feedback gain. Substitution yields the closed-loop LDI \(\dot x=(A(t)+B_u(t)K)x+B_w(t)w\) and \(z=(C_z(t)+D_{zu}(t)K)x+D_{zw}(t)w\). State-feedback synthesis seeks a matrix \(K\) such that this closed-loop LDI satisfies prescribed specifications, such as stability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the stated uncertain linear differential inclusion, a constant control law u = Kx is linear constant state feedback, and K is the state-feedback gain. Substituting the law produces closed-loop state and output matrices A(t) + Bu(t)K and Cz(t) + Dzu(t)K. State-feedback synthesis searches for a gain that gives the closed-loop inclusion specified properties such as stability.
assumptions_latex: \Omega\text{ is a singleton, a polytope, or a matrix linear-fractional image of a unit ball}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \dot x=(A(t)+B_u(t)K)x+B_w(t)w,\qquad z=(C_z(t)+D_{zu}(t)K)x+D_{zw}(t)w.

review_flags: exact fixed-order dynamic output-feedback source required
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-order continuous-time dynamic output feedback in direct controller coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a fixed-order dynamic output-feedback controller with parameters \(K\), the bounded-real inequality contains the term \(A_{\mathrm{cl}}(K)^{\mathsf T}P+P A_{\mathrm{cl}}(K)\). Since \(A_{\mathrm{cl}}(K)\) depends affinely on controller matrices, this expression contains products between \(P\) and \(K\). Thus the feasibility set in the direct variables \((P,K,\gamma)\) is generally nonconvex and is not an LMI feasible set. Convexification requires additional structure, a change of variables with compatibility conditions, or a relaxation; fixing either \(P\) or \(K\) removes the corresponding bilinearity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Direct fixed-order output-feedback H-infinity synthesis couples controller and Lyapunov variables bilinearly, so its feasible set is generally nonconvex.

children.title: Robust H-Infinity Synthesis
children.top_down_role: Worst-case performance models with structured uncertainty.

knowledge_statements.title: Robust H-Infinity Synthesis
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Common-quadratic full-state-feedback synthesis for a continuous-time polytopic generalized plant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At every vertex \(i\in\{1,\ldots,N\}\), consider \(\dot x=A_i x+B_{1,i}w+B_{2,i}u\), \(z=C_{1,i}x+D_{11,i}w+D_{12,i}u\), and the feedback law \(u=Kx\). If common variables \(X\in\mathbb S^n\), \(Y\), and \(\gamma>0\) satisfy \(X\succ0\) and
\[\begin{bmatrix}\operatorname{He}(A_iX+B_{2,i}Y)&B_{1,i}&(C_{1,i}X+D_{12,i}Y)^{\mathsf T}\\ B_{1,i}^{\mathsf T}&-\gamma I&D_{11,i}^{\mathsf T}\\ C_{1,i}X+D_{12,i}Y&D_{11,i}&-\gamma I\end{bmatrix}\prec0\]
for every vertex, where \(\operatorname{He}(M)=M+M^{\mathsf T}\), then \(K=YX^{-1}\) provides a common quadratic certificate for every joint convex combination of the vertex data. Each resulting closed loop is asymptotically stable and has induced \(L_2\)-gain from \(w\) to \(z\) strictly below \(\gamma\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Common vertexwise bounded-real LMIs produce one state-feedback gain that certifies robust stability and an H-infinity bound throughout a polytopic plant family.
assumptions_latex: The vertex index set is \(\{1,\ldots,N\}\), and all vertex realizations have compatible finite dimensions.
Uncertainty consists of joint convex combinations of \((A_i,B_{1,i},B_{2,i},C_{1,i},D_{11,i},D_{12,i})\).
Full-state feedback \(u=Kx\) is used, and the displayed LMIs are strictly feasible with common \(X\), \(Y\), and \(\gamma\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The gain \(K=YX^{-1}\) robustly stabilizes every joint convex combination and gives induced \(L_2\)-gain below \(\gamma\).

If there exist symmetric matrices \(P\succ0\) and \(Q\succ0\) satisfying
\[\begin{bmatrix}A^{\mathsf T}P+PA+Q&PA_d\\ A_d^{\mathsf T}P&-Q\end{bmatrix}\prec0,\]

\[V(x_t)=x(t)^{\mathsf T}Px(t)+\int_{t-h}^{t}x(s)^{\mathsf T}Qx(s)\,ds\]
has a strictly negative derivative along every nonzero trajectory. Consequently, the zero solution is asymptotically stable. The condition is sufficient and delay-independent, so it may be conservative for a prescribed value of \(h\).

children.title: Stochastic-System LMIs
children.top_down_role: LMI interfaces for systems with stochastic or multiplicative-noise effects.

assumptions_latex: The state obeys the Itô equation \(dx=Ax\,dt+\sum_{k=1}^m N_kx\,dW_k\).
The processes \(W_1,\ldots,W_m\) are independent standard Wiener processes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed LMI is equivalent to exponential mean-square stability.
review_flags: authoritative locator for the exact Itô formulation is missing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional continuous-time Itô systems with multiplicative state noise.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The origin is exponentially stable in mean square if and only if there exists a symmetric matrix \(P\succ0\) such that
\[A^{\mathsf T}P+PA+\sum_{k=1}^{m}N_k^{\mathsf T}PN_k\prec0.\]
Equivalently, for \(V(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Px\), the infinitesimal generator satisfies \(\mathcal LV(x)<0\) for every \(x\neq0\). Here exponential mean-square stability means that constants \(c>0\) and \(\alpha>0\) exist with \(\mathbb E\lVert x(t)\rVert^2\leq c e^{-\alpha t}\mathbb E\lVert x(0)\rVert^2\) for all \(t\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A linear Itô system is exponentially mean-square stable exactly when one positive matrix satisfies its stochastic Lyapunov LMI.
knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic-System LMIs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated finite-dimensional Itô Lyapunov equivalence is standard and internally precise, but the exact if-and-only-if formulation has no cited source or inspectable locator.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If a symmetric matrix \(P\succ0\) exists such that
\[A_i^{\mathsf T}P+PA_i\prec0\qquad\text{for every }i\in\{1,\ldots,r\},\]
then the same inequality holds for every matrix \(A(\lambda)=\sum_{i=1}^{r}\lambda_iA_i\) with \(\lambda_i\geq0\) and \(\sum_i\lambda_i=1\). Hence \(V(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Px\) decreases uniformly along every nonzero trajectory of the inclusion, and the origin is uniformly exponentially stable for all measurable convex combinations, including arbitrary switching among the vertices.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The direct quadratic stability constraint
\[A_{\mathrm{cl}}(K)^{\mathsf T}P+P A_{\mathrm{cl}}(K)\prec0,\qquad P\succ0,\]
is affine in \(P\) when \(K\) is fixed and affine in \(K\) when \(P\) is fixed, but generally contains products of entries of \(P\) and \(K\) when both vary. It is therefore a bilinear matrix inequality, not an LMI, and its joint feasible set can be nonconvex. An exact SDP formulation requires special structure and an invertible change of variables; otherwise alternating minimization or convex relaxation does not establish global optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Jointly optimizing a controller and quadratic certificate usually creates bilinear matrix terms, marking the boundary beyond direct semidefinite modeling.

knowledge_statements.title: Max-Cut Vector Lifts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unit-vector relaxation of weighted undirected Max-Cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a weighted undirected graph \(G=(V,E)\) with \(V=\{1,\ldots,n\}\) and weights \(w_{ij}\geq0\), a sign vector \(s\in\{-1,1\}^n\) has cut value
\[\operatorname{cut}(s)=\frac12\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E}w_{ij}(1-s_is_j).\]
The vector lift replaces the signs by unit vectors \(v_i\in\mathbb R^r\) and uses
\[\max\ \frac12\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E}w_{ij}(1-v_i^{\mathsf T}v_j)\quad\text{subject to}\quad \lVert v_i\rVert_2=1\ \text{for every }i\in V.\]
Every sign solution is represented by \(v_i=s_i u\) for any fixed unit vector \(u\), so the lifted optimum is an upper bound on the maximum cut value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a weighted graph, the Max-Cut vector lift replaces each sign by a unit vector and each sign product by an inner product, yielding an upper-bound relaxation.
assumptions_latex: The weighted undirected graph is \(G=(V,E)\), where \(V=\{1,\ldots,n\}\) and \(w_{ij}\geq0\) for every \(\{i,j\}\in E\).
The lifted vectors belong to a common finite-dimensional space \(\mathbb R^r\) and satisfy \(\lVert v_i\rVert_2=1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The lifted vector program is the standard Max-Cut semidefinite relaxation in vector form and upper-bounds the maximum cut value.

notation.meaning: weighted undirected graph with vertex and edge sets
unit vector assigned to vertex i
fixed unit vector used to embed a sign solution
weighted value of the cut encoded by s

children.title: Max-Cut Gram-Matrix Lifts
children.top_down_role: PSD Gram representations used for basic Max-Cut relaxation.

knowledge_statements.title: Max-Cut Gram-Matrix Lifts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Elliptope lift of weighted undirected Max-Cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a weighted undirected graph with \(V=\{1,\ldots,n\}\), weights \(w_{ij}\geq0\), and weighted Laplacian \(L\) defined by \(L_{ii}=\sum_{j:\{i,j\}\in E}w_{ij}\), \(L_{ij}=-w_{ij}\) on edges, and \(L_{ij}=0\) otherwise. For \(s\in\{-1,1\}^n\), the matrix \(X=ss^{\mathsf T}\) satisfies \(X\succeq0\), \(\operatorname{diag}(X)=\mathbf1\), and \(\operatorname{rank}(X)=1\). Dropping the rank constraint gives
\[\max_{X\in\mathbb S^n}\ \frac14\langle L,X\rangle\quad\text{subject to}\quad X\succeq0,\qquad \operatorname{diag}(X)=\mathbf1.\]
Its objective also equals \(\frac12\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E}w_{ij}(1-X_{ij})\). Every cut matrix is feasible, so the SDP optimum upper-bounds the maximum cut value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a weighted graph, lifting sign products to a positive semidefinite matrix and dropping rank one gives the elliptope relaxation and an upper bound on Max-Cut.
assumptions_latex: The weighted undirected graph is \(G=(V,E)\), where \(V=\{1,\ldots,n\}\) and \(w_{ij}\geq0\).
The matrix variable belongs to \(\mathbb S^n\), and \(L\) uses the stated weighted-Laplacian convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The elliptope program is an SDP relaxation whose value upper-bounds the maximum cut value.

notation.meaning: all-ones vector in the relevant dimension
weighted graph Laplacian under the stated convention

children.title: Vector–Gram Representation Equivalence
children.top_down_role: Structural correspondence between the vector and matrix viewpoints.

knowledge_statements.title: Vector–Gram Representation Equivalence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional equivalence underlying the vector and Gram forms of the Max-Cut SDP relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(X\in\mathbb S^n\), the conditions \(X\succeq0\) and \(X_{ii}=1\) for every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\) hold if and only if there are unit vectors \(v_1,\ldots,v_n\in\mathbb R^r\), for some \(r\leq n\), such that
\[X_{ij}=v_i^{\mathsf T}v_j\qquad\text{for all }i,j\in\{1,\ldots,n\}.\]
Under this correspondence, any objective depending linearly on the entries \(X_{ij}\) has the same value in the Gram-matrix and unit-vector representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive semidefinite matrix with unit diagonal is exactly a Gram matrix of unit vectors, so the vector and matrix Max-Cut formulations are equivalent.
assumptions_latex: The matrix \(X\) is a real symmetric \(n\)-by-\(n\) matrix.
The representing vectors may belong to any finite-dimensional Euclidean space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Unit-vector families and positive-semidefinite matrices with unit diagonal describe the same feasible representations.

notation.meaning: vectors whose pairwise inner products form X
ambient Gram-factor dimension, which may be chosen no larger than n

knowledge_statements.title: Strengthened Max-Cut Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Metric-inequality strengthening of the elliptope relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \([n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}\), let \(X\in\mathbb S^n\) satisfy \(X\succeq0\) and \(X_{ii}=1\) for every \(i\in[n]\), and define \(y_{ij}=(1-X_{ij})/2\) for distinct \(i,j\in[n]\). For every three distinct indices \(i,j,k\in[n]\), impose
\[y_{ij}\leq y_{ik}+y_{jk},\qquad y_{ik}\leq y_{ij}+y_{jk},\qquad y_{jk}\leq y_{ij}+y_{ik},\qquad y_{ij}+y_{ik}+y_{jk}\leq2.\]
These inequalities are valid for every cut-incidence vector in \(\operatorname{CUT}_n\). Their intersection with the elliptope preserves all discrete cuts and may remove fractional elliptope points. For a Max-Cut maximization objective, the strengthened optimum remains an upper bound on the maximum cut value and is no larger than the base SDP optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Triangle and perimeter inequalities preserve every cut while potentially removing fractional elliptope points, thereby tightening the Max-Cut upper bound.
assumptions_latex: The base relaxation has \(X\in\mathbb S^n\), \(X\succeq0\), and \(X_{ii}=1\) for every \(i\in[n]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Adding all displayed triangle and perimeter inequalities yields a valid tightening of the Max-Cut SDP relaxation.

notation.meaning: relaxed separation variable for vertices i and j
convex hull of cut-incidence vectors on n labeled vertices

children.title: Random-Hyperplane Rounding
children.top_down_role: Geometric randomized rounding interfaces for Max-Cut SDP solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Random-Hyperplane Rounding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Goemans–Williamson hyperplane rounding of a feasible Max-Cut vector solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given feasible unit vectors \(v_1,\ldots,v_n\in\mathbb R^r\), sample \(g\) uniformly from the unit sphere \(\mathbb S^{r-1}\) and set
\[s_i=\begin{cases}1,&g^{\mathsf T}v_i\geq0,\\-1,&g^{\mathsf T}v_i<0.\end{cases}\]
Return the cut \(S=\{i\in V:s_i=1\}\). For every pair \(i,j\in V\),
\[\Pr(s_i\neq s_j)=\frac{\arccos(v_i^{\mathsf T}v_j)}{\pi}.\]
For a weighted graph \(G=(V,E)\), its expected cut weight is
\[\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E}w_{ij}\frac{\arccos(v_i^{\mathsf T}v_j)}{\pi}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sample a random hyperplane through the origin and use its two sides as a cut; each pair is separated with probability equal to its angle divided by pi.
assumptions_latex: The weighted undirected graph is \(G=(V,E)\), with \(V=\{1,\ldots,n\}\) and weights \(w_{ij}\geq0\).
Feasible unit vectors \(v_1,\ldots,v_n\in\mathbb R^r\) are available from the Max-Cut vector relaxation.
The direction \(g\) is uniformly distributed on \(\mathbb S^{r-1}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The signs define a cut, and each pair \(i,j\) is separated with probability \(\arccos(v_i^{\mathsf T}v_j)/\pi\).

notation.meaning: feasible unit vector assigned to vertex i
uniform random unit normal to the rounding hyperplane
recovered cut sign for vertex i

children.title: Discrete Cut Recovery
children.top_down_role: Interfaces connecting relaxed solutions to feasible graph cuts.

knowledge_statements.title: Discrete Cut Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite candidate selection for recovering a verifiable feasible cut from a Max-Cut SDP factor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a weighted undirected graph with \(V=\{1,\ldots,n\}\), and let \(X=V_X^{\mathsf T}V_X\) be a Gram factorization of a feasible Max-Cut SDP point, with columns \(v_1,\ldots,v_n\). Given \(T\in\mathbb N\) with \(T\geq1\) and nonzero directions \(g_1,\ldots,g_T\), form
\[s_i^{(t)}=\operatorname{sign}(g_t^{\mathsf T}v_i)\]
for every \(i\in V\) and \(t\in\{1,\ldots,T\}\), choosing either sign when the inner product is zero. Compute
\[W_t=\frac12\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E}w_{ij}(1-s_i^{(t)}s_j^{(t)}),\]
choose \(t^\star\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{1\leq t\leq T}W_t\), and return \(S=\{i\in V:s_i^{(t^\star)}=1\}\). The returned signs define a feasible cut, and \(W_{t^\star}\) is a directly verifiable lower bound on the maximum cut value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Project the SDP vectors onto finitely many directions, form one cut from each sign pattern, and return the candidate with the greatest computed weight.
assumptions_latex: The weighted undirected graph is \(G=(V,E)\), where \(V=\{1,\ldots,n\}\) and \(w_{ij}\geq0\).
A Gram factorization \(X=V_X^{\mathsf T}V_X\) of a feasible Max-Cut SDP point is available.
The number of trials satisfies \(T\in\mathbb N\) and \(T\geq1\), and each trial direction \(g_t\) is nonzero and dimensionally compatible with the Gram vectors.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned sign vector is Max-Cut feasible, and its computed weight \(W_{t^\star}\) is a verifiable lower bound on the optimum.

notation.meaning: matrix in a Gram factorization of X
column of the Gram factor associated with vertex i
candidate cut-sign vector from trial t
computed weight of the trial-t cut

children.title: Approximation Guarantees
children.top_down_role: Quality guarantees associated with Max-Cut rounding families.

assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is a finite undirected graph with nonnegative edge weights \(w_{ij}\).
\(X^\star\) is optimal for the displayed Max-Cut SDP.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[w(\delta(S))]\ge \alpha_{\mathrm{GW}}\operatorname{SDP}(G)\ge \alpha_{\mathrm{GW}}\operatorname{OPT}(G)\).

notation.meaning: weight of the cut induced by S

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expected guarantee for random-hyperplane rounding of the standard weighted Max-Cut SDP.

source_refs.locator: 2.2 Applications of Semidefinite Optimization p. 25
source_refs.source_title: Semidefinite Optimization and Convex Algebraic Geometry

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define
\[\operatorname{SDP}(G)=\max\left\{\frac12\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E}w_{ij}(1-X_{ij}):X\succeq0,\ X_{ii}=1\ \text{for all }i\in V\right\}.\]
Factor \(X^\star\) as \(X^\star_{ij}=\langle v_i,v_j\rangle\), choose a uniformly random hyperplane through the origin, and place vertices on opposite sides according to the signs of their projections. Then
\[\mathbb E[w(\delta(S))]\ge\alpha_{\mathrm{GW}}\operatorname{SDP}(G)\ge\alpha_{\mathrm{GW}}\operatorname{OPT}(G),\qquad \alpha_{\mathrm{GW}}=\min_{-1\le\rho<1}\frac{(2/\pi)\arccos(\rho)}{1-\rho}\approx0.87856.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Random-hyperplane rounding of an optimal Max-Cut SDP solution returns a cut whose expected weight is at least 0.87856 times the maximum cut weight.
knowledge_statements.title: Approximation Guarantees

children.title: Integrality-Gap Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Instances and regimes limiting relaxation-based approximation quality.

assumptions_latex: \(G\) ranges over finite undirected graphs with nonnegative edge weights.
The relaxation uses the standard unit-diagonal Max-Cut SDP.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha_{\mathrm{GW}}\le \operatorname{OPT}(G)/\operatorname{SDP}(G)\le1\), and the lower boundary is approached by a graph sequence.

notation.meaning: Max-Cut optimum divided by its SDP upper bound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case boundary for the standard Max-Cut SDP, expressed in approximation-ratio convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every nontrivial weighted instance,
\[\alpha_{\mathrm{GW}}\le r(G):=\frac{\operatorname{OPT}(G)}{\operatorname{SDP}(G)}\le1.\]
Moreover, the boundary is asymptotically tight: for every \(\varepsilon>0\), there exists a finite graph \(G_\varepsilon\) such that
\[r(G_\varepsilon)\le\alpha_{\mathrm{GW}}+\varepsilon.\]
Equivalently, under the reciprocal convention the worst-case integrality gap satisfies
\[\sup_G\frac{\operatorname{SDP}(G)}{\operatorname{OPT}(G)}=\frac1{\alpha_{\mathrm{GW}}}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The standard Max-Cut SDP has worst-case optimum-to-relaxation ratio 0.87856; graph families approach this boundary, so its reciprocal integrality gap is sharp.
knowledge_statements.title: Integrality-Gap Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The universal ratio bound follows from the approximation theorem, but the asserted asymptotic tightness and reciprocal worst-case gap require an authoritative source with a theorem, section, or page locator. No source is cited, so the sharp boundary cannot be accepted at the stated confidence.

children.title: Primal Theta SDP
children.top_down_role: Primal matrix formulation of the stable-set theta bound.

assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is a finite simple graph with \(n=|V|\ge1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed SDP value is \(\vartheta(G)\).

notation.meaning: all-ones matrix in the vertex ordering

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Trace-normalized primal SDP in the stable-set convention for the Lovász theta number.

source_refs.locator: 2.2 Applications of Semidefinite Optimization p. 25
source_refs.source_title: Semidefinite Optimization and Convex Algebraic Geometry

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
In the stable-set convention, the Lovász theta number is represented by
\[\vartheta(G)=\max_{X\in\mathbb S^n}\left\{\langle J,X\rangle:\operatorname{Tr}(X)=1,\ X_{ij}=0\ \text{for every }\{i,j\}\in E,\ X\succeq0\right\}.\]
The variable \(X\) is indexed by \(V\), and each undirected edge imposes one symmetric zero constraint. The trace normalization makes the feasible set bounded, while positive semidefiniteness makes it closed and convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The stable-set theta number maximizes the all-ones inner product over positive semidefinite, trace-one matrices whose edge entries vanish.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal Theta SDP

children.title: Dual Theta SDP
children.top_down_role: Dual matrix formulation of the stable-set theta bound.

assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is a finite simple graph with \(n=|V|\ge1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed minimization is the conic dual of the trace-normalized primal theta SDP.

notation.meaning: symmetric matrix supported on graph edges

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual SDP paired with the trace-normalized stable-set formulation.

source_refs.locator: 2 Semidefinite Optimization p. 3
source_refs.source_title: Semidefinite Optimization and Convex Algebraic Geometry

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The conic dual representation is
\[\vartheta(G)=\min_{t\in\mathbb R,\,Z\in\mathbb S^n}\left\{t:tI+Z-J\succeq0,\ Z_{ii}=0\ \text{for all }i,\ Z_{ij}=0\ \text{whenever }i\ne j\ \text{and }\{i,j\}\notin E\right\}.\]
Thus \(Z\) may have nonzero entries only at off-diagonal positions corresponding to edges. Its entries are unrestricted in sign; they are the multipliers for the primal edge-zero equalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The dual minimizes a scalar t such that tI plus an edge-supported symmetric matrix dominates the all-ones matrix semidefinitely.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual Theta SDP

children.title: Theta Representation Equivalence
children.top_down_role: Correspondence among equivalent primal and dual theta formulations.

assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is a finite simple graph with at least one vertex.
The primal and dual use the support and normalization conventions displayed in their records.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The primal maximum and dual minimum are attained and equal to \(\vartheta(G)\).

notation.meaning: optimal values of the paired theta programs

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional strong duality and attainment for the displayed primal-dual theta pair.

source_refs.locator: 2 Semidefinite Optimization p. 3
source_refs.source_title: Semidefinite Optimization and Convex Algebraic Geometry

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(p^\star\) be the maximum in the trace-normalized primal theta SDP and let \(d^\star\) be the minimum in its edge-supported dual formulation. For every finite simple graph with at least one vertex, both displayed programs are strictly feasible, their finite optimal values are attained, and
\[p^\star=d^\star=\vartheta(G).\]
Thus the two programs are equivalent representations under the stated graph, support, and normalization conventions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For every nonempty finite simple graph, the displayed primal and dual theta programs are strictly feasible, attain their optima, and have the common value given by the Lovász theta number.
knowledge_statements.title: Theta Representation Equivalence

children.title: Theta Attainment Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Structural regimes affecting attainment or representation correspondence.

assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is a finite simple graph with \(n=|V|\ge1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Both optima of the normalized theta pair are attained, whereas removing the primal trace normalization makes the primal objective unbounded above.

notation.meaning: feasible set of the trace-normalized primal theta SDP

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Attainment in finite dimensions and failure of finiteness after removal of the primal trace normalization.

source_refs.locator: 2.1 From Linear to Semidefinite Optimization p. 3
source_refs.source_title: Semidefinite Optimization and Convex Algebraic Geometry

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the trace-normalized primal theta SDP, the feasible set
\[\mathcal F_G=\left\{X\in\mathbb S^n:X\succeq0,\ \operatorname{Tr}(X)=1,\ X_{ij}=0\ \text{for every }\{i,j\}\in E\right\}\]
is nonempty and compact, and the primal maximum is attained. The paired edge-supported dual also attains its minimum. If the trace equation is removed from the primal, the resulting problem is unbounded above: for every \(\lambda\ge0\), the matrix \(X=\lambda I\) is feasible and has objective value
\[\langle J,X\rangle=\lambda n.\]
Accordingly, the unnormalized primal does not define a finite theta value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The normalized finite-dimensional theta pair attains both optima. Removing the primal trace equation permits arbitrarily large scalar identity matrices and makes the primal objective unbounded.
knowledge_statements.title: Theta Attainment Boundaries

children.title: Orthonormal-Representation View
children.top_down_role: Geometric graph representations underlying theta bounds.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The minimum over orthonormal representations and handles equals \(\vartheta(G)\).

notation.meaning: unit vector assigned to vertex i

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric representation using the convention that nonadjacent vertices receive orthogonal vectors.

source_refs.locator: 2.2 Applications of Semidefinite Optimization p. 25
source_refs.source_title: Semidefinite Optimization and Convex Algebraic Geometry

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An orthonormal representation of \(G\) is a family of unit vectors \((u_i)_{i\in V}\) in some Euclidean space such that
\[\langle u_i,u_j\rangle=0\qquad\text{whenever }i\ne j\text{ and }\{i,j\}\notin E.\]
For a unit handle \(c\), interpret a zero denominator as \(+\infty\). Then the stable-set-convention theta number satisfies
\[\vartheta(G)=\min_{(u_i),\,\|c\|=1}\ \max_{i\in V}\frac{1}{\langle c,u_i\rangle^2}.\]
The ambient Euclidean dimension may be restricted to a finite dimension no larger than \(|V|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Theta is the smallest worst reciprocal squared handle projection over unit-vector representations in which every nonadjacent vertex pair is orthogonal.
knowledge_statements.title: Orthonormal-Representation View

children.title: Weighted Stable-Set Theta Variants
children.top_down_role: Vertex-weighted and support-function extensions.

assumptions_latex: \(w\in\mathbb R_+^V\) is a nonnegative vertex-weight vector.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha(G,w)\le\vartheta(G,w)\), with equality of the weighted and unweighted notation when \(w=\mathbf1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Support-function extension of the graph theta relaxation to nonnegative vertex weights.

source_refs.locator: 2.2 Applications of Semidefinite Optimization p. 25
source_refs.source_title: Semidefinite Optimization and Convex Algebraic Geometry

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the graph theta body by
\[\operatorname{TH}(G)=\left\{x\in\mathbb R^V:\exists X\in\mathbb S^V,\ \begin{pmatrix}1&x^{\mathsf T}\\x&X\end{pmatrix}\succeq0,\ X_{ii}=x_i,\ X_{ij}=0\ \text{for }\{i,j\}\in E\right\}.\]
The weighted theta value is its support function
\[\vartheta(G,w)=\max\left\{w^{\mathsf T}x:x\in\operatorname{TH}(G)\right\}.\]
Every stable-set incidence vector belongs to \(\operatorname{TH}(G)\); therefore
\[\alpha(G,w):=\max_{S\text{ stable}}\sum_{i\in S}w_i\le\vartheta(G,w),\qquad \vartheta(G,\mathbf1)=\vartheta(G).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The weighted theta number is the support function of the graph theta body and upper-bounds the maximum total weight of a stable set.
knowledge_statements.title: Weighted Stable-Set Theta Variants

children.title: Complement-Graph Theta Relations
children.top_down_role: Theta relationships induced by graph complementation.

assumptions_latex: \(G\) is a finite simple graph on \(n\ge1\) vertices.
\(\overline G\) denotes the simple complement of \(G\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\vartheta(G)\vartheta(\overline G)\ge n\), with equality for vertex-transitive \(G\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Product relation between theta numbers of a graph and its complement.

source_refs.locator: 2.2 Applications of Semidefinite Optimization p. 25
source_refs.source_title: Semidefinite Optimization and Convex Algebraic Geometry

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every finite simple graph \(G\) on \(n\) vertices, the Lovász theta numbers of complementary graphs obey
\[\vartheta(G)\,\vartheta(\overline G)\ge n.\]
If the automorphism group of \(G\) acts transitively on its vertices, then equality holds:
\[\vartheta(G)\,\vartheta(\overline G)=n.\]
Since vertex transitivity is preserved by complementation, this equality is symmetric in \(G\) and \(\overline G\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Theta values of complementary graphs have product at least the vertex count, and the product equals that count for vertex-transitive graphs.
knowledge_statements.title: Complement-Graph Theta Relations

children.title: Coloring Bounds
children.top_down_role: Theta-based bounds connected to graph coloring.

assumptions_latex: \(\chi(\overline G)\) is the chromatic number of its complement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\vartheta(G)\le\chi(\overline G)\), equivalently \(\vartheta(\overline G)\le\chi(G)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Theta upper bound by coloring in the complementary-graph convention.

source_refs.locator: 2.2 Applications of Semidefinite Optimization p. 25
source_refs.source_title: Semidefinite Optimization and Convex Algebraic Geometry

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every finite simple graph \(G\),
\[\vartheta(G)\le\chi(\overline G).\]
Equivalently, after replacing \(G\) by its complement,
\[\vartheta(\overline G)\le\chi(G).\]
Thus any proper coloring of \(\overline G\) supplies an integer upper bound on the stable-set-convention theta value of \(G\), while a theta computation supplies a lower bound on the chromatic number of \(\overline G\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The theta number of a graph does not exceed the chromatic number of its complement, so theta also lower-bounds complementary coloring.
knowledge_statements.title: Coloring Bounds

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An affine linear polynomial \(\ell\in\mathbb R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\) is \(k\)-sums of squares modulo \(I\) if there exist polynomials \(h_1,\ldots,h_m\) with \(\deg h_j\le k\) such that
\[\ell-\sum_{j=1}^m h_j^2\in I.\]
The \(k\)-th theta body of \(I\) is
\[\operatorname{TH}_k(I)=\left\{x\in\mathbb R^n:\ell(x)\ge0\ \text{for every affine linear }\ell\text{ that is }k\text{-sums of squares modulo }I\right\}.\]
In particular, \(\operatorname{cl}(\operatorname{conv}(V_{\mathbb R}(I)))\subseteq\operatorname{TH}_k(I)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A theta body consists of points satisfying every affine inequality having a bounded-degree sum-of-squares certificate modulo the chosen polynomial ideal.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Theta bodies and \((1,k)\)-SOS ideals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ideal-based theta-body hierarchy associated with the real variety of a polynomial ideal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I=\langle g_1,\ldots,g_m\rangle\subseteq\mathbb R[\mathbf x]\) and \(\mathbf K=V_{\mathbb R}(I)\). An affine-linear polynomial \(\ell\in\mathbb R[\mathbf x]_1\) is \(k\)-SOS modulo \(I\) if \(\ell\equiv\sigma\pmod I\) for some \(\sigma\in\Sigma[\mathbf x]_k\). The \(k\)-th theta body is \[\operatorname{TH}_k(I)=\{\mathbf x\in\mathbb R^n:\ell(\mathbf x)\geq0\text{ for every }\ell\in\mathbb R[\mathbf x]_1\text{ that is }k\text{-SOS modulo }I\}.\] The hierarchy satisfies \(\operatorname{TH}_1(I)\supseteq\operatorname{TH}_2(I)\supseteq\cdots\supseteq\operatorname{TH}_k(I)\supseteq\cdots\supseteq\mathbf K\). The ideal \(I\) is \((1,k)\)-SOS if every \(\ell\in\mathbb R[\mathbf x]_1\) nonnegative on \(\operatorname{conv}(V_{\mathbb R}(I))\) is \(k\)-SOS modulo \(I\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an ideal defining a real algebraic variety, the kth theta body is the set of points satisfying every affine-linear inequality that is SOS modulo the ideal at level k. These bodies form a nested outer hierarchy containing the variety. The ideal is (1,k)-SOS when every affine-linear polynomial nonnegative on the convex hull of its real variety has such a certificate.
assumptions_latex: \mathbf K=V_{\mathbb R}(I)=\{\mathbf x\in\mathbb R^n:g_j(\mathbf x)=0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{TH}_1(I)\supseteq\operatorname{TH}_2(I)\supseteq\cdots\supseteq\operatorname{TH}_k(I)\supseteq\cdots\supseteq\mathbf K,\qquad I\text{ is }(1,k)\text{-SOS}\iff\forall\ell\in\mathbb R[\mathbf x]_1,\ \ell\geq0\text{ on }\operatorname{conv}(V_{\mathbb R}(I))\Rightarrow\ell\text{ is }k\text{-SOS modulo }I.
