children.title: Lifted Graph Relaxations
children.top_down_role: Higher-dimensional PSD lifts for graph optimization models.

knowledge_statements.title: Lifted Graph Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Order-k moment lift for the stable-set ideal of a finite graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) and \(I_G=\langle x_i^2-x_i,\ x_ix_j:\{i,j\}\in E\rangle\). An order-\(k\) lifted relaxation uses a linear functional \(L:\mathbb R[x]_{\le 2k}\to\mathbb R\) satisfying \(L(1)=1\), \(L(p)=0\) for every \(p\in I_G\cap\mathbb R[x]_{\le 2k}\), and \(L(q^2)\ge0\) for every \(q\in\mathbb R[x]_{\le k}\). Equivalently, \(M_k(L)\succeq0\) and the ideal-induced linear equations hold. Projection by \(y_i=L(x_i)\) gives a convex outer approximation of \(\operatorname{STAB}(G)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A truncated positive moment matrix satisfying the stable-set ideal equations projects to a convex relaxation containing every stable-set incidence vector.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\operatorname{STAB}(G)\subseteq\{(L(x_i))_{i\in V}:L(1)=1,\ M_k(L)\succeq0,\ L(I_G\cap\mathbb R[x]_{\le2k})=0\}.\]

notation.meaning: moment matrix indexed by monomials of degree at most k

children.title: Algebraic Strengthening Variants
children.top_down_role: Algebraically generated variants with differing relaxation strength.

knowledge_statements.title: Algebraic Strengthening Variants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotonic strengthening obtained by increasing the degree of ideal-based sum-of-squares certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the stable-set ideal \(I_G\), define \(\mathrm{TH}_k(I_G)\) as the set of points at which every affine polynomial congruent modulo \(I_G\) to a sum of squares of polynomials of degree at most \(k\) is nonnegative. Increasing the certificate degree enlarges the collection of certified affine inequalities, so \(\mathrm{TH}_{k+1}(I_G)\subseteq\mathrm{TH}_k(I_G)\). Every level contains the convex hull of the real variety; for \(I_G\), this convex hull is \(\operatorname{STAB}(G)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Higher-degree sum-of-squares certificates yield successively tighter theta bodies, all of which contain the stable-set polytope.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\operatorname{STAB}(G)\subseteq\mathrm{TH}_{k+1}(I_G)\subseteq\mathrm{TH}_k(I_G).\]

notation.meaning: order-k theta body of the ideal

children.title: Combinatorial Arrangement SDP Family
children.top_down_role: Equipartition, quadratic-assignment, and traveling-salesperson relaxation families.

children.title: Graph-Partition SDPs
children.top_down_role: Semidefinite relaxations for partition or equipartition problems.

knowledge_statements.title: Graph-Partition SDPs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Moment-matrix relaxation for a prescribed-size vertex partition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_{ir}\) indicate that vertex \(i\) belongs to part \(r\), whose prescribed size is \(m_r\). Replace \(xx^\top\) by \(Y\) and impose \(\begin{pmatrix}1&x^\top\\x&Y\end{pmatrix}\succeq0\), \(Y_{(i,r),(i,r)}=x_{ir}\), \(\sum_r x_{ir}=1\), and \(\sum_i x_{ir}=m_r\). Valid linearizations of the assignment equations may also be imposed. For edge weights \(w_{ij}\), the relaxed cut objective is \(\frac12\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E}w_{ij}\sum_r(x_{ir}+x_{jr}-2Y_{(i,r),(j,r)})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partition indicators and their products are lifted into a positive semidefinite moment matrix while assignment, part-size, and cut-cost relations remain linear.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Dropping \(Y=xx^\top\) produces an SDP relaxation whose feasible set contains every prescribed-size graph partition.

children.title: Quadratic-Assignment SDPs
children.top_down_role: Semidefinite relaxations for quadratic assignment models.

knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic-Assignment SDPs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order matrix lift of the quadratic assignment problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For facilities and locations indexed by \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\), let \(x_{ir}\) be permutation-assignment variables and set \(x=\operatorname{vec}(x_{ir})\). The rank-one formulation uses \(Y=xx^\top\), row and column assignment equations, and \(x_{ir}^2=x_{ir}\). Its SDP relaxation replaces rank one by \(\begin{pmatrix}1&x^\top\\x&Y\end{pmatrix}\succeq0\), retains \(Y_{(i,r),(i,r)}=x_{ir}\), and may impose valid linearizations of the assignment identities. The quadratic cost becomes \(\sum_{i,j,r,s}A_{ij}B_{rs}Y_{(i,r),(j,s)}+\sum_{i,r}C_{ir}x_{ir}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The quadratic assignment problem becomes an SDP relaxation by lifting products of permutation variables and dropping the lift's rank-one constraint.
assumptions_latex: \(A,B,C\) are real coefficient matrices of compatible dimensions.
Facilities and locations have the same finite cardinality \(n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every permutation assignment induces a feasible lifted point, so the minimization SDP value is a lower bound on the quadratic-assignment optimum.

children.title: Ordering SDPs
children.top_down_role: Semidefinite relaxations for permutation and ordering problems.

knowledge_statements.title: Ordering SDPs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Moment relaxation of the linear-ordering incidence formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For distinct items \(i,j\), let \(y_{ij}=1\) mean that \(i\) precedes \(j\). A total order satisfies \(y_{ij}+y_{ji}=1\), \(y_{ij}+y_{jk}+y_{ki}\le2\) for distinct \(i,j,k\), and \(y_{ij}^2=y_{ij}\). Introduce \(Y=yy^\top\) and relax this identity to \(\begin{pmatrix}1&y^\top\\y&Y\end{pmatrix}\succeq0\) with \(Y_{aa}=y_a\), while retaining the ordering equations, triangle inequalities, and any selected valid linearized products. A linear ordering objective remains linear in \(y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Binary precedence variables are augmented by a positive semidefinite product matrix, producing an outer relaxation of total-order incidence vectors.
assumptions_latex: The objective is linear in pairwise precedence indicators.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The projected SDP feasible region contains the linear-ordering polytope.

children.title: Traveling-Salesperson SDP Variants
children.top_down_role: Ordering-based SDP relaxations for traveling-salesperson models.

knowledge_statements.title: Traveling-Salesperson SDP Variants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Edge-incidence rank lift for the symmetric traveling-salesperson problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_e\) indicate whether edge \(e\) belongs to a Hamiltonian tour of the complete graph on \(n\) vertices. Tour vectors satisfy \(\sum_{e\in\delta(v)}x_e=2\), \(\sum_{e\in\delta(S)}x_e\ge2\) for every nonempty proper \(S\), and \(x_e^2=x_e\). An edge-lift SDP introduces \(Y\), imposes \(\begin{pmatrix}1&x^\top\\x&Y\end{pmatrix}\succeq0\) and \(Y_{ee}=x_e\), and retains a chosen collection of valid degree, subtour, and linearized consistency constraints. The tour cost is \(\sum_e c_ex_e\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: TSP variants strengthen degree and subtour relaxations by adding a positive semidefinite matrix representing products of tour-edge indicators.
assumptions_latex: The graph is complete and undirected with \(n\ge3\).
\(c_e\in\mathbb R\) is the cost of edge \(e\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every Hamiltonian-tour incidence vector has the feasible lift \(Y=xx^\top\), so each stated SDP is an outer relaxation.

notation.meaning: cut consisting of edges with exactly one endpoint in S

children.title: Invariant-Algebra Symmetry-Reduction Interface
children.top_down_role: Combinatorial bounds organized through invariant matrix algebras.

children.title: Association-Scheme Matrix Algebras
children.top_down_role: Invariant matrix-algebra representations arising from association schemes.

knowledge_statements.title: Association-Scheme Matrix Algebras
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bose–Mesner algebra of a finite commutative association scheme.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A commutative association scheme on a finite set \(\Omega\) is represented by zero-one matrices \(A_0,\ldots,A_d\) such that \(A_0=I\), \(\sum_{i=0}^dA_i=J\), the transpose of each \(A_i\) belongs to the collection, and \(A_iA_j=\sum_{k=0}^dp_{ij}^kA_k\) with \(p_{ij}^k\in\mathbb Z_+\), while all \(A_i\) commute. Its Bose–Mesner algebra is \(\mathcal A=\operatorname{span}\{A_0,\ldots,A_d\}\), a finite-dimensional commutative matrix \(*\)-algebra containing \(I\) and \(J\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An association scheme partitions ordered pairs into regular relations whose adjacency matrices span a commutative matrix algebra closed under transpose and multiplication.
assumptions_latex: The commutative convention for association schemes is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal A\) is closed under matrix multiplication and transpose and has basis \(\{A_0,\ldots,A_d\}\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Symmetric association scheme
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a symmetric association scheme through its symmetric zero-one adjacency matrices and records the resulting pairwise commutativity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A family \(\mathcal A=\{A_0,\ldots,A_l\}\) of symmetric \(0,1\)-matrices of order \(n\) is a symmetric association scheme if \(A_0=I\), \(\sum_{i=0}^l A_i=J\), and, for every \(i,j\), there exist numbers \(p_{ij}^k\) such that \(A_iA_j=\sum_{k=0}^l p_{ij}^kA_k\). These conditions imply \(A_iA_j=A_jA_i\) for all \(i,j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A symmetric association scheme is a family of symmetric zero-one matrices containing the identity, summing to the all-ones matrix, and closed under multiplication within their linear span. The matrices commute pairwise.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A_0=I,\quad \sum_{i=0}^lA_i=J,\quad \forall i,j\ \exists\{p_{ij}^k\}_{k=0}^l:\ A_iA_j=\sum_{k=0}^lp_{ij}^kA_k;\qquad \forall i,j,\ A_iA_j=A_jA_i.

children.title: Symmetry-Reduced SDPs
children.top_down_role: Reduced semidefinite models obtained from problem symmetries.

knowledge_statements.title: Symmetry-Reduced SDPs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Group averaging reduction for invariant semidefinite programs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider an SDP whose objective and affine feasible set \(\mathcal F\) are invariant under \(X\mapsto P_gXP_g^\top\) for every \(g\) in a finite group \(\Gamma\), where each \(P_g\) is orthogonal. For every feasible \(X\), the Reynolds average \(\bar X=|\Gamma|^{-1}\sum_{g\in\Gamma}P_gXP_g^\top\) is feasible, has the same objective value, is positive semidefinite, and satisfies \(P_g\bar X=\bar XP_g\) for every \(g\). Thus restriction to the commutant preserves the infimum; if an optimum is attained, an invariant optimum exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Averaging any feasible SDP matrix over a finite symmetry group preserves feasibility and value, so restricting optimization to invariant matrices preserves the infimum.
assumptions_latex: \(\Gamma\) is a finite group with an orthogonal matrix representation.
All objective and constraint data are invariant under the induced conjugation action.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\inf_{X\in\mathcal F}\langle C,X\rangle=\inf_{X\in\mathcal F\cap\operatorname{Comm}(\Gamma)}\langle C,X\rangle.\]

notation.meaning: matrices commuting with the group representation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Symmetry-Adapted PSD Certificate for Invariant SOS Polynomials
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An exact Gram-type characterization using symmetry-adapted matrix polynomials defined in the preceding representation-theoretic construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(g\in\mathbb R[X]_{\le 2d}^{G}\), \(g\) is a sum of squares if and only if
\[
g=\langle A_1,B^{(1)}\rangle+\cdots+\langle A_l,B^{(l)}\rangle
\]
for symmetric positive-semidefinite matrices
\[
A_j\in\operatorname{Mat}_{\eta_j\times\eta_j}(\mathbb R),\qquad A_j=A_j^{\mathsf T},\qquad A_j\succeq0\quad(1\le j\le l).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An invariant polynomial of degree at most 2d is a sum of squares exactly when it admits the stated symmetry-adapted Gram representation with symmetric positive-semidefinite coefficient matrices.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Group-invariant semidefinite program
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definitions induced by an orthogonal finite-group action on real symmetric matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\mathbb R^n,\rho)\) be a representation of a finite group \(G\), expressed in a \(G\)-invariant orthonormal basis so that \(M(g)M(g)^T=I\) for all \(g\in G\). Define \(X^g:=M(g)XM(g)^T\) for \(X\in\operatorname{Sym}_n(\mathbb R)\). A set \(\mathcal L\subseteq\operatorname{Sym}_n(\mathbb R)\) is \(G\)-invariant if \(X\in\mathcal L\) implies \(X^g\in\mathcal L\) for every \(g\in G\). The linear functional \(\langle C,X\rangle\) is \(G\)-invariant if \(\langle C,X^g\rangle=\langle C,X\rangle\) for all \(X\) and \(g\). An SDP is \(G\)-invariant if both its feasible set and its objective are \(G\)-invariant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An orthogonal finite-group representation acts on symmetric matrices by conjugation. A set or linear objective is invariant when this action preserves it, and an SDP is invariant when both its feasible set and objective are preserved.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: X^g=M(g)XM(g)^T;\quad \text{an SDP is }G\text{-invariant iff its feasible set and objective are }G\text{-invariant}

children.title: Orbit-Based Block Diagonalization
children.top_down_role: Block structure exposed through group or orbit decompositions.

knowledge_statements.title: Orbit-Based Block Diagonalization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block decomposition of the commutant arising from a finite permutation-group action.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a finite group \(\Gamma\) act on a finite set \(\Omega\), and let its permutation representation act unitarily on \(\mathbb C^\Omega\). With an isotypic decomposition \(\mathbb C^\Omega\cong\bigoplus_{r=1}^t(\mathbb C^{d_r}\otimes\mathbb C^{m_r})\), there is a unitary matrix \(U\) such that every Hermitian matrix \(X\) commuting with the action satisfies \(U^*XU=\bigoplus_{r=1}^t(I_{d_r}\otimes Z_r)\), where each \(Z_r\) is Hermitian of order \(m_r\). The zero-one matrices of the orbits of \(\Gamma\) on \(\Omega\times\Omega\) span the commutant. Moreover, \(X\succeq0\) exactly when \(Z_r\succeq0\) for every \(r\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a finite permutation-group action, orbital matrices span the invariant algebra, whose representation-theoretic block decomposition replaces one large PSD constraint by smaller PSD blocks.
assumptions_latex: \(\Gamma\) is finite and acts by permutations on a finite set \(\Omega\).
The representation space and SDP matrices are complex Hermitian.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[X\succeq0\iff Z_r\succeq0\quad\text{for every }r=1,\ldots,t.\]

knowledge_statements.title: Rank-One Matrix Lifts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Homogenized rank-one lift of a real vector variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), define \(Z=\begin{pmatrix}1&x^\top\\x&X\end{pmatrix}\). The exact rank-one lift is characterized by \(Z=\begin{pmatrix}1\\x\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}1\\x\end{pmatrix}^{\!\top}\), equivalently by \(Z\succeq0\), \(Z_{00}=1\), and \(\operatorname{rank}(Z)=1\). Under these conditions \(X=xx^\top\), so \(x^\top Qx=\langle Q,X\rangle\) for every \(Q\in\mathbb S^n\). Removing only the rank constraint yields the convex condition \(Z\succeq0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A vector and all its quadratic products form a normalized rank-one PSD matrix; dropping rank one gives the standard convex matrix relaxation.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb S^n\) when representing a quadratic form.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[X=xx^\top\iff\begin{pmatrix}1&x^\top\\x&X\end{pmatrix}\succeq0\ \text{and}\ \operatorname{rank}\begin{pmatrix}1&x^\top\\x&X\end{pmatrix}=1.\]

knowledge_statements.title: Shor SDP Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard Shor relaxation for a real quadratically constrained quadratic program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider minimizing \(x^\top Q_0x+2c_0^\top x+d_0\) subject to \(x^\top Q_ix+2c_i^\top x+d_i\le0\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\), with symmetric \(Q_i\). Introduce \(X\) for \(xx^\top\) and replace the rank-one identity by \(\begin{pmatrix}1&x^\top\\x&X\end{pmatrix}\succeq0\). The Shor relaxation minimizes \(\langle Q_0,X\rangle+2c_0^\top x+d_0\) subject to \(\langle Q_i,X\rangle+2c_i^\top x+d_i\le0\) for every \(i\) and the displayed PSD constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Shor's relaxation linearizes every quadratic form in a lifted matrix and drops the exact lift's rank-one requirement.
assumptions_latex: The original QCQP is interpreted as a minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[p_{\mathrm{Shor}}\le p_{\mathrm{QCQP}}\] whenever the original QCQP has a feasible point.

notation.meaning: optimal value of the Shor relaxation

knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Relaxation Gaps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A three-dimensional correlation example exhibiting a strict rank-relaxation gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min\{X_{12}+X_{13}+X_{23}:X\succeq0,\ X_{11}=X_{22}=X_{33}=1,\ \operatorname{rank}(X)=1\}\). Its optimal value is \(-1\). After deleting the rank constraint, the optimal value is \(-3/2\), attained by the matrix having unit diagonal and every off-diagonal entry equal to \(-1/2\). Hence PSD feasibility alone does not recover the convex hull of the normalized rank-one feasible matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dropping rank one from a normalized three-by-three PSD model changes the optimum from −1 to −3/2, giving a strict relaxation gap.
assumptions_latex: The objective sums the three distinct off-diagonal entries.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[p_{\mathrm{SDP}}=-\frac32<-1=p_{\mathrm{rank}-1}.\]

children.title: QCQP Semidefinite Relaxations

knowledge_statements.title: QCQP Semidefinite Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shor lifting for a quadratically constrained quadratic minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(q_i(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Q_i x+2c_i^{\mathsf T}x+d_i\), where \(Q_i\in\mathbb S^n\), for \(i=0,\ldots,m\). The QCQP \(\inf\{q_0(x):q_i(x)\leq0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\) has the semidefinite relaxation
\[\inf_{x,X}\ \langle Q_0,X\rangle+2c_0^{\mathsf T}x+d_0\quad\text{subject to}\quad \langle Q_i,X\rangle+2c_i^{\mathsf T}x+d_i\leq0,\quad i=1,\ldots,m,\quad \begin{pmatrix}1&x^{\mathsf T}\\x&X\end{pmatrix}\succeq0.\]
It is obtained by replacing \(X=xx^{\mathsf T}\) with \(X\succeq xx^{\mathsf T}\). Its value is a lower bound on the QCQP value; a feasible optimum satisfying \(X=xx^{\mathsf T}\) recovers a globally optimal QCQP point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replace xx-transpose by a free lifted matrix and impose the corresponding block positive-semidefinite constraint. The resulting SDP gives a lower bound and is exact with optimizer recovery when an optimal augmented lift has rank one, equivalently when X equals xx-transpose.
assumptions_latex: The QCQP is interpreted as a minimization problem with inequality constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v_{\mathrm{SDP}}\leq v_{\mathrm{QCQP}}\), with equality and recovery when an SDP optimum satisfies \(X=xx^{\mathsf T}\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded statement using quantities defined in the preceding QCQP relaxation setup. The recurrent malformed \(\Leftrightarrow\) glyph is interpreted as subtraction from the formula structure.

\[
\bar q-\underline p\geq \frac{2}{\pi}(\bar p-\underline p),

\]

children.title: Trust-Region QCQPs
children.top_down_role: Quadratic optimization models with trust-region structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Trust-Region QCQPs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical single-ball trust-region subproblem, including an indefinite quadratic objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(Q\in\mathbb S^n\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), a center \(a\in\mathbb R^n\), and a radius \(\Delta>0\), the classical trust-region QCQP is
\[\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\ x^{\mathsf T}Qx+2c^{\mathsf T}x+d\quad\text{subject to}\quad \lVert x-a\rVert_2^2\leq\Delta^2.\]
The objective need not be convex: \(Q\) may be indefinite. After translating \(y=x-a\), the problem has one convex quadratic constraint \(y^{\mathsf T}y\leq\Delta^2\) and a possibly nonconvex quadratic objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A trust-region QCQP minimizes a possibly indefinite quadratic function over one Euclidean ball of positive radius.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The feasible set is the compact ball \(\{x\in\mathbb R^n:\lVert x-a\rVert_2\leq\Delta\}\).

notation.meaning: objective Hessian matrix up to a factor of two

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the leaf and is standard, but no source is cited and the scalar d appearing in the objective is not introduced.

children.title: Exact SDP Relaxation Regimes
children.top_down_role: Problem regimes where semidefinite relaxation preserves the optimum.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact SDP Relaxation Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exactness of the Shor relaxation for the classical single-ball trust-region problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(Q\in\mathbb S^n\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(\Delta>0\), consider \(p^*=\min\{x^{\mathsf T}Qx+2c^{\mathsf T}x+d:\lVert x\rVert_2^2\leq\Delta^2\}\). Its Shor relaxation is
\[r^*=\min_{x,X}\ \langle Q,X\rangle+2c^{\mathsf T}x+d\quad\text{subject to}\quad \operatorname{tr}(X)\leq\Delta^2,\quad \begin{pmatrix}1&x^{\mathsf T}\\x&X\end{pmatrix}\succeq0.\]
Then \(r^*=p^*\). Moreover, the relaxation admits an optimal solution from which an optimal trust-region vector can be recovered; equivalently, an optimal rank-one lifted matrix exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For one positive-radius Euclidean-ball constraint, the Shor SDP has the same optimal value as the possibly nonconvex trust-region problem and permits recovery of a global optimizer.
assumptions_latex: \(\Delta>0\), so the ball constraint has a strict feasible point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r^*=p^*\), and an optimal lift with \(X=xx^{\mathsf T}\) exists.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exactness theorem is plausible for the classical positive-radius trust-region problem, but its value-exactness and rank-one recovery claims require a specific theorem locator. The scalar d is also not introduced.

children.title: Hidden-Convexity Geometry
children.top_down_role: Geometric structure associated with exact trust-region relaxation.

knowledge_statements.title: Hidden-Convexity Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dines convexity for the joint range of two homogeneous quadratic forms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A,B\in\mathbb S^n\). The joint homogeneous quadratic range
\[\mathcal R=\{(x^{\mathsf T}Ax,x^{\mathsf T}Bx):x\in\mathbb R^n\}\subseteq\mathbb R^2\]
is a convex cone, although each coordinate is generally nonconvex as a function of \(x\). Consequently, feasibility and separation questions involving two homogeneous quadratic forms can be analyzed by convex separation in \(\mathbb R^2\). This hidden convexity is the geometric mechanism behind scalar-multiplier certificates and exact semidefinite relaxation for a single strictly feasible quadratic inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The paired values of two homogeneous quadratic forms constitute a convex cone. This low-dimensional convexity enables separation certificates behind single-constraint QCQP exactness.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal R\) is convex and closed under multiplication by nonnegative scalars.

notation.meaning: joint range of the two quadratic forms

children.title: Nonexact Relaxation Boundary
children.top_down_role: Structural changes associated with loss of exactness.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonexact Relaxation Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A three-variable binary QCQP whose Shor relaxation has a strict value gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider the triangle maximum-cut QCQP
\[\max_{x\in\mathbb R^3}\ \frac12\sum_{1\leq i<j\leq3}(1-x_ix_j)\quad\text{subject to}\quad x_i^2=1,\quad i=1,2,3.\]
Every feasible sign vector cuts at most two edges, so its optimum is \(2\). The Shor relaxation replaces \(x_ix_j\) by \(X_{ij}\) and imposes \(X\succeq0\) and \(X_{ii}=1\). The correlation matrix having every off-diagonal entry equal to \(-1/2\) is feasible and has objective \(9/4\). Hence the relaxation is nonexact. Thus the single-quadratic-constraint exactness regime does not extend to arbitrary multiple quadratic equalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The triangle max-cut QCQP has value 2, while its SDP relaxation attains 9/4. Multiple quadratic equalities can therefore destroy trust-region exactness.
assumptions_latex: The QCQP is a maximization problem with three binary-square equalities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v_{\mathrm{SDP}}=9/4>2=v_{\mathrm{QCQP}}\).

children.title: Valid-Inequality Families

knowledge_statements.title: Valid-Inequality Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reformulation-linearization inequalities generated from pairs of linear constraint slacks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose a QCQP contains linear inequalities \(a_j^{\mathsf T}x\leq b_j\) for \(j=1,\ldots,k\), and let \(X\) denote its quadratic lift. For every pair \((j,\ell)\), nonnegativity of the slack product gives the valid lifted inequality
\[b_jb_\ell-b_j a_\ell^{\mathsf T}x-b_\ell a_j^{\mathsf T}x+a_j^{\mathsf T}Xa_\ell\geq0.\]
It holds whenever \(X=xx^{\mathsf T}\). Adding any collection of these inequalities to the Shor relaxation preserves every lifted QCQP-feasible point and can only shrink the SDP feasible region.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Products of nonnegative linear slacks yield linear inequalities in the lifted variables. Adding these RLT cuts preserves original feasible points and strengthens the SDP relaxation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each displayed inequality is valid for exact lifts, and adjoining it produces a relaxation contained in the original Shor relaxation.

children.title: Relaxation-Dominance Comparisons
children.top_down_role: Structural comparisons among stronger and weaker SDP formulations.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation-Dominance Comparisons
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasible-set inclusion criterion for comparing minimization relaxations of one lifted QCQP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F\) be the exact lifted feasible set of a minimization QCQP, and let \(R_1,R_2\) be convex relaxation sets satisfying \(F\subseteq R_1\subseteq R_2\). For the same lifted linear objective \(L\), define \(v_i=\inf\{L(Y):Y\in R_i\}\) and \(v_F=\inf\{L(Y):Y\in F\}\). Then
\[v_2\leq v_1\leq v_F.\]
Thus \(R_1\) dominates \(R_2\): every lower bound produced by \(R_1\) is at least as strong as the corresponding bound from \(R_2\). Strict dominance for a given instance occurs when \(v_1>v_2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For minimization, the relaxation with the smaller feasible set gives a no-weaker lower bound. Strictly different sets need not yield strictly different values for every objective.
assumptions_latex: All three problems use the same linear lifted objective \(L\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v_2\leq v_1\leq v_F\).

children.title: Integrality-Gap Effects
children.top_down_role: Approximation-quality changes produced by relaxation strengthening.

knowledge_statements.title: Integrality-Gap Effects
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effect of valid SDP strengthening on the additive gap for discrete minimization QCQPs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let a discrete minimization QCQP have finite optimum \(p^*\), and let an SDP relaxation have finite value \(r^*\leq p^*\). Its additive integrality gap is \(g=p^*-r^*\geq0\). If valid lifted inequalities replace the relaxation set \(R\) by \(R'\) with \(F\subseteq R'\subseteq R\), then the strengthened value \(r'^*\) satisfies
\[r^*\leq r'^*\leq p^*,\qquad 0\leq p^*-r'^*\leq g.\]
Accordingly, valid strengthening cannot enlarge the additive gap, although it need not reduce it strictly. A zero gap certifies value exactness but does not by itself guarantee that every relaxed optimizer is integral.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Valid cuts can only raise a minimization SDP bound and reduce or preserve its additive integrality gap. Zero gap ensures value exactness, not integrality of every SDP optimizer.
assumptions_latex: The discrete QCQP and both relaxations have finite optimal values.

children.title: Redundancy Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Regimes where added inequalities provide no additional relaxation strength.

knowledge_statements.title: Redundancy Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Support-function criterion for redundancy of a proposed lifted linear inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(R\subseteq\mathbb S^N\) be a nonempty SDP relaxation set and consider the proposed inequality \(\langle H,Y\rangle\leq h\). Define its support value
\[\sigma_R(H)=\sup\{\langle H,Y\rangle:Y\in R\}.\]
The inequality is redundant for \(R\) if and only if \(\sigma_R(H)\leq h\). It cuts no point when this inequality holds, cuts only boundary maximizers when \(\sigma_R(H)=h\), and strictly strengthens the relaxation when \(\sigma_R(H)>h\) and at least one violating point is removed. If \(\sigma_R(H)=+\infty\), the inequality is necessarily nonredundant whenever \(h\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lifted inequality is redundant exactly when the relaxation's support value in its normal direction does not exceed its right-hand side.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\langle H,Y\rangle\leq h\) is redundant on \(R\) if and only if \(\sigma_R(H)\leq h\).

notation.meaning: support value of R in direction H

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The support-value equivalence is elementary and correctly targeted, but it has no cited source. The statement also says the inequality both cuts no point and cuts boundary maximizers when the support value equals h; equality points are active, not removed.

children.title: Nearest-Correlation SDPs

knowledge_statements.title: Nearest-Correlation SDPs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Frobenius-norm projection of a symmetric matrix onto the correlation-matrix spectrahedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(C\in\mathbb S^n\), the nearest-correlation problem in squared Frobenius norm is
\[\min_{X\in\mathbb S^n}\ \lVert X-C\rVert_F^2\quad\text{subject to}\quad X\succeq0,\quad \operatorname{diag}(X)=\mathbf1.\]
Writing \(z=\operatorname{vec}(X-C)\), it has the linear-objective SDP epigraph representation
\[\min_{X,t}\ t\quad\text{subject to}\quad X\succeq0,\quad \operatorname{diag}(X)=\mathbf1,\quad \begin{pmatrix}t&z^{\mathsf T}\\z&I\end{pmatrix}\succeq0.\]
By the Schur complement, the last constraint is equivalent to \(t\geq z^{\mathsf T}z=\lVert X-C\rVert_F^2\), so both formulations have the same optimizers and optimal value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Project a symmetric matrix onto the positive-semidefinite matrices with unit diagonal. A Schur-complement epigraph converts the squared Frobenius objective into an SDP.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The quadratic projection model equals the displayed linear-objective SDP epigraph model.

notation.meaning: vector of diagonal entries of X

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Schur-complement SDP representation is mathematically standard and fits the leaf, but it lacks a source locator and should identify the block identity as having dimension n squared.

children.title: Covariance-Fitting SDPs
children.top_down_role: PSD-constrained estimation models for covariance matrices.

knowledge_statements.title: Covariance-Fitting SDPs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted least-squares fitting of a PSD covariance matrix under affine structural constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal A:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be linear, let \(y\in\mathbb R^m\), and let \(W\in\mathbb S_{++}^m\). A covariance-fitting model is
\[\min_{X\in\mathbb S^n}\ \lVert W^{1/2}(\mathcal A(X)-y)\rVert_2^2\quad\text{subject to}\quad X\succeq0,\quad \mathcal B(X)=b,\]
where \(\mathcal B(X)=b\) encodes affine structure. With \(z=W^{1/2}(\mathcal A(X)-y)\), the equivalent SDP epigraph replaces the objective by minimizing \(t\) subject to the same constraints and
\[\begin{pmatrix}t&z^{\mathsf T}\\z&I_m\end{pmatrix}\succeq0.\]
The Schur complement makes this LMI equivalent to \(t\geq\lVert z\rVert_2^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fit a positive-semidefinite covariance matrix to linear observations by weighted least squares, with optional affine structure. A Schur-complement epigraph yields an SDP.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal A\) and \(\mathcal B\) are linear maps.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The weighted least-squares covariance fit has the displayed linear-objective SDP epigraph representation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The weighted least-squares epigraph construction is plausible and appropriately classified, but no source is supplied. The codomain of the structural map B and the space containing b are not introduced.

children.title: PSD Completion Variants
children.top_down_role: Partial-data completion models with positive-semidefinite structure.

knowledge_statements.title: PSD Completion Variants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Chordal positive-semidefinite completion criterion for partially specified symmetric matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a chordal undirected graph containing every loop, and let \(A\) be a partial symmetric matrix whose specified entries are exactly \(A_{ij}\) with \(\{i,j\}\in E\). For each maximal clique \(C\) of \(G\), all entries of the principal submatrix \(A[C]\) are specified. Then \(A\) admits a completion \(X\in\mathbb S^{|V|}\) satisfying \(X\succeq0\) and \(X_{ij}=A_{ij}\) on \(E\) if and only if
\[A[C]\succeq0\quad\text{for every maximal clique }C\text{ of }G.\]
Thus chordality converts global PSD-completability into PSD tests on clique submatrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a chordal sparsity graph, a partial symmetric matrix has a PSD completion exactly when every fully specified maximal-clique principal submatrix is PSD.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is chordal and contains all loops.
The specified entries of \(A\) correspond exactly to \(E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A PSD completion exists if and only if \(A[C]\succeq0\) for every maximal clique \(C\).

notation.meaning: principal submatrix indexed by clique C

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The chordal PSD-completion criterion is a substantive theorem and fits the terminal container, but acceptance requires a specific authoritative theorem or section locator.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(N,p\in\mathbb N\) and let \(a_i\in\mathbb R^p\) for \(i=1,\ldots,N\). Choose \(w\in\mathbb R^N\) with \(w_i\ge0\) and \(\sum_{i=1}^N w_i=1\), and define \(M(w)=\sum_{i=1}^N w_i a_i a_i^\top\). knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(X\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), the spectral-norm epigraph satisfies \[\|X\|_2\le t\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \begin{pmatrix}tI_m&X\\X^\top&tI_n\end{pmatrix}\succeq0.\] The nuclear norm satisfies \[\|X\|_* =\min_{U\in\mathbb S^m,\,V\in\mathbb S^n}\ \tfrac12\bigl(\operatorname{tr}U+\operatorname{tr}V\bigr)\quad\text{subject to}\quad \begin{pmatrix}U&X\\X^\top&V\end{pmatrix}\succeq0.\] Consequently, a model using either norm in an objective or constraint has an SDP formulation whenever its remaining objective and constraints are affine or semidefinite representable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Spectral-norm and nuclear-norm constraints have exact block-matrix SDP representations; they preserve SDP representability when combined with other semidefinite-representable model components.

knowledge_statements.title: Spectral-Estimation SDPs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operator-norm fitting of an affine symmetric matrix estimator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A(x)=A_0+\sum_{k=1}^q x_kA_k\in\mathbb S^n\) and let \(S\in\mathbb S^n\) be observed. The operator-norm spectral estimator \(\min_x\|A(x)-S\|_2\) is the SDP \[\min_{x,t}\ t\quad\text{subject to}\quad -tI_n\preceq A(x)-S\preceq tI_n.\] At every feasible pair, the inequalities are equivalent to requiring every eigenvalue of \(A(x)-S\) to lie in \([-t,t]\); hence the optimal \(t\) is the smallest attainable worst absolute eigenvalue error.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fitting an affine symmetric model in operator norm is an SDP that bounds all residual eigenvalues between two scalar matrix bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The two-sided LMI exactly represents \(\min_x\|A(x)-S\|_2\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\in\mathbb S^n\) and let \(r\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\). The SDP \[\max_{P\in\mathbb S^n}\ \langle S,P\rangle\quad\text{subject to}\quad 0\preceq P\preceq I_n,\quad \operatorname{tr}P=r\] has value equal to the sum of the \(r\) largest eigenvalues of \(S\). An optimal solution may be chosen as the orthogonal projector onto a leading \(r\)-dimensional invariant subspace. If \(r<n\) and the \(r\)-th largest eigenvalue strictly exceeds the \((r+1)\)-st largest eigenvalue, that projector is the unique optimizer; when \(r=n\), the unique feasible matrix is \(P=I_n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maximizing covariance alignment over the Fantope yields a leading rank-r invariant subspace, with uniqueness under a boundary eigengap or when r equals n.

knowledge_statements.title: Spectral-Regularization Variants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Trace regularization as nuclear-norm regularization on the PSD cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(X\in\mathbb S_+^n\), all singular values equal its nonnegative eigenvalues, so \[\|X\|_*=\operatorname{tr}X.\] Therefore, if \(\mathcal A:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is linear and \(f:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) is convex, the PSD spectral-regularization model \[\min_{X\succeq0}\ f(\mathcal A(X))+\lambda\|X\|_*\] is identical to \(\min_{X\succeq0} f(\mathcal A(X))+\lambda\operatorname{tr}X\) for every \(\lambda\ge0\). When \(f\) has an SDP epigraph, the regularized model is an SDP.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On PSD matrices, nuclear norm equals trace, converting nuclear-norm spectral regularization into a linear SDP objective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: PSD nuclear-norm regularization is exactly trace regularization.

knowledge_statements.title: Euclidean-Distance Matrix Completion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Centered Gram representation for partial squared Euclidean distances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\in\mathbb S^n\) be hollow and let \(\Omega\) index specified off-diagonal squared distances \(d_{ij}\). A centered Euclidean realization exists exactly when there is \(B\in\mathbb S_+^n\) such that \[B\mathbf1=0,\qquad B_{ii}+B_{jj}-2B_{ij}=d_{ij}\quad((i,j)\in\Omega).\] Any such \(B\) is a centered Gram matrix. Factoring \(B=XX^\top\) produces points given by the rows of \(X\), and the realization dimension is \(\operatorname{rank}B\). Adding unspecified distance variables gives a PSD completion model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partial squared distances are realizable exactly when their specified entries arise linearly from a centered PSD Gram matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Feasibility of the displayed affine PSD system is equivalent to Euclidean-distance completion without a prescribed dimension bound.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Weighted closest-matrix completion formulation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Property-constrained closest completion, with PSD and Euclidean-distance specializations and an exact-completion test for indicator weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let A be a partially specified symmetric real matrix, let H be symmetric and entrywise nonnegative, and let \mathcal X_P=\{X:X\text{ satisfies }(P)\}. The weighted closest-matrix problem is \[\min_{X\in\mathcal X_P}\|H\circ(A-X)\|_F^2,\qquad \|B\|_F=\sqrt{\operatorname{Tr}(B^TB)}.\] If H_{ij}=0 for free entries and H_{ij}=1 for fixed entries, then A has an exact completion satisfying (P) if and only if the optimal value is zero. The PSD and Euclidean-distance choices of (P) define CPM and CDM, respectively; both are semidefinite programs, and CPM is a special case of CDM.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Property-constrained completion can be formulated by minimizing a weighted squared Frobenius distance. With zero weights on free entries and unit weights on fixed entries, exact completion is equivalent to a zero optimal value. The PSD and Euclidean-distance cases are CPM and CDM; both are semidefinite programs, with CPM a special case of CDM.
assumptions_latex: H_{ij}=0\text{ on free entries and }H_{ij}=1\text{ on fixed entries for the exactness equivalence}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A\text{ has an exact }(P)\text{-completion}\iff \min_{X\in\mathcal X_P}\|H\circ(A-X)\|_F^2=0;\quad \mathrm{CPM}\text{ and }\mathrm{CDM}\text{ are SDPs, and CPM is a special case of CDM}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Euclidean distance matrix and embedding dimension
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines dissimilarity matrices, squared Euclidean-distance realizations, and minimal embedding dimension.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An n\times n symmetric matrix D with nonnegative entries and zero diagonal is a dissimilarity matrix (or pre-distance matrix). It is a Euclidean distance matrix if there exist points x^1,\ldots,x^n\in\mathbb R^r such that \[D_{ij}=\|x^i-x^j\|_2^2\qquad (i,j=1,\ldots,n).\] Its embedding dimension is the smallest dimension r admitting such a realization, and r\le n-1.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dissimilarity or pre-distance matrix is symmetric, entrywise nonnegative, and has zero diagonal. It is a Euclidean distance matrix when its entries are squared Euclidean distances between realizing points. Its embedding dimension is the smallest dimension admitting such a realization and is at most n minus one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: D\text{ is an EDM}\iff \exists r\le n-1,\ \exists x^1,\ldots,x^n\in\mathbb R^r:\ D_{ij}=\|x^i-x^j\|_2^2\ \forall i,j;\quad \operatorname{edim}(D)=\min r.

children.title: Sensor-Network Localization SDP
children.top_down_role: Localization, realization, and rigidity interfaces based on distance lifts.

knowledge_statements.title: Sensor-Network Localization SDP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard Gram lift with exact sensor and anchor distance equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let unknown sensors be columns of \(X\in\mathbb R^{d\times n}\), and introduce \(Z\in\mathbb S^n\) with \(Y=\begin{pmatrix}I_d&X\\X^\top&Z\end{pmatrix}\succeq0\). For a sensor pair \((i,j)\), impose \(Z_{ii}+Z_{jj}-2Z_{ij}=d_{ij}^2\). For an anchor \(a_k\in\mathbb R^d\) and sensor \(i\), impose \(Z_{ii}-2a_k^\top x_i+\|a_k\|_2^2=d_{ki}^2\). These linear equations and \(Y\succeq0\) form an SDP relaxation; it is exact when an optimum satisfies \(Z=X^\top X\), equivalently \(\operatorname{rank}Y=d\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sensor localization becomes an SDP by lifting sensor inner products; rank d certifies an exact geometric realization.
assumptions_latex: Measured quantities are squared Euclidean distances
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The lifted constraints relax localization, and \(\operatorname{rank}Y=d\) recovers an exact realization.

knowledge_statements.title: Optimal-Power-Flow SDP Relaxation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complex voltage-product lift with the rank-one constraint removed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v\in\mathbb C^n\) be the bus-voltage vector and lift \(W=vv^*\in\mathbb H_+^n\). Every quadratic network quantity \(v^*H_kv\), with \(H_k\in\mathbb H^n\), becomes \(\operatorname{tr}(H_kW)\). Thus voltage-magnitude, injection, line-flow, and linear generation-cost constraints become affine constraints or convex conic constraints in \(W\). The AC optimal-power-flow model additionally requires \(\operatorname{rank}W=1\); deleting only this nonconvex constraint yields the standard SDP relaxation. If an optimal relaxed solution has rank one, its factor recovers a globally optimal feasible voltage vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: AC optimal power flow lifts voltage quadratics to a PSD matrix; dropping rank one gives an SDP, while rank-one recovery certifies exactness.
assumptions_latex: Network quantities are represented by Hermitian quadratic forms
Remaining generation-cost epigraphs are convex conic representable
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Dropping \(\operatorname{rank}W=1\) gives an SDP relaxation, and a rank-one optimum is exact.

knowledge_statements.title: Gram-Matrix SOS Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gram-matrix characterization of bounded-degree sum-of-squares polynomials.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p\in\mathbb R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\) have degree at most \(2d\), and let \(z_d(x)\) contain all monomials of degree at most \(d\). Then \(p\) is a sum of squares of polynomials of degree at most \(d\) if and only if there exists a symmetric matrix \(Q\succeq0\) such that \[p(x)=z_d(x)^\top Qz_d(x).\] Equating coefficients gives affine equations in the entries of \(Q\); hence bounded-degree SOS membership is semidefinite feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polynomial is bounded-degree SOS exactly when it has a PSD Gram matrix satisfying linear coefficient-matching equations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: SOS membership is equivalent to existence of \(Q\succeq0\) with \(p=z_d^\top Qz_d\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(y=(y_\alpha)_{|\alpha|\le2d}\) be a real truncated sequence indexed by \(\alpha\in\mathbb N^n\). Its order-\(d\) moment matrix is \[M_d(y)=(y_{\alpha+\beta})_{|\alpha|\le d,\,|\beta|\le d}.\] For every polynomial \(q(x)=\sum_{|\alpha|\le d}c_\alpha x^\alpha\) with coefficient vector \(c=(c_\alpha)_{|\alpha|\le d}\), one has \(c^\top M_d(y)c=L_y(q^2)\), where \(L_y(x^\gamma)=y_\gamma\). If \(y_\alpha=\int x^\alpha\,d\mu(x)\) for a positive measure \(\mu\), then \(M_d(y)\succeq0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A truncated moment matrix stores moments indexed by sums of monomial exponents, represents the Riesz functional on polynomial squares through coefficient vectors, and is PSD for every positive representing measure.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g(x)=\sum_\gamma g_\gamma x^\gamma\) and let \(y=(y_\alpha)_{|\alpha|\le2d}\). For an order \(r\) satisfying \(2r+\deg g\le2d\), the localizing matrix is \[M_r(gy)=\left(\sum_\gamma g_\gamma y_{\alpha+\beta+\gamma}\right)_{|\alpha|\le r,\,|\beta|\le r}.\] For every polynomial \(q(x)=\sum_{|\alpha|\le r}c_\alpha x^\alpha\) with coefficient vector \(c=(c_\alpha)_{|\alpha|\le r}\), one has \(c^\top M_r(gy)c=L_y(gq^2)\). If \(y\) has a positive representing measure supported on \(\{x:g(x)\ge0\}\), then \(M_r(gy)\succeq0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A localizing matrix encodes moments weighted by a constraint polynomial, represents the Riesz functional on the weighted polynomial square through its coefficient vector, and is PSD for measures supported where that polynomial is nonnegative.

knowledge_statements.title: Truncation-Order Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Degree compatibility for finite moment and localizing matrices in a relaxation of order \(d\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(y=(y_\alpha)_{|\alpha|\le 2d}\) be a truncated multisequence and let \(g_j\in\mathbb R[x]\). The moment matrix \(M_d(y)\) is well defined because each entry uses a moment \(y_{\alpha+\beta}\) of degree at most \(2d\). Put \(r_j=\lceil\deg(g_j)/2\rceil\). The localizing matrix \(M_{d-r_j}(g_jy)\) uses moments of degree at most \(2(d-r_j)+\deg(g_j)\le 2d\), and hence requires \(d\ge r_j\). Increasing the order from \(d\) to \(d+1\) retains every previous moment and principal moment-localizing constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Order d supplies moments through degree 2d; a polynomial constraint of degree e uses localizing order d−ceil(e/2). Higher orders retain all lower-order constraints.
assumptions_latex: \(d\in\mathbb N\) and \(y\) is indexed through degree \(2d\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M_d(y)\) and \(M_{d-r_j}(g_jy)\) use only available moments, and the order-\(d\) constraints embed in order \(d+1\).

notation.meaning: moment matrix indexed by monomials of degree at most d
ceiling of half the degree of g_j

knowledge_statements.title: Support-Constrained Variants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Moment-localizing representation for measures supported on a basic closed semialgebraic set with optional equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_j(x)\ge0,\ j=1,\ldots,m,\ h_k(x)=0,\ k=1,\ldots,s\}\), and let \(y_\alpha=\int_Kx^\alpha\,d\mu(x)\) for a finite positive measure \(\mu\) supported on \(K\). For every admissible truncation order, \[M_d(y)\succeq0,\qquad M_{d-r_j}(g_jy)\succeq0,\qquad M_{d-t_k}(h_ky)=0,\] where \(r_j=\lceil\deg(g_j)/2\rceil\) and \(t_k=\lceil\deg(h_k)/2\rceil\). These constraints are necessary finite-dimensional semidefinite conditions for support on \(K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A measure supported where inequalities are nonnegative and equations vanish produces positive semidefinite moment and inequality-localizing matrices, and zero equation-localizing matrices.
assumptions_latex: \(\mu\) is a finite positive Borel measure supported on \(K\).
The truncated moments needed by the displayed matrices are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M_d(y)\succeq0\), \(M_{d-r_j}(g_jy)\succeq0\), and \(M_{d-t_k}(h_ky)=0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Theta-Body Approximations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ideal-based outer approximations defined by bounded-degree sums of squares modulo an ideal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I\subseteq\mathbb R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\) be an ideal. An affine polynomial \(\ell\) is \(k\)-sos modulo \(I\) if there exist polynomials \(q_1,\ldots,q_N\) with \(\deg q_i\le k\) such that \(\ell-\sum_iq_i^2\in I\). The order-\(k\) theta body is \[\operatorname{TH}_k(I)=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:\ell(x)\ge0\text{ for every affine }\ell\text{ that is }k\text{-sos modulo }I\}.\] It is a closed convex outer approximation of \(\operatorname{conv}(V_{\mathbb R}(I))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The kth theta body enforces every affine inequality having a degree-k sum-of-squares certificate modulo the ideal, thereby outer-approximating the real variety’s convex hull.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{conv}(V_{\mathbb R}(I))\subseteq\operatorname{TH}_k(I)\), and \(\operatorname{TH}_k(I)\) is convex.

notation.meaning: sum of squares of degree-at-most-k polynomials, modulo I

knowledge_statements.title: Convex-Hull Lift Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Truncated moment spectrahedra whose coordinate projections outer-approximate convex hulls of real algebraic sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I\subseteq\mathbb R[x]\), let \(d\ge1\), and let \(L:\mathbb R[x]_{2d}\to\mathbb R\) be linear. Impose \(L(1)=1\), \(L(q)=0\) for every \(q\in I\cap\mathbb R[x]_{2d}\), and \(L(p^2)\ge0\) for every \(p\in\mathbb R[x]_d\). These conditions form a spectrahedron through the moment matrix constraint \(M_d(L)\succeq0\). Its projection \[Q_d(I)=\{(L(x_1),\ldots,L(x_n)):L\text{ satisfies the preceding conditions}\}\] is convex and contains \(\operatorname{conv}(V_{\mathbb R}(I))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normalized positive truncated functionals annihilating an ideal form a moment spectrahedron; projecting to first moments gives a convex outer lift of the variety’s convex hull.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{conv}(V_{\mathbb R}(I))\subseteq Q_d(I)\), with \(Q_d(I)\) a spectrahedral projection.

knowledge_statements.title: Algebraic Strength Levels
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nesting and finite exactness criteria for degree-indexed theta-body relaxations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an ideal \(I\subseteq\mathbb R[x]\), increasing the certificate degree enlarges the collection of affine polynomials recognized as sums of squares modulo \(I\). Consequently, \[\operatorname{conv}(V_{\mathbb R}(I))\subseteq\operatorname{TH}_{k+1}(I)\subseteq\operatorname{TH}_k(I).\] The relaxation is exact at level \(k\) if every affine polynomial nonnegative on \(V_{\mathbb R}(I)\) is \(k\)-sos modulo \(I\); under this condition, \(\operatorname{TH}_k(I)=\overline{\operatorname{conv}(V_{\mathbb R}(I))}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Higher algebraic levels yield tighter theta bodies. A level is exact when all valid affine inequalities possess certificates at that level.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{conv}(V_{\mathbb R}(I))\subseteq\operatorname{TH}_{k+1}(I)\subseteq\operatorname{TH}_k(I)\), with equality under the stated certificate condition.

knowledge_statements.title: Weak Polynomial Solvability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak optimization of rational SDPs under explicit conditioning and bounded-geometry assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider minimizing \(c^Tx\) over a rationally encoded spectrahedron \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\). Suppose rational data provide \(x_0\), \(0<r\le R\), and \(B(x_0,r)\subseteq K\subseteq B(0,R)\), and suppose polynomial-time separation is available. For rational \(\varepsilon>0\), the ellipsoid method returns a weakly feasible \(\hat x\) whose objective is within \(\varepsilon\) of the optimum, using time polynomial in the input length, \(n\), \(\log(R/r)\), and \(\log(1/\varepsilon)\). This is approximate, not exact, polynomial solvability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rational, well-bounded SDP with polynomial-time separation can be optimized to prescribed weak accuracy in time polynomial in encoding and logarithmic accuracy parameters.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) has rational encoding and known inner and outer radii.
A polynomial-time separation oracle for \(K\) is available.
\(\varepsilon>0\) is rational and encoded in binary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\hat x\) is computable in time \(\operatorname{poly}(L,n,\log(R/r),\log(1/\varepsilon))\) with weak feasibility and \(c^T\hat x\le\inf_{x\in K}c^Tx+\varepsilon\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The claim depends on the precise weak-feasibility and weak-optimization convention, oracle precision, and rational bit model. No source is supplied, so the stated hypotheses and polynomial bound cannot be validated reliably.

children.title: Encoding-Sensitive Exactness Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Encoding-sensitive distinctions among approximation, exact feasibility, and exact certification.

children.title: Input Encoding Size
children.top_down_role: Encoding-sensitive parameters governing SDP input size.

knowledge_statements.title: Input Encoding Size
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary length convention for rational semidefinite-program data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a rational SDP specified by symmetric matrices \(A_0,A_1,\ldots,A_n\in\mathbb Q^{m\times m}\), a rational objective \(c\in\mathbb Q^n\), and rational side constraints, write every rational coefficient in reduced binary numerator-denominator form. Its input encoding size \(L\) is the total bit length of these integers together with the indices, dimensions, relation symbols, and structural metadata needed to reconstruct the instance. Polynomial-time claims are measured as functions of \(L\), not merely of \(m\) and \(n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Input size counts the complete binary representation of all rational coefficients, dimensions, indices, and constraint metadata, rather than matrix dimensions alone.
assumptions_latex: All numerical SDP data are rational and represented in binary.
A fixed reasonable sparse or dense encoding convention is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L\) equals the total binary description length of the complete SDP instance.

notation.meaning: matrix order and number of scalar decision variables

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is plausible and the content kind fits, but encoding length depends on a specified computational representation, including sparse versus dense matrix storage and metadata conventions. No inspectable source supports the selected convention.

children.title: Approximate Bit Complexity
children.top_down_role: Bit-complexity viewpoints for approximate SDP solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Approximate Bit Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Turing-model resource bound for weakly accurate SDP solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under rational encoding, polynomial-time separation, and certified bounds \(B(x_0,r)\subseteq K\subseteq B(0,R)\), an ellipsoid implementation can compute a rational weak solution at accuracy \(\varepsilon>0\) using a number of bit operations polynomial in \(L\), \(n\), \(\log(R/r)\), and \(\log(1/\varepsilon)\). The numerators and denominators stored during the computation and in the output may likewise be chosen with polynomially bounded bit length. Thus accuracy enters through \(\log(1/\varepsilon)\), subject to the stated regularity data.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a well-bounded rational SDP, weak epsilon-accuracy requires polynomially many bit operations and polynomial-size rational iterates, with logarithmic dependence on inverse accuracy.
assumptions_latex: The rational instance has binary length \(L\) and polynomial-time separation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{bitcost}=\operatorname{poly}(L,n,\log(R/r),\log(1/\varepsilon))\), with polynomially bounded output bit length.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The asserted Turing-model bit bound and polynomial bounds on intermediate and output rational sizes require a source fixing separation-oracle precision, rounding, and weak-solution conventions. No source is supplied.

children.title: Exact Feasibility Status
children.top_down_role: Encoding-sensitive classification of exact feasibility.

assumptions_latex: Any additional affine constraints have rational data.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The exact status is feasible precisely when the displayed real existential condition holds; tolerance-based acceptance is a different predicate.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact, rather than tolerance-based, feasibility predicate for rational affine semidefinite systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given rational symmetric matrices \(A_0,A_1,\ldots,A_n\), exact feasibility asks whether \[\exists x\in\mathbb R^n\quad A_0+\sum_{i=1}^n x_iA_i\succeq0,\] together with any stated rational affine equalities. This predicate permits singular feasible matrices and feasible sets with empty interior. It is distinct from weak feasibility, which accepts a prescribed spectral or constraint tolerance; consequently, a weak polynomial-time approximation guarantee alone does not determine exact feasibility at boundary instances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact feasibility asks whether a real point satisfies the semidefinite and affine constraints with zero tolerance, including singular boundary solutions.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Feasibility Status

children.title: Exact Certificate Status
children.top_down_role: Complexity distinctions associated with exact certification.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Certificate Status
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct rational certificates for exact feasibility or strong infeasibility of affine SDPs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For constraints \(\langle A_i,X\rangle=b_i\) and \(X\succeq0\), a rational matrix \(X\) satisfying all equalities and admitting an exact rational factorization \(X=BB^T\) is a verifiable feasibility certificate. A rational vector \(y\) satisfying \(S=\sum_i y_iA_i\succeq0\) and \(b^Ty<0\), with an exact rational positive-semidefiniteness certificate for \(S\), certifies infeasibility because every feasible \(X\) would give \(b^Ty=\langle S,X\rangle\ge0\). Boundary instances need not admit either rational certificate form.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact rational factorizations certify feasibility, while a rational positive-semidefinite dual combination with negative right-hand-side pairing certifies strong infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: All displayed identities and inequalities are checked exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Either certificate is finitely verifiable and proves its asserted status, although the pair is not claimed complete for all SDPs.

notation.meaning: dual positive-semidefinite combination of constraint matrices

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Both displayed certificate forms are sufficient and the content kind fits, but their exact rational verification model and the boundary-instance qualification require an authoritative semidefinite alternative or facial-reduction source. No source is supplied.

children.title: Oracle-Ellipsoid Complexity Interface
children.top_down_role: Oracle-based complexity viewpoints for LMI feasibility and optimization.

children.title: Separation-Oracle Access
children.top_down_role: Complexity models based on separation access to semidefinite feasible regions.

knowledge_statements.title: Separation-Oracle Access
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong separation oracle for a spectrahedron in the real-arithmetic oracle model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(K=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:A(x)=A_0+\sum_i x_iA_i\succeq0\}\), query a point \(x\). Compute the least eigenvalue of \(A(x)\). If it is nonnegative, return \(x\in K\). Otherwise choose a corresponding unit eigenvector \(v\), set \(a_i=v^TA_iv\), and return the valid inequality \[a^Tz\ge -v^TA_0v.\] Every \(z\in K\) satisfies this inequality, whereas the queried point violates it because \(v^TA(x)v<0\). Stop after returning membership or the separating inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A negative eigenvector of the queried matrix yields an affine inequality valid for the spectrahedron and violated by the query point.
assumptions_latex: Eigenvalue and eigenvector computations are available in the stated oracle model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure returns membership when \(A(x)\succeq0\), otherwise a hyperplane strongly separating \(x\) from \(K\).

notation.meaning: unit eigenvector for a negative eigenvalue
normal vector of the separating inequality

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The negative-eigenvector separation argument is mathematically plausible and algorithm is the correct content kind, but exact eigenvalue-sign decisions and eigenvector access differ materially between real-arithmetic and rational bit-oracle models. The stated model needs an inspectable source.

children.title: Ellipsoid Complexity Model
children.top_down_role: Ellipsoid-based viewpoints for LMI feasibility or optimization.

knowledge_statements.title: Ellipsoid Complexity Model
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle-call complexity for weak feasibility of a bounded convex set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be convex and contained in a known ball of radius \(R\), and assume access to a separation oracle. Given \(0<\rho<R\), the central-cut ellipsoid method makes \(O(n^2\log(R/\rho))\) oracle calls and polynomial additional arithmetic work to either find a point accepted by the weak-feasibility specification or conclude that \(K\) contains no Euclidean ball of radius \(\rho\). With rational data and controlled oracle precision, the corresponding bit complexity is polynomial in the encoding length and \(\log(R/\rho)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The ellipsoid method solves weak feasibility with polynomial oracle calls, logarithmic radius-ratio dependence, and polynomial bit cost under controlled rational precision.
assumptions_latex: A separation oracle with suitable precision is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The oracle-call count is \(O(n^2\log(R/\rho))\), with polynomial auxiliary work under the stated encoding assumptions.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The oracle-call order is standard for an appropriate central-cut ellipsoid formulation, but the precise alternative returned, cut convention, oracle precision, and bit-complexity conclusion are source-sensitive. No authoritative locator is supplied.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Central-cut ellipsoid update and geometric volume bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Central-cut ellipsoid recursion used in the LMI feasibility or optimization setting; the minimum-volume update formulas require dimension at least two.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m\ge 2\) and let \(\mathcal E^{(k)}=\{z:(z-x^{(k)})^T(A^{(k)})^{-1}(z-x^{(k)})\le 1\}\), where \(A^{(k)}=(A^{(k)})^T\succ0\). Suppose \(\mathcal E^{(k)}\) contains an optimal point and the retained central half-ellipsoid \(\{z\in\mathcal E^{(k)}:g^{(k)T}(z-x^{(k)})\le0\}\), with \(g^{(k)}\ne0\), also contains an optimal point. Define \(\widehat g=(g^{(k)T}A^{(k)}g^{(k)})^{-1/2}g^{(k)}\), \(x^{(k+1)}=x^{(k)}-\frac{1}{m+1}A^{(k)}\widehat g\), and \(A^{(k+1)}=\frac{m^2}{m^2-1}\left(A^{(k)}-\frac{2}{m+1}A^{(k)}\widehat g\widehat g^TA^{(k)}\right)\). Then \(\mathcal E^{(k+1)}\) is the minimum-volume ellipsoid containing that half-ellipsoid and contains an optimal point. Iterating valid cuts yields \(\operatorname{vol}(\mathcal E^{(k)})\le e^{-k/(2m)}\operatorname{vol}(\mathcal E^{(0)})\). When \(m=1\), the minimum-length enclosure of a half-interval is the half-interval itself, and the method reduces to bisection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For dimension at least two, a valid central cut is normalized and used in the stated center and shape updates. The resulting ellipsoid is the minimum-volume enclosure of the retained half-ellipsoid and continues to contain an optimal point. Repeated valid cuts give the geometric volume bound exp(-k/(2m)) times the initial volume. In one dimension, the update is instead ordinary interval bisection.
assumptions_latex: \{z\in\mathcal E^{(k)}:g^{(k)T}(z-x^{(k)})\le0\}\text{ contains an optimal point at every applied cut}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal E^{(k+1)}\text{ is the minimum-volume enclosure of the retained half-ellipsoid, contains an optimal point, and }\operatorname{vol}(\mathcal E^{(k)})\le e^{-k/(2m)}\operatorname{vol}(\mathcal E^{(0)});\text{ for }m=1\text{ the method reduces to bisection.}

knowledge_statements.title: Oracle-to-Optimization Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak optimization from weak separation for bounded rational convex sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be convex with \(B(a,r)\subseteq K\subseteq B(a,R)\), where \(0<r\le R\), and let a weak separation oracle return, at rational query \(x\) and tolerance \(\delta>0\), either approximate membership or a separating hyperplane of prescribed accuracy. For rational \(c\) and \(\varepsilon>0\), the ellipsoid method computes \(\hat x\) whose objective is within \(\varepsilon\) of \(\inf_{x\in K}c^{\mathsf T}x\), using a number of oracle calls polynomial in \(n\), the input encoding length, \(\log(R/r)\), and \(\log(1/\varepsilon)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bounded convex set with a weak separation oracle can be optimized over to prescribed accuracy using polynomially many oracle calls.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_{\mathrm{oracle}}=\operatorname{poly}(n,L,\log(R/r),\log(1/\varepsilon))\).

children.title: Rank-Constrained SDP Boundary
children.top_down_role: Complexity changes caused by retaining matrix-rank restrictions.

knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Constrained SDP Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank-one correlation constraints recover binary quadratic optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For varying \(n\), define \(\mathcal C_n^{(1)}=\{X\in\mathbb S_+^n:\operatorname{diag}(X)=\mathbf1,\ \operatorname{rank}(X)=1\}\). Every \(X\in\mathcal C_n^{(1)}\) has the form \(X=zz^{\mathsf T}\) for some \(z\in\{-1,1\}^n\), and conversely every such vector produces a member of \(\mathcal C_n^{(1)}\). Consequently, optimizing \(\langle C,X\rangle\) over \(\mathcal C_n^{(1)}\) is binary quadratic optimization and is NP-hard in general. Dropping the rank constraint yields the convex elliptope \(\{X\succeq0:\operatorname{diag}(X)=\mathbf1\}\), an SDP relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding rank one to the correlation SDP exactly restores binary quadratic optimization and its general NP-hardness; removing rank gives a convex relaxation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{X\in\mathcal C_n^{(1)}}\langle C,X\rangle=\min_{z\in\{-1,1\}^n}z^{\mathsf T}Cz\), an NP-hard problem family.

children.title: Bilinear Matrix Constraints

knowledge_statements.title: Bilinear Matrix Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A scalar bilinear matrix inequality already destroys convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the one-dimensional symmetric matrix inequality \([xy-1]\succeq0\), equivalently \(xy\ge1\), in variables \((x,y)\in\mathbb R^2\). Its feasible set is nonconvex: both \((1,1)\) and \((-1,-1)\) are feasible, whereas their midpoint \((0,0)\) is infeasible. Thus replacing affine dependence in an LMI by bilinear dependence does not, in general, define a spectrahedron or a convex feasible region. Convex SDP algorithms therefore do not apply without relaxation, lifting, or additional structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even a scalar bilinear matrix inequality can have a nonconvex feasible set, placing general bilinear matrix constraints outside convex SDP.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{(x,y):[xy-1]\succeq0\}\) is not convex.
review_flags: specific scholarly locator for the BMI nonconvexity boundary required
standard_field_rationale: explicit scalar counterexample establishes the stated boundary

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Bilinear Matrix Inequality Feasibility Problem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines BMI feasibility through a symmetric matrix polynomial with degree-two decision dependence.

Given symmetric matrices \(F_0,F_i,F_{ij}\) of a common order, a bilinear matrix inequality problem asks for \(x\in\mathbb R^m\) such that

\]
The class includes combinatorial-optimization formulations such as MAX-CUT.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bilinear matrix inequality problem seeks a vector x for which a symmetric matrix polynomial, consisting of affine and pairwise-product terms in x, is positive semidefinite. The class includes formulations such as MAX-CUT.

children.title: Nonconvex Hardness Mechanisms

knowledge_statements.title: Nonconvex Hardness Mechanisms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic equalities encode Boolean variables and weighted graph cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a graph \(G=(V,E)\) with nonnegative rational weights \(w_{ij}\), consider variables \(z_i\in\mathbb R\) constrained by \(z_i^2=1\). The problem \[\max\ \frac12\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E}w_{ij}(1-z_iz_j)\quad\text{subject to}\quad z_i^2=1\ \text{for every }i\in V\] has optimal value equal to the maximum cut weight of \(G\). Therefore exact global optimization of this quadratically constrained family is NP-hard. Through the rank-one substitution \(X=zz^{\mathsf T}\), the same family gives an NP-hard rank-constrained semidefinite model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Boolean quadratic equalities encode weighted Max-Cut, yielding an NP-hard family of nonconvex quadratic problems and, through a rank-one matrix substitution, rank-constrained semidefinite problems.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{OPT}=\operatorname{MaxCut}(G)\), so exact global optimization of the displayed family is NP-hard.

notation.meaning: sign variable identifying a side of the cut
rank-one matrix zz^T used in the semidefinite reformulation

children.title: Primal–Dual Interior-Point Methods
children.top_down_role: Potential-reduction, path-following, scaling, and predictor-corrector families.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal–Dual Interior-Point Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic infeasible-start path-following template for standard-form primal–dual SDP pairs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the primal–dual pair \(\min\{\langle C,X\rangle:\mathcal A(X)=b,\ X\succeq0\}\) and \(\max\{b^{\mathsf T}y:\mathcal A^*y+S=C,\ S\succeq0\}\), initialize \((X^0,y^0,S^0)\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\times\mathbb R^m\times\mathbb S_{++}^n\). At iteration \(k\), set \(\mu_k=\langle X^k,S^k\rangle/n\), choose \(\sigma_k\in(0,1)\), and solve a chosen symmetrized primal–dual Newton system that reduces the primal and dual residuals and targets \(X\circ S=\sigma_k\mu_k I\). Choose a step length preserving \(X^{k+1}\succ0\) and \(S^{k+1}\succ0\), then update \((X,y,S)\). Define \(r_p=\mathcal A(X)-b\), \(r_d=\mathcal A^*y+S-C\), \(\eta_p=\|r_p\|/(1+\|b\|)\), \(\eta_d=\|r_d\|/(1+\|C\|)\), and \(\eta_g=\langle X,S\rangle/(1+|\langle C,X\rangle|+|b^{\mathsf T}y|)\). Stop when \(\max\{\eta_p,\eta_d,\eta_g\}\le\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A primal–dual path-following method initializes all primal and dual variables, repeatedly solves symmetrized Newton systems while preserving positive definiteness, and stops when defined feasibility and complementarity residuals meet the tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At termination, \(\max\{\eta_p,\eta_d,\eta_g\}\le\varepsilon\).

children.title: Spectral Bundle Methods
children.top_down_role: Bundle frameworks specialized to spectral optimization structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Spectral Bundle Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bundle minimization of a largest-eigenvalue objective over a convex set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=\lambda_{\max}(A_0+\sum_{i=1}^m x_iA_i)+c^{\mathsf T}x\) on a closed convex set \(Q\). At evaluated points \(x^j\), select unit maximal eigenvectors \(u^j\) and form \(g_i^j=(u^j)^{\mathsf T}A_i u^j+c_i\). Maintain the cutting-plane model \(m_k(x)=\max_{j\in J_k}\{f(x^j)+(g^j)^{\mathsf T}(x-x^j)\}\). Compute \(z^k\) by minimizing \(m_k(x)+\|x-x^k\|^2/(2t_k)\) over \(Q\). Accept \(z^k\) as a serious step when actual decrease is a fixed fraction of predicted decrease; otherwise retain \(x^k\), add the new cut, and continue.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Spectral bundle methods combine maximal-eigenvector subgradients, a cutting-plane model, and proximal serious/null steps.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) is nonempty, closed, and convex
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each iteration produces a trial point and either a serious update or an enriched bundle model.
review_flags: spectral bundle algorithm source and serious-step convention required
standard_field_rationale: canonical proximal cutting-plane construction using eigenvector subgradients

children.title: Nonsmooth Eigenvalue Optimization

knowledge_statements.title: Nonsmooth Eigenvalue Optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convexity and subdifferential of an affine largest-eigenvalue function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F(x)=A_0+\sum_{i=1}^m x_iA_i\) with \(A_i\in\mathbb S^n\), and define \(f(x)=\lambda_{\max}(F(x))\). Then \(f\) is finite and convex on \(\mathbb R^m\). If \(E_{\max}(F(x))\) denotes the maximal-eigenvalue eigenspace, then \[\partial f(x)=\left\{\bigl(\langle A_1,Z\rangle,\ldots,\langle A_m,Z\rangle\bigr):Z\succeq0,\ \operatorname{tr}Z=1,\ \operatorname{range}(Z)\subseteq E_{\max}(F(x))\right\}.\] In particular, a unit maximal eigenvector \(u\) gives the subgradient \((u^{\mathsf T}A_i u)_{i=1}^m\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The largest eigenvalue of an affine symmetric matrix is convex, and its subgradients are generated by density matrices supported on the top eigenspace.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\) is convex and has the displayed subdifferential.

knowledge_statements.title: Proximal Bundle Variants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stabilized bundle scheme for a proper closed convex objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For minimizing a proper closed convex function \(f\) over a closed convex set \(Q\), maintain a center \(x^k\) and affine minorants \(\ell_j(x)=f(x^j)+(g^j)^{\mathsf T}(x-x^j)\), where \(g^j\in\partial f(x^j)\). With \(m_k=\max_{j\in J_k}\ell_j\), compute \(z^k\in\arg\min_{x\in Q}\{m_k(x)+\|x-x^k\|^2/(2t_k)\}\). Evaluate \(f(z^k)\); use a serious step when actual decrease sufficiently matches predicted decrease, and otherwise use a null step. Variants may aggregate inactive cuts or adapt \(t_k\), while preserving the minorant property.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Proximal bundle variants stabilize cutting-plane models with a quadratic term and update the center only after sufficient objective decrease.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The model remains a global minorant, and each trial yields a serious or null step.

standard_field_rationale: standard serious/null-step proximal bundle template

knowledge_statements.title: Mixed Polyhedral–Semidefinite Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint polyhedral and semidefinite constraints as a convex composite model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F(x)=F_0+\sum_{i=1}^m x_iF_i\) be symmetric affine and let \(P=\{x:Ax\le b\}\). The mixed feasible region is \(P\cap\{x:F(x)\succeq0\}\), and it admits the equivalent scalar representation \[P\cap\{x:F(x)\succeq0\}=\{x:Ax\le b,\ \lambda_{\max}(-F(x))\le0\}.\] Hence minimizing a convex function \(h\) over this region is equivalently minimizing \(h(x)+\delta_P(x)+\delta_{\mathbb S_+^n}(F(x))\). Polyhedral cuts handle \(P\), while eigenvectors of violated semidefinite constraints generate valid affine spectral cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A model combining linear inequalities and an LMI has equivalent indicator-composite and largest-eigenvalue representations, supporting polyhedral and spectral cuts together.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The mixed feasible set and composite objective have the displayed equivalent representations.
