knowledge_statements.title: First-Order Cone Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal–dual proximal method for linearly coupled conic models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_x f(x)+g(Kx)\), where proximal maps of \(f\) and \(g^*\) are computable; conic constraints arise by taking \(g\) as an indicator of a cone-affine set. Choose \(\tau,\sigma>0\) with \(\tau\sigma\|K\|^2<1\), initialize \((x^0,y^0)\), and set \[y^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\sigma g^*}(y^k+\sigma K\bar x^k),\qquad x^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\tau f}(x^k-\tau K^*y^{k+1}),\qquad \bar x^{k+1}=2x^{k+1}-x^k.\] Stop when normalized primal and dual residuals meet prescribed tolerances; return the final or ergodically averaged iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A first-order primal–dual cone method alternates proximal primal and dual updates under a norm-based stepsize condition and stops using residuals.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(g\) are proper, closed, and convex
their required proximal maps are computable
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The iteration defines primal–dual trial points and a residual-controlled output.

notation.meaning: adjoint of the linear operator K

children.title: Operator-Splitting Methods
children.top_down_role: Splitting-based solver families for structured SDP formulations.

knowledge_statements.title: Operator-Splitting Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: ADMM splitting for separable convex objectives with linear coupling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min_{x,z} f(x)+g(z)\) subject to \(Bx+Cz=d\), choose \(\rho>0\) and initialize \((z^0,u^0)\). Iterate \[x^{k+1}\in\arg\min_x f(x)+\frac{\rho}{2}\|Bx+Cz^k-d+u^k\|^2,\] \[z^{k+1}\in\arg\min_z g(z)+\frac{\rho}{2}\|Bx^{k+1}+Cz-d+u^k\|^2,\qquad u^{k+1}=u^k+Bx^{k+1}+Cz^{k+1}-d.\] Cone constraints are represented by indicator terms in \(f\) or \(g\). Stop when the primal residual and the corresponding dual residual are below specified absolute-relative tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: ADMM separates objective and cone components into alternating subproblems, followed by a scaled dual update and residual-based stopping.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(g\) are proper, closed, and convex
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is selected when both primal and dual residual tests pass.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The scaled ADMM updates are standard, but the corresponding dual residual for general operators B and C is not defined, and no authoritative operator-splitting locator is supplied.

children.title: Projection-Based Variants
children.top_down_role: First-order variants organized around cone or affine projections.

knowledge_statements.title: Projection-Based Variants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projected subgradient iteration with explicit semidefinite-cone projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb S^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, and suppose \(f:C\to\mathbb R\) is convex with available subgradients. Initialize \(X^0\in C\), choose \(g^k\in\partial f(X^k)\) and \(\alpha_k>0\), and update \(X^{k+1}=\Pi_C(X^k-\alpha_k g^k)\). For \(C=\mathbb S_+^n\), if \(Y=Q\operatorname{Diag}(\lambda)Q^{\mathsf T}\), then \(\Pi_C(Y)=Q\operatorname{Diag}(\max\{\lambda_i,0\})Q^{\mathsf T}\). Stop after a budget or stationarity test and return the best-objective iterate; standard diminishing steps satisfy \(\sum_k\alpha_k=\infty\) and \(\sum_k\alpha_k^2<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projected subgradient variants take a first-order step and restore feasibility; projection onto the PSD cone truncates negative eigenvalues.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every iterate lies in \(C\), with PSD projection obtained by eigenvalue thresholding.

children.title: Residual-Based Stopping Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Stopping classifications based on numerical residual information.

assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal A:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is linear and \(\varepsilon>0\).
The SDP is \(\min\{\langle C,X\rangle:\mathcal A(X)=b,\ X\succeq0\}\) with dual \(\max\{b^Ty:\mathcal A^*y+S=C,\ S\succeq0\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\max\{r_p,r_d,r_g,r_K\}\leq\varepsilon\) is a scale-normalized residual stopping certificate, not an exact optimality certificate.

notation.meaning: Normalized primal, dual, and objective-gap residuals.
Normalized distance to the primal and dual semidefinite cones.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A solver-independent normalized interface for approximate SDP termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an iterate \((X,y,S)\), define \(r_p=\|\mathcal A(X)-b\|_2/(1+\|b\|_2)\), \(r_d=\|\mathcal A^*y+S-C\|_F/(1+\|C\|_F)\), and \(r_g=|\langle C,X\rangle-b^Ty|/(1+|\langle C,X\rangle|+|b^Ty|)\). Define \(r_K=\max\{\operatorname{dist}_F(X,\mathbb S_+^n)/(1+\|X\|_F),\operatorname{dist}_F(S,\mathbb S_+^n)/(1+\|S\|_F)\}\). The residual stopping interface declares approximate termination when \(\max\{r_p,r_d,r_g,r_K\}\leq\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stop when normalized primal feasibility, dual feasibility, objective gap, and cone-violation residuals are all at most the requested tolerance.
knowledge_statements.title: Residual-Based Stopping Interfaces

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the stopping-interface leaf and is mathematically coherent, but the particular normalizations are solver-interface choices rather than canonical SDP residual definitions. A specific operator-splitting solver or standards source is required to support these formulas.

children.title: Low-Rank Factorized Methods
children.top_down_role: Factor-space approaches for large SDPs with anticipated low-rank solutions.

assumptions_latex: \(r\geq1\), \(Y_0\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\), penalty \(\mu>0\), and step sizes \(\alpha_k>0\) are given.
The primal SDP has equality constraints \(\mathcal A(X)=b\) and objective \(\langle C,X\rangle\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output \(X_k=Y_kY_k^T\) is positive semidefinite with rank at most \(r\), while feasibility is assessed through \(\|\mathcal A(X_k)-b\|_2\).

notation.meaning: Low-rank factor and represented semidefinite matrix.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic-penalty factorization for equality-constrained primal SDPs.

source_refs.locator: 1.4.3 A dual view: Rank relaxation p. 16
source_refs.source_title: Advances in Linear Matrix Inequality Methods in Control

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Replace \(X\succeq0\) by \(X=YY^T\) with \(Y\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\), and set \(F_\mu(Y)=\langle C,YY^T\rangle+(\mu/2)\|\mathcal A(YY^T)-b\|_2^2\). Starting from \(Y_0\), compute \(Y_{k+1}=Y_k-\alpha_k\nabla F_\mu(Y_k)\), where \(\nabla F_\mu(Y)=2[C+\mu\mathcal A^*(\mathcal A(YY^T)-b)]Y\). Stop when the factor-gradient and feasibility residuals meet prescribed tolerances, and return \(X_k=Y_kY_k^T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimize over a factor Y so that X=YYᵀ is automatically positive semidefinite and low rank, stopping on factor-gradient and feasibility residuals.

children.title: Homogeneous Self-Dual Embedding Models

assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a closed convex cone and the primal-dual conic pair is finite-dimensional.
The embedding variables include scales \(\tau\geq0\) and \(\kappa\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Positive \(\tau\) permits normalization to a primal-dual solution, whereas \(\tau=0<\kappa\) yields a nonzero recession certificate when the corresponding normalized ray is valid.

notation.meaning: Closed primal cone and its dual.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convention-independent recovery properties of a homogeneous self-dual conic embedding.

source_refs.locator: 5 Self-Dual Embeddings p. 111

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A homogeneous self-dual embedding represents the primal and dual conic systems by one scale-homogeneous feasibility system in variables \((x,y,s,\tau,\kappa)\in K\times\mathbb R^m\times K^*\times\mathbb R_+^2\). Its equations are linear and invariant under \((x,y,s,\tau,\kappa)\mapsto\lambda(x,y,s,\tau,\kappa)\) for \(\lambda>0\). They are constructed so that \(\tau>0\) gives normalized variables \((x/\tau,y/\tau,s/\tau)\), while \(\tau=0<\kappa\) exposes a nonzero primal- or dual-recession certificate according to its signed data pairings.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A homogeneous embedding combines primal, dual, and certificate equations in one scalable conic system whose scale variables determine how a solution is interpreted.

children.title: Optimal Solution Recovery

assumptions_latex: An embedding point \((X,y,S,\tau,\kappa)\) satisfies the chosen homogeneous self-dual SDP equations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((\widehat X,\widehat y,\widehat S)=(X/\tau,y/\tau,S/\tau)\) is a primal-dual optimal solution.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an embedding solution with \(\tau>0\), set \(\widehat X=X/\tau\), \(\widehat y=y/\tau\), and \(\widehat S=S/\tau\). The embedding equations then reduce to \(\mathcal A(\widehat X)=b\), \(\mathcal A^*\widehat y+\widehat S=C\), \(\widehat X\succeq0\), and \(\widehat S\succeq0\). If \(\kappa=0\), the embedded gap equation gives \(\langle C,\widehat X\rangle=b^T\widehat y\); hence the recovered feasible pair is primal-dual optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the embedding solution has positive normalization scale and zero certificate scale, divide its primal-dual variables by the normalization scale to recover an optimum.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Optimal-Value Recovery Along a Self-Dual Embedding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recovery of an attained finite SDP optimum from normalized self-dual-embedding quantities; primal attainment follows from Assumption 5.8.1 and finite \(d^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose \((P)\) and \((D)\) are in perfect duality, \(d^*<+\infty\), and finite \(d^*\) implies \(\mathcal P^*\neq\varnothing\). Let \(X^*\in\mathcal P^*\). Then
\[
d^*=\operatorname{Tr}(CX^*)=\lim_{t\to\infty}\frac{b^Ty(\mu^{(t)})}{\tau(\mu^{(t)})}=\lim_{t\to\infty}\operatorname{Tr}\!\left(\frac{CX(\mu^{(t)})}{\tau(\mu^{(t)})}\right).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under perfect duality and the stated attainment assumption, a finite dual optimum equals the objective at a primal optimum and the limits of the normalized dual and primal embedding objectives.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: d^*=\operatorname{Tr}(CX^*)=\lim_{t\to\infty}\frac{b^Ty(\mu^{(t)})}{\tau(\mu^{(t)})}=\lim_{t\to\infty}\operatorname{Tr}\!\left(\frac{CX(\mu^{(t)})}{\tau(\mu^{(t)})}\right).

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A recovered pair is maximally complementary when it lies in \(\operatorname{ri}(\mathcal X^*)\times\operatorname{ri}(\mathcal S^*)\); such a pair attains the largest possible ranks on the respective optimal sets, but maximal rank alone need not characterize relative-interior membership.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal X^*\) be the primal optimal set and let \(\mathcal S^*\) be the set of optimal dual slacks. A recovered optimal pair \((X^*,S^*)\) is maximally complementary when \(X^*\in\operatorname{ri}(\mathcal X^*)\) and \(S^*\in\operatorname{ri}(\mathcal S^*)\). Such relative-interior points have the largest ranks attainable within their respective optimal sets, and complementarity requires \(\langle X^*,S^*\rangle=0\). The converse implication from maximal rank to relative-interior membership is not asserted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A maximally complementary recovered pair lies in the relative interiors of both optimal sets. Such points attain the largest available ranks, although maximal rank alone does not guarantee relative-interior membership.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The sign pattern of \((\tau,\kappa)\), together with certificate pairings, separates solution recovery, infeasibility-ray recovery, and an indeterminate degenerate regime.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact regime split for interpreting nonzero homogeneous embedding solutions.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Embedding recovery has three regimes. If \(\tau>0\) and \(\kappa=0\), division by \(\tau\) recovers a primal-dual optimum. If \(\tau=0\) and \(\kappa>0\), the homogeneous variables define recession directions; the signs of their data pairings determine whether primal infeasibility or dual infeasibility with primal unboundedness is certified. If \(\tau=\kappa=0\), neither normalization is available, so ordinary optimality or infeasibility status cannot be concluded without additional facial or degeneracy analysis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive normalization scale yields an optimum; positive certificate scale with zero normalization yields a status ray; two zero scales require degeneracy analysis.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Self-dual-embedding procedure for determining SDP status
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded summary. The source truncates one unboundedness condition in the limiting classification; that condition remains explicitly unresolved. The source also states recovery of $S^*/\tau^*$ alone as an optimal solution of $(D)$, although the displayed formulation has variables $(y,S)$; no missing component is inferred.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For $(D)$, solve its self-dual embedding together with its Lagrangean dual $(P)$ to obtain a maximally complementary embedding solution $(y^*,X^*,\tau^*,\vartheta^*,S^*,\rho^*,\nu^*)$. If $\tau^*>0$, the extract states that $S^*/\tau^*$ is an optimal solution of $(D)$. If $\rho^*>0$, strong infeasibility of $(P)$, $(D)$, or both is detected. If $\tau^*=\rho^*=0$, solve the embedding of the extended Lagrange--Slater dual $(P_{gf})$ and its Lagrangean dual by following the embedded central path. The resulting trace limit equals $d^*$ when $d^*$ is finite and is $+\infty$ when $(D)$ is weakly infeasible; the extract also assigns $+\infty$ under a truncated condition beginning that $(D)$ is "unbounded without an ...".
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve the SDP self-dual embedding and inspect its scaling variables. Positive tau yields the optimal object stated in the extract, positive rho detects strong infeasibility, and the case tau equals rho equals zero invokes an extended embedding and its central path. The trace limit equals the finite optimal value and diverges for weak infeasibility, as well as for an additional unboundedness case whose condition is truncated.
assumptions_latex: (y^*,X^*,\tau^*,\vartheta^*,S^*,\rho^*,\nu^*)\text{ is a maximally complementary solution of the embedding.}
X(\mu),\tau(\mu)\text{ are embedded-central-path variables in the branch }\tau^*=\rho^*=0.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \tau^*>0\Rightarrow\text{the extract identifies }S^*/\tau^*\text{ as optimal for }(D);\quad \rho^*>0\Rightarrow\text{strong infeasibility of }(P),(D),\text{ or both is detected};\quad \tau^*=\rho^*=0\Rightarrow\lim_{\mu\to0}\operatorname{Tr}\!\left(\frac{CX(\mu)}{\tau(\mu)}\right)=\begin{cases}d^*,&d^*\text{ is finite},\\+\infty,&(D)\text{ is weakly infeasible},\\+\infty,&\text{the source's truncated unboundedness condition holds.}\end{cases}

Report strongly primal infeasible if \(\mathcal A^*y_I\preceq0\) and \(b^Ty_I>0\). Given primal feasibility, report primal unbounded below if \(D\succeq0\), \(\mathcal A(D)=0\), and \(\langle C,D\rangle<0\). If no predicate holds, return an indeterminate status rather than inferring one from failure of another certificate.

An embedding is augmented by face variables or exposing certificates.

The interface is required to distinguish a genuine certificate on the minimal faces from failure of strict feasibility in the unreduced cone.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An extended-dual interface consists of a spectrahedrally represented feasible set \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{ext}}\), an objective \(d_{\mathrm{ext}}\), and a projection to ordinary dual variables or facial certificates. Any projected ordinary dual point supplies a valid bound; auxiliary blocks certify the facial steps responsible for exactness.

children.title: Ordinary-Status Failure Boundary
children.top_down_role: Degenerate regimes not resolved by ordinary embedding statuses.

knowledge_statements.title: Ordinary-Status Failure Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak infeasibility boundary for ordinary feasible, infeasible, and unbounded statuses in an SDP embedding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the primal feasibility system \(\mathcal A(X)=b\), \(X\succeq0\). It is weakly infeasible when no \(X\succeq0\) satisfies \(\mathcal A(X)=b\), yet \(\inf_{X\succeq0}\|\mathcal A(X)-b\|=0\). At this boundary, no positive residual tolerance separates feasibility from infeasibility, and there need not exist a strict separating certificate \(y\) with \(\mathcal A^*y\succeq0\) and \(b^\top y<0\). Consequently, an ordinary self-dual embedding whose status logic uses only vanishing residuals and strict primal-dual rays may converge toward its zero-status boundary without certifying either feasibility or infeasibility; facial reduction or an extended-dual certificate is then required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weakly infeasible SDPs can have arbitrarily small residuals but neither a feasible point nor a strict separating ray, making ordinary embedding statuses inconclusive.
assumptions_latex: The residual norm is any norm on \(\mathbb R^m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{X\succeq0}\|\mathcal A(X)-b\|=0\) does not imply feasibility or an ordinary strict infeasibility certificate.

notation.meaning: cone of real positive-semidefinite symmetric matrices

children.title: Block-Structured Linear Algebra

knowledge_statements.title: Block-Structured Linear Algebra
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block representation of Newton systems arising from partitioned SDP variables and constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\in\mathbb S^N\) be partitioned according to \(\mathbb R^N=\bigoplus_{j=1}^q\mathbb R^{n_j}\), with blocks \(H_{ij}\), and write \(z=(z_1,\ldots,z_q)\), \(r=(r_1,\ldots,r_q)\). Then \(Hz=r\) is equivalently the coupled family \(\sum_{j=1}^q H_{ij}z_j=r_i\) for \(i=1,\ldots,q\). If \(H_{ij}=0\) outside an edge set \(E\), each block equation involves only neighboring blocks. Block elimination may therefore apply local diagonal-block solves and retain only the nonzero cross-block couplings, without changing the solution set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A partitioned linear system is a family of local block equations coupled only through its nonzero off-diagonal blocks.
assumptions_latex: \(H\in\mathbb S^N\) and the block dimensions sum to \(N\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Hz=r\iff \sum_{j=1}^qH_{ij}z_j=r_i\) for every \(i\).

notation.meaning: block in block row i and block column j

knowledge_statements.title: Schur-Complement Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact block elimination for a two-by-two symmetric linear system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(H_{11}u+H_{12}v=r_1\) and \(H_{21}u+H_{22}v=r_2\), with nonsingular \(H_{11}\), form \(S=H_{22}-H_{21}H_{11}^{-1}H_{12}\) and \(g=r_2-H_{21}H_{11}^{-1}r_1\). Solve \(Sv=g\), then recover \(u=H_{11}^{-1}(r_1-H_{12}v)\). If \(S\) is nonsingular, this procedure returns the unique solution of the original block system. Implementations apply solves with \(H_{11}\) rather than explicitly forming \(H_{11}^{-1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eliminate the first block, solve the resulting Schur-complement system, and back-substitute to recover the unique full solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v=S^{-1}g\) and \(u=H_{11}^{-1}(r_1-H_{12}v)\) solve the original system.

children.title: Cross-Block Coupling
children.top_down_role: Constraint interactions coupling otherwise separable PSD blocks.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Block Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effect of off-diagonal blocks on separability and Schur-complement fill.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a symmetric block matrix \(H=D+C\), let \(D=\operatorname{diag}(H_{11},\ldots,H_{qq})\) and let \(C\) contain the off-diagonal blocks. The system \(Hz=r\) decomposes into independent block systems exactly when \(C=0\). If a block \(k\) with nonsingular \(H_{kk}\) is eliminated, the remaining blocks are updated by \(H'_{ij}=H_{ij}-H_{ik}H_{kk}^{-1}H_{kj}\). Thus two remaining blocks can become coupled whenever both couple to the eliminated block, even if \(H_{ij}=0\) initially.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Off-diagonal blocks prevent independent solves, and eliminating a shared neighboring block can create new couplings between previously uncoupled blocks.
assumptions_latex: The eliminated diagonal block \(H_{kk}\) is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C=0\) characterizes block separability, while elimination produces updates \(H'_{ij}=H_{ij}-H_{ik}H_{kk}^{-1}H_{kj}\).

notation.meaning: block-diagonal part of the system matrix

knowledge_statements.title: Chordal-Decomposition Computation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Clique conversion of a sparse positive-semidefinite completion constraint on a chordal graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be chordal with maximal cliques \(C_1,\ldots,C_p\), and let \(X\) be a partial symmetric matrix whose specified entries are the diagonal and edges of \(G\). Then \(X\) has a positive-semidefinite completion if and only if \(X[C_k,C_k]\succeq0\) for every \(k\). A converted SDP may introduce matrices \(X_k\in\mathbb S^{|C_k|}_+\) and impose equality of entries shared by intersecting cliques. Under a clique tree, consistency on each tree edge suffices to define one globally consistent partial matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For chordal sparsity, one large PSD-completion constraint becomes clique-sized PSD constraints plus equality constraints on clique overlaps.
assumptions_latex: All diagonal and edge entries of the partial matrix are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X\) admits a positive-semidefinite completion if and only if \(X[C_k,C_k]\succeq0\) for all maximal cliques \(C_k\).

notation.meaning: principal submatrix indexed by clique C
a maximal clique of the chordal graph

children.title: Low-Rank Data Operations

knowledge_statements.title: Low-Rank Data Operations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matrix-free application of low-rank symmetric SDP data matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose an SDP data matrix is represented as \(A=D+UV^\top+VU^\top\), where \(D\) is diagonal and \(U,V\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\). For an input vector \(x\), compute \(p=V^\top x\), \(q=U^\top x\), and return \(Ax=Dx+Up+Vq\). For a symmetric matrix \(X\), compute the trace pairing as \(\langle A,X\rangle=\langle D,X\rangle+\operatorname{tr}(V^\top XU)+\operatorname{tr}(U^\top XV)\). These formulas avoid storing or forming a dense \(n\times n\) matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Low-rank factors permit matrix-vector products and SDP trace pairings without forming the associated dense data matrix.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is diagonal and \(U,V\) each have \(r\) columns.
All matrix products are dimensionally conformable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The stated operations use \(O(nr+n)\) arithmetic for a matrix-vector product and \(O(nr)\) storage.

children.title: Partial-Spectrum Computation
children.top_down_role: Computational interfaces using selected eigenvalues or eigenspaces.

knowledge_statements.title: Partial-Spectrum Computation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matrix-free computation of selected extreme eigenpairs for symmetric SDP operators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a symmetric linear operator \(M:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\), a target count \(k<n\), and tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\), construct an orthonormal search basis \(Q\), form the projected matrix \(T=Q^\top MQ\), and extract its \(k\) desired extreme Ritz pairs \((\theta_i,s_i)\). Set \(u_i=Qs_i\), expand or restart the subspace using residuals \(r_i=Mu_i-\theta_i u_i\), and stop when \(\|r_i\|_2\leq\varepsilon\max\{1,|\theta_i|\}\) for every requested pair. Return \((\theta_i,u_i)_{i=1}^k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A projected iterative eigensolver returns only the requested extreme eigenpairs and stops when every Ritz residual meets the chosen tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(M\) is symmetric and available through matrix-vector products.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each returned pair satisfies \(\|Mu_i-\theta_i u_i\|_2\leq\varepsilon\max\{1,|\theta_i|\}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record describes a generic restarted projection framework rather than one fully specified eigensolver, and no source identifies the convergence or residual-stopping interface being asserted. An authoritative locator for a concrete Lanczos, Arnoldi, or related symmetric partial-spectrum method is required.

children.title: Truncated Eigenspace Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Approximate spectral representations based on restricted eigenspaces.

knowledge_statements.title: Truncated Eigenspace Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual and spectral-gap interface for certifying an approximate invariant subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\in\mathbb S^n\), let \(U\in\mathbb R^{n\times k}\) satisfy \(U^\top U=I\), and set \(\Theta=U^\top MU\) and \(R=MU-U\Theta\). The tuple \((U,\Theta,R)\) is a directly checkable truncated-eigenspace certificate. It certifies exact invariance when \(R=0\). More generally, if the eigenvalues represented by \(\Theta\) are separated from the unwanted spectrum of \(M\) by a gap \(\delta>0\), then the sine of the largest principal angle between \(\operatorname{range}(U)\) and the corresponding exact invariant subspace is at most \(\|R\|_2/\delta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An orthonormal basis, its Ritz matrix, a small residual, and a spectral gap certify the accuracy of a truncated invariant subspace.
assumptions_latex: The targeted and unwanted spectra are separated by \(\delta>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|\sin\Theta_{\mathrm{ang}}\|_2\leq\|R\|_2/\delta\).

notation.meaning: matrix of principal angles to the exact invariant subspace

review_flags: Precise invariant-subspace perturbation theorem locator required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The residual tuple is directly checkable, but the principal-angle bound depends on a precise residual perturbation theorem and an exact definition of separation between the Ritz spectrum and the complementary exact spectrum. Those hypotheses cannot be validated without a theorem-level source.

children.title: Symmetry-Reduced Computation
children.top_down_role: Block diagonalization and orbit-based model compression.

knowledge_statements.title: Symmetry-Reduced Computation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Invariant-subspace block diagonalization and orbit compression for symmetric SDP models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a finite group \(\Gamma\) act orthogonally by matrices \(P_g\) on \(\mathbb R^n\), and suppose the SDP objective and constraints are invariant under \(X\mapsto P_gXP_g^\top\). The averaging map \(\Pi(X)=|\Gamma|^{-1}\sum_{g\in\Gamma}P_gXP_g^\top\) preserves feasibility, positive semidefiniteness, and objective value. Hence an invariant optimal solution may be sought in the fixed-point algebra. After an orthogonal change of basis \(Q\) adapted to the representation, every invariant symmetric matrix is block diagonal, so the PSD constraint reduces to PSD constraints on its blocks; coefficients constant on group orbits need only one reduced variable per orbit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Averaging yields an invariant optimizer, after which representation blocks and coefficient orbits compress the SDP without changing its optimum.
assumptions_latex: Every objective and constraint datum is invariant under the action.
The original SDP attains an optimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exists an optimal \(X^*=\Pi(X^*)\), and \(Q^\top X^*Q\) is block diagonal in a symmetry-adapted basis.

notation.meaning: orthogonal matrix representing group element g

review_flags: Authoritative symmetry-reduction and block-diagonalization locator required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Averaging over a finite orthogonal group is standard, but the exact block form of the fixed-point algebra depends on the real representation and its multiplicities. The one-variable-per-orbit assertion also needs an appropriate coordinate or permutation-action setting. A source is required to fix these details reliably.

children.title: Forward Error Models

knowledge_statements.title: Forward Error Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Forward error of a computed primal-dual SDP output relative to an exact solution set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For SDP data \(d\), let \(S(d)\) be its nonempty exact solution set in a normed output space, and let \(\widehat z\) be a computed output. Its absolute forward error is \(e_{\mathrm f}(\widehat z;d)=\inf_{z\in S(d)}\|\widehat z-z\|\). Given a positive scale \(s(d)\), the relative forward error is \(e_{\mathrm f}(\widehat z;d)/s(d)\). For a unique solution \(z^*\), the absolute error reduces to \(\|\widehat z-z^*\|\). This model measures displacement in solution space, not merely residuals in the defining equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Forward error is the distance from the computed output to the exact solution set, optionally normalized by a chosen problem scale.
assumptions_latex: The output space carries a specified norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(e_{\mathrm f}(\widehat z;d)=\operatorname{dist}(\widehat z,S(d))\).

notation.meaning: exact solution set for the data

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(d\) denote SDP data, let \(S(d)\) be the associated exact solution set, and let \(\widehat z\) be a computed output. For a norm \(\|\cdot\|_{\mathcal D}\) on data space, the absolute backward error is \(e_{\mathrm b}(\widehat z;d)=\inf\{\|\Delta d\|_{\mathcal D}:\widehat z\in S(d+\Delta d)\}\). Given a positive data scale \(t(d)\), the relative backward error is \(e_{\mathrm b}(\widehat z;d)/t(d)\). Thus backward stability means that the reported output exactly solves a nearby SDP whose admissible data perturbation is small.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Backward error is the smallest perturbation of the SDP data that makes the computed output an exact solution of the perturbed problem.

children.title: Regularized Error Models

knowledge_statements.title: Regularized Error Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regularized backward-error model balancing data perturbation against output size or displacement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(d\) be SDP data, \(S(d)\) its solution set, \(\widehat z\) a computed output, \(R\) a proper nonnegative regularizer, and \(\lambda>0\). Define the regularized error by \[e_{\lambda}(\widehat z;d)=\inf_{\Delta d,\,z}\left\{\|\Delta d\|_{\mathcal D}+\lambda R(z-\widehat z):z\in S(d+\Delta d)\right\}.\] The model permits simultaneous adjustment of data and output while penalizing both. If output adjustment is forbidden by taking \(R(w)=0\) for \(w=0\) and \(R(w)=+\infty\) otherwise, then \(e_\lambda\) reduces to absolute backward error.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Regularized error minimizes a weighted combination of data perturbation and adjustment of the computed output to a nearby exact solution.
assumptions_latex: Perturbations \(\Delta d\) preserve the chosen SDP data structure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(e_{\lambda}\) interpolates between a nearby-data model and a penalized nearby-output model.

notation.meaning: penalty on adjustment of the computed output

children.title: Scaling Pathologies
children.top_down_role: Numerical difficulties associated with poorly balanced problem data.

assumptions_latex: \(D\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is diagonal and positive definite.
The domain and codomain \(\mathbb S^n\) carry the Frobenius norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_D\) preserves positive semidefiniteness and has condition number \(\kappa_{F\to F}(T_D)=\kappa_2(D)^2\), which can be arbitrarily large.

notation.meaning: spectral condition number of the diagonal matrix
operator condition number induced by the Frobenius norm

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A concrete congruence-scaling mechanism that creates numerical imbalance without changing cone membership.

source_refs.locator: 1.1 Semidefinite programming p. 1

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=\operatorname{diag}(d_1,\ldots,d_n)\succ0\) and define \(T_D:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb S^n\) by \(T_D(X)=DXD\). Then \(X\succeq0\) if and only if \(T_D(X)\succeq0\). For the operator norm induced by the Frobenius norm, \(\|T_D\|_{F\to F}=(\max_i d_i)^2\), \(\|T_D^{-1}\|_{F\to F}=(\min_i d_i)^{-2}\), and \(\kappa_{F\to F}(T_D)=\kappa_2(D)^2\). Thus congruence-equivalent SDP representations can have arbitrarily ill-conditioned changes of variables as \(\max_i d_i/\min_i d_i\to\infty\), even though exact cone membership is preserved.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Diagonal congruence preserves the PSD cone, but the condition number of the change of variables is the square of the diagonal scaling condition number and can become arbitrarily large.
knowledge_statements.title: Scaling Pathologies

children.title: Conditioning of Optimality Systems
children.top_down_role: Sensitivity characteristics of linearized optimality systems.

assumptions_latex: The KKT residual map \(F\) is continuously differentiable near a solution \(z_*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Locally, solution error is bounded by a constant approaching \(\|J_*^{-1}\|\) times the KKT residual.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local normwise conditioning of a smooth, nonsingular primal-dual optimality system.

source_refs.locator: 3.3.1 Facial structure, nondegeneracy and strict complementarity p. 37

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb R^N\to\mathbb R^N\) encode a fixed smooth formulation of the SDP KKT equations, and suppose \(F(z_*)=0\). If \(F\) is continuously differentiable near \(z_*\) and \(J_*=F'(z_*)\) is nonsingular, then for every \(\eta>0\) there exists a neighborhood \(U\) of \(z_*\) such that every \(z\in U\) satisfies \(\|z-z_*\|\le (\|J_*^{-1}\|+\eta)\|F(z)\|\). Thus \(\|J_*^{-1}\|\) is the first-order absolute condition measure of this optimality system; a relative condition measure additionally depends on the selected scaling of variables, equations, and data.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonsingular KKT Jacobian yields a local residual-to-solution error bound. Its inverse norm measures first-order absolute sensitivity, while relative conditioning depends on scaling.
knowledge_statements.title: Conditioning of Optimality Systems

source_witnesses.locator: 3.3.1 Facial structure, nondegeneracy and strict complementarity p. 37

children.title: Degenerate Optimality Systems
children.top_down_role: Optimality systems affected by local rank deficiency or degeneracy.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The represented optimality system is first-order degenerate at \(z_*\) exactly when \(F'(z_*)\) has a nontrivial null direction.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order degeneracy for a fixed smooth representation of the SDP KKT equations.

source_refs.locator: 3.3.1 Facial structure, nondegeneracy and strict complementarity p. 37

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a differentiable square KKT residual map \(F:\mathbb R^N\to\mathbb R^N\) and a solution \(z_*\) satisfying \(F(z_*)=0\), call the represented optimality system first-order degenerate at \(z_*\) when \(F'(z_*)\) is singular. Equivalently, there exists \(h\in\mathbb R^N\setminus\{0\}\) such that \(F'(z_*)h=0\). For each such direction, \(F(z_*+th)=o(|t|)\) as \(t\to0\). An inverse-Jacobian residual bound is therefore unavailable for this representation at \(z_*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed smooth KKT formulation is first-order degenerate when its Jacobian has a nonzero null direction; residual growth along that direction is smaller than linear displacement.
knowledge_statements.title: Degenerate Optimality Systems

source_witnesses.locator: 3.3.1 Facial structure, nondegeneracy and strict complementarity p. 37

children.title: Scaling–Degeneracy Interactions
children.top_down_role: Combined effects of data scaling and structural degeneracy.

assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb R^N\to\mathbb R^N\) is differentiable at a solution \(z_*\), with \(N\ge2\).
\(R,S\in\mathbb R^{N\times N}\) are nonsingular equation and variable scalings.
Condition numbers use a fixed subordinate matrix norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Nonsingular scaling preserves Jacobian rank and exact degeneracy but can make the condition number of a nonsingular Jacobian arbitrarily large.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates rank-invariant degeneracy from scaling-dependent numerical conditioning for square KKT systems of dimension at least two.

source_refs.locator: 3.3.1 Facial structure, nondegeneracy and strict complementarity p. 37

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(J=F'(z_*)\) be the Jacobian of a square KKT system on \(\mathbb R^N\), where \(N\ge2\). Under \(z=S\widetilde z\) and \(\widetilde F(\widetilde z)=RF(S\widetilde z)\), the scaled Jacobian is \(\widetilde J=RJS\). For nonsingular \(R\) and \(S\), \(\operatorname{rank}(\widetilde J)=\operatorname{rank}(J)\), so exact Jacobian degeneracy is invariant under this scaling. If \(J\) is nonsingular, then \(\kappa(\widetilde J)\le\kappa(R)\kappa(J)\kappa(S)\) for the selected subordinate norm, and admissible choices of \(R\) and \(S\) can make \(\kappa(\widetilde J)\) arbitrarily large. Thus normwise conditioning is scaling-dependent although exact singularity is not.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Invertible equation and variable scalings preserve KKT Jacobian rank and therefore cannot remove exact degeneracy, but they can make the measured condition number arbitrarily large.
knowledge_statements.title: Scaling–Degeneracy Interactions

children.title: Weak-Infeasibility Status Boundary
children.top_down_role: Residual patterns that do not distinguish near feasibility from weak infeasibility.

children.title: Weak-Infeasibility Signatures
children.top_down_role: Residual and geometric patterns associated with weak infeasibility.

assumptions_latex: \(L=\{X\in\mathbb S^n:\mathcal A(X)=b\}\) is a nonempty closed affine space.
Distances use a fixed norm on \(\mathbb S^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Weak infeasibility is characterized by disjointness at zero distance, necessarily unbounded near-feasible sequences, and absence of positive-margin separation.

notation.meaning: distance between the affine set and cone

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional geometric signatures of weakly infeasible SDP feasibility systems.

source_refs.locator: 3.4 Infeasibility Certificates p. 106

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The feasibility system \(L\cap\mathbb S_+^n\ne\varnothing\) is weakly infeasible precisely when \(L\cap\mathbb S_+^n=\varnothing\) and \(\delta=\operatorname{dist}(L,\mathbb S_+^n)=0\). Equivalently, there exist \(X_k\in L\) and \(Y_k\in\mathbb S_+^n\) such that \(\|X_k-Y_k\|\to0\). Every such approximating pair of sequences satisfies \(\max\{\|X_k\|,\|Y_k\|\}\to\infty\). No affine functional separates \(L\) and \(\mathbb S_+^n\) with a strictly positive margin.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weak infeasibility means that the affine set misses the PSD cone at zero distance. Every near-feasible approximating sequence escapes to infinity, and no positive-margin affine separator exists.
knowledge_statements.title: Weak-Infeasibility Signatures

children.title: Near-Feasibility Ambiguity
children.top_down_role: Numerical regimes where near feasibility is difficult to classify.

assumptions_latex: The SDP feasibility system is weakly infeasible.
The numerical decision uses a positive residual tolerance \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every positive tolerance admits infeasible points that satisfy the approximate feasibility test.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tolerance-induced ambiguity at the weak-infeasibility boundary.

source_refs.locator: 3.4 Infeasibility Certificates p. 106

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(L\cap\mathbb S_+^n=\varnothing\) but \(\operatorname{dist}(L,\mathbb S_+^n)=0\). For every tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\), there exist \(X_\varepsilon\in L\) and \(Y_\varepsilon\succeq0\) such that \(\|X_\varepsilon-Y_\varepsilon\|<\varepsilon\). Hence a test that accepts feasibility whenever the affine residual is zero and the cone distance is at most \(\varepsilon\) accepts \(X_\varepsilon\), even though exact feasibility is false. No fixed positive absolute tolerance can distinguish feasible systems from all weakly infeasible systems solely through these residuals; additional structural information or a certified exact-status procedure is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At weak infeasibility, every positive tolerance admits an apparently feasible point. Residual thresholds alone therefore cannot distinguish exact feasibility from weak infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.title: Near-Feasibility Ambiguity

children.title: Status-Classification Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Threshold-sensitive boundaries between competing status interpretations.

assumptions_latex: \(L\) is a nonempty closed affine subset of \(\mathbb S^n\).
Distance is measured in any fixed norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact feasibility, strong infeasibility, and weak infeasibility are separated by intersection and the sign of \(\delta\).

notation.meaning: distance between the constraint set and cone

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric status partition for finite-dimensional SDP feasibility.

source_refs.locator: 3.4 Infeasibility Certificates p. 106

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\mathbb S_+^n\) and \(\delta=\inf\{\|X-Y\|:X\in L,\ Y\in K\}\). The SDP feasibility system is feasible when \(L\cap K\ne\varnothing\). It is strongly infeasible when \(L\cap K=\varnothing\) and \(\delta>0\), equivalently when the two convex sets admit strict separation with positive margin. It is weakly infeasible when \(L\cap K=\varnothing\) and \(\delta=0\). These cases are mutually exclusive and exhaustive. Thus \(\delta=0\) alone does not certify feasibility: it is the common boundary occupied by both feasible and weakly infeasible systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An SDP is feasible if the affine set meets the PSD cone, strongly infeasible if their distance is positive, and weakly infeasible if disjoint at zero distance.
knowledge_statements.title: Status-Classification Boundaries

children.title: Approximate PSD Decisions
children.top_down_role: Threshold-sensitive classification near the PSD cone boundary.

assumptions_latex: \(X\in\mathbb S^n\) is represented exactly for the stated spectral test.
\(\tau\ge0\) is a fixed absolute eigenvalue tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Approximate PSD acceptance is equivalent to \(\lambda_{\min}(X)\ge-\tau\), with an ambiguity band of width \(2\tau\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Absolute spectral-threshold convention for numerical PSD classification.

source_refs.locator: 2.1 From Linear to Semidefinite Optimization p. 3
source_refs.source_title: Semidefinite Optimization and Convex Algebraic Geometry

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(X\in\mathbb S^n\) and \(\tau\ge0\), declare \(X\) approximately positive semidefinite at absolute tolerance \(\tau\) exactly when \(\lambda_{\min}(X)\ge-\tau\), equivalently when \(X+\tau I\succeq0\). A three-way decision declares certified PSD when \(\lambda_{\min}(X)\ge\tau\), certified non-PSD when \(\lambda_{\min}(X)<-\tau\), and threshold-ambiguous when \(-\tau\le\lambda_{\min}(X)<\tau\). For a scale-relative rule, \(\tau\) must be replaced explicitly by a quantity such as \(\tau_{\mathrm{abs}}+\tau_{\mathrm{rel}}\|X\|_2\); otherwise the classification is not invariant under scalar rescaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximate PSD means the smallest eigenvalue is at least minus a stated tolerance. Eigenvalues near zero form an explicit ambiguity band, and scaling requires a relative term.
knowledge_statements.title: Approximate PSD Decisions

source_witnesses.locator: 2.1 From Linear to Semidefinite Optimization p. 3

children.title: Numerical-Rank Decisions
children.top_down_role: Threshold-sensitive classification of effective matrix rank.

assumptions_latex: \(X\in\mathbb S^n\) has eigenvalues ordered by decreasing absolute value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The numerical rank is the count of eigenvalues whose magnitudes exceed \(\tau\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Thresholded rank for real symmetric matrices, including PSD SDP iterates.

source_refs.locator: 2.1 From Linear to Semidefinite Optimization p. 3
source_refs.source_title: Semidefinite Optimization and Convex Algebraic Geometry

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\in\mathbb S^n\) have eigenvalues satisfying \(|\lambda_1(X)|\ge\cdots\ge|\lambda_n(X)|\). For an absolute threshold \(\tau\ge0\), define the numerical rank by \(r_\tau(X)=\#\{i:|\lambda_i(X)|>\tau\}\). Equivalently, because a symmetric matrix has singular values \(|\lambda_i(X)|\), this is its singular-value threshold rank. A scale-aware convention uses \(\tau=\tau_{\mathrm{abs}}+\tau_{\mathrm{rel}}\|X\|_2\). The strict inequality fixes boundary behavior: an eigenvalue with magnitude exactly \(\tau\) is counted as numerically zero. Numerical rank is therefore a property of the pair \((X,\tau)\), not of \(X\) alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Numerical rank counts eigenvalues whose magnitudes exceed a declared threshold. It depends on both the matrix and the absolute or scale-aware tolerance convention.
knowledge_statements.title: Numerical-Rank Decisions

source_witnesses.locator: 2.1 From Linear to Semidefinite Optimization p. 3
source_witnesses.source_title: Semidefinite Optimization and Convex Algebraic Geometry

children.title: Approximate Complementarity Decisions
children.top_down_role: Threshold-sensitive assessment of primal–dual complementarity.

assumptions_latex: \(X,S\in\mathbb S^n\) are primal and dual slack candidates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Approximate complementarity requires separate cone tests and a normalized trace-product test.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tolerance-based complementarity decision for symmetric primal-dual SDP slacks.

source_refs.locator: 1.1 Semidefinite programming p. 1

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Declare \((X,S)\) approximately complementary at tolerances \((\tau_p,\tau_d,\tau_c)\) when \(\lambda_{\min}(X)\ge-\tau_p\), \(\lambda_{\min}(S)\ge-\tau_d\), and \(|\langle X,S\rangle|\le\tau_c\sigma\), where \(\langle X,S\rangle=\operatorname{tr}(XS)\) and \(\sigma=\max\{1,\|X\|_F\|S\|_F\}\). If \(X\succeq0\) and \(S\succeq0\) exactly, then \(\langle X,S\rangle=0\) is equivalent to \(XS=0\); with approximate PSD matrices, a small trace product is only a tolerance-dependent numerical decision. Cone violations and complementarity must therefore be tested separately rather than inferred from the trace product alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximate complementarity combines separate approximate-PSD checks for both slacks with a normalized small trace product; the trace test alone does not control cone violations.
knowledge_statements.title: Approximate Complementarity Decisions

children.title: Singular-Threshold Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Classification instability near singular spectral regimes.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any threshold decision involving an eigenvalue within \(\varepsilon\) of its boundary can change under an admissible perturbation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Perturbation boundary for eigenvalue-threshold PSD and rank decisions.

source_refs.locator: 2.1 From Linear to Semidefinite Optimization p. 3
source_refs.source_title: Semidefinite Optimization and Convex Algebraic Geometry

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every ordered eigenvalue, Weyl's bound gives \(|\lambda_i(X+E)-\lambda_i(X)|\le\|E\|_2\le\varepsilon\). Consequently, the sign of \(\lambda_i(X)\) is certified against all admissible perturbations only when \(|\lambda_i(X)|>\varepsilon\). More generally, a threshold comparison \(|\lambda_i(X)|>\tau\) is stable only when the eigenvalue magnitude lies outside the boundary band \([\tau-\varepsilon,\tau+\varepsilon]\). Thus PSD, nullity, and numerical-rank decisions are intrinsically ambiguous when relevant eigenvalues lie within the perturbation radius of zero or of the selected threshold; reporting a hard classification there suppresses information required for reliability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eigenvalues move by at most the spectral perturbation norm. PSD and rank classifications are unstable whenever a relevant eigenvalue lies within that radius of a decision threshold.
knowledge_statements.title: Singular-Threshold Boundaries

source_witnesses.locator: 2.1 From Linear to Semidefinite Optimization p. 3

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Failure boundary is the appropriate role, but the formula is not reliable as written. Weyl's indexed bound requires algebraically ordered eigenvalues, whereas rank-threshold stability is more naturally stated for ordered singular values. The claim that sign is certified only for strict distance greater than the perturbation radius also depends on whether zero belongs to the accepted class; equality can be robust for a nonnegative PSD decision. The cited introductory PSD section does not specifically support Weyl perturbation bounds or these boundary conventions. A source on eigenvalue and singular-value perturbation is required before selecting the exact corrected statement.

children.title: Certificate Postprocessing
children.top_down_role: Transformation of numerical output into independently checkable evidence.

knowledge_statements.title: Certificate Postprocessing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sound postprocessing of approximate SDP certificates into exactly checkable candidates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given floating-point candidates \(\widehat X,\widehat y,\widehat Z\), exact problem data \((\mathcal A,b,C)\), and a reconstruction tolerance \(\tau>0\), initialize \((X,y,Z)\) by componentwise rational reconstruction within distance \(\tau\) of the candidates. Enforce symmetry by replacing each matrix with its symmetric part, then solve the exact affine equations \(\mathcal A(X)=b\) and \(C-\mathcal A^*(y)=Z\) while fixing reconstructed entries whenever consistent. Test every resulting equality in exact arithmetic and test \(X\succeq0\) and \(Z\succeq0\) using an exact positive-semidefiniteness criterion. Output the reconstructed certificate only if all required tests pass; otherwise return failure without making a certification claim.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rationally reconstruct an approximate SDP solution, enforce the exact affine equations, and output it only after exact equality and positive-semidefiniteness tests succeed.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal A:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R^m\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(C\in\mathbb S^n\) have exact representable entries.
\(\widehat X,\widehat Z\in\mathbb S^n\), \(\widehat y\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(\tau>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathrm{output}\neq\mathrm{failure}\Longrightarrow \mathcal A(X)=b,\ X\succeq0,\ C-\mathcal A^*(y)=Z,\ Z\succeq0\).

notation.meaning: Adjoint of the SDP constraint map under the trace inner product.

review_flags: No supplied locator supports a canonical rational-reconstruction and affine-correction procedure.
Exact PSD testing and failure behavior are specified for soundness, but completeness depends on the reconstruction method.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits Certificate Postprocessing, and its guarded output is sound in principle. However, no source or locator supports the proposed reconstruction and affine-correction procedure, and “fixing reconstructed entries whenever consistent” does not specify a deterministic exact method or its failure conditions. Source support is required before the mathematical algorithm can be reliably reviewed.

children.title: Exact Feasibility Validation
children.top_down_role: Exact checking interfaces for recovered feasibility evidence.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Feasibility Validation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact primal-feasibility certificate for a rational semidefinite system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the semidefinite feasibility system \(\mathcal A(X)=b\), \(X\succeq0\), an exactly represented matrix \(X\in\mathbb S^n\) is a feasibility certificate when exact arithmetic verifies every component of \(\mathcal A(X)-b\) to be zero and verifies \(X\succeq0\). For rational \(X\), the latter may be checked exactly by confirming that every principal minor of \(X\) is nonnegative. Passing both checks proves that \(X\) belongs to the spectrahedron \(\{W\in\mathbb S^n:\mathcal A(W)=b,\ W\succeq0\}\); numerical residual bounds alone do not constitute this exact certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact matrix certifies SDP feasibility when it satisfies every affine equation exactly and an exact test proves it positive semidefinite.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal A:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R^m\) and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\) have exact rational data.
\(X\in\mathbb S^n\) is represented exactly over \(\mathbb Q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal A(X)=b\ \land\ X\succeq0\Longrightarrow X\in\{W\in\mathbb S^n:\mathcal A(W)=b,\ W\succeq0\}.\)

children.title: Exact Infeasibility Validation
children.top_down_role: Exact checking interfaces for recovered infeasibility evidence.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Infeasibility Validation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong separating certificate for infeasibility of an SDP equality system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the feasibility system \(\mathcal A(X)=b\), \(X\succeq0\). An exactly represented vector \(y\in\mathbb R^m\) certifies infeasibility if exact arithmetic verifies \(\mathcal A^*(y)\succeq0\) and \(b^{\mathsf T}y<0\). Indeed, any feasible \(X\) would satisfy \(b^{\mathsf T}y=\langle y,\mathcal A(X)\rangle=\langle\mathcal A^*(y),X\rangle\ge0\), contradicting the strict inequality. Thus these finite exact checks are sufficient for infeasibility. Their absence does not establish feasibility: weakly infeasible semidefinite systems need not admit a certificate of this strict form.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A vector exactly certifies infeasibility when its adjoint image is positive semidefinite but its inner product with the right-hand side is negative.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal A:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R^m\) and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\) are exact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal A^*(y)\succeq0\ \land\ b^{\mathsf T}y<0\Longrightarrow \nexists X\in\mathbb S^n:\mathcal A(X)=b,\ X\succeq0.\)

notation.meaning: Trace inner product for matrices or Euclidean inner product for vectors.

children.title: Exact Optimality Validation
children.top_down_role: Exact checking interfaces for recovered optimality evidence.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Optimality Validation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact primal-dual optimality certificate for standard-form semidefinite programming.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the primal SDP \(\inf\{\langle C,X\rangle:\mathcal A(X)=b,\ X\succeq0\}\) and dual SDP \(\sup\{b^{\mathsf T}y:C-\mathcal A^*(y)=Z,\ Z\succeq0\}\), an exactly represented triple \((X,y,Z)\) certifies attained optimality when exact arithmetic verifies primal feasibility, dual feasibility, and \(\langle C,X\rangle=b^{\mathsf T}y\). Equivalently, after verifying \(Z=C-\mathcal A^*(y)\), equality of objectives is \(\langle X,Z\rangle=0\). Weak duality then makes \(X\) primal optimal and \((y,Z)\) dual optimal, with their common exact value equal to both optimal values.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact primal and dual feasibility together with equal objective values certifies optimality of both SDP solutions and their common value.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal A:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R^m\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(C\in\mathbb S^n\) are exact.
\(X,Z\in\mathbb S^n\) and \(y\in\mathbb R^m\) are represented exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal A(X)=b,\ X\succeq0,\ C-\mathcal A^*(y)=Z,\ Z\succeq0,\ \langle C,X\rangle=b^{\mathsf T}y\Longrightarrow X\text{ and }(y,Z)\text{ are optimal}.\)

notation.meaning: Adjoint of the primal equality-constraint map.
Trace inner product of symmetric matrices.
